For when it is said: Abraham believed that Christ was to be born, the sense is, he had faith concerning the nativity of Christ, which was then future; but in the assumption, when it is said, now it is false that Christ is to be born, the sense is: the nativity of Christ is not future: whence 547Bfrom those two premises it in no way follows that Abraham believed something false.

QUESTION XII. But though our outward man. It is asked whether the outward man and the inward man are two men, and whether the outward man and the old man, and the inward man and the new man, are the same. Solution. As the old man and the new man are not two men, but one, although according to one thing he be called old, according to another new, so the outward man and the inward man are not two men, but one and the same, so called according to diverse things. Nor is the old man the same as the outward man; nor is the new man the same as the inward man. For the old man consists in fault and punishment, which two are found not only in the outward man, but also in the inward man. But the new man 547Cis understood according to justice and glory: which two also pertain to the inward man. But the outward man is called whatever we have in common with the beasts; the inward man, what is common to us with the angels.

QUESTION XIII. Who hath given us the pledge of the Spirit, etc. (II Cor. V). It is asked how the Holy Spirit is called a pledge, and of what thing he is the earnest? Solution. The Holy Spirit is love, and from the love which we have toward God, we are certain of his promise; and because we have this certitude from the Holy Spirit, therefore the Holy Spirit is given to us by God as it were an earnest and a pledge. Now a pledge is the certitude of a thing believed, or promised, or to be believed. 547DKnowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we persuade men. Fear is divided into five species, as was already said in the Epistle to the Romans, nor is there need to go back over it.

QUESTION XIV. For whether we be transported in mind, etc. It is asked what are the excesses of mind. Solution. There are two excesses, either dread, or straining toward things above: so that in a certain manner lower things slip from the memory. In this excess of mind were all the saints: to whom the secret things of God, surpassing the world, were revealed.

QUESTION XV. Christ died for all. It is asked how Christ died for all: since his death does not profit all: for it does not profit those to be damned, but only the elect. Solution. 548AAccording to Jerome it is thus understood, for all who are to be saved. For universality is sometimes restricted, and this in many ways. For sometimes the universal sign gathers the individuals of the kinds, sometimes the kinds of the individuals, sometimes neither, but the greater or the more worthy part of the universality itself. Or according to Augustine, Christ died for all, because his death merited this, that through him all should be saved, unless it remained in themselves: for it was sufficient for the salvation of all.

QUESTION XVI. God was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself. It is asked how the Father is said to be in the Son, or the Son in the Father: or how that 548Bis to be understood: He that seeth me, seeth the Father also (Joan. XIV). Solution. The one is said to be or to be seen in the other for this reason, that their substance is naturally one. Which I add, that I may exclude the Sabellian heresy. There is unity where there is no diversity, but in every way indifference, and equality, and identity. Whence Hilary says: The Father is seen in the Son on account of the united likeness of nature: for so do we detest the pest of the Arians, that we no less execrate the madness of the Sabellians; so do we confess God to be three, that he is one, and so one, that he is three. For many in our days are Sabellians as to their understanding, who confess three persons: but when it is said that the three persons are one substance, they understand nothing else than what Sabellius understood: 548Cwhich comes about because they do not attend to the manifold signification of this name, substance. For Hilary says that when it is said: The Father and the Son are one substance, such a manner of speaking has both the conscience of faith, and a fraud ready at hand. Then he opens up both, saying: If you signify the Father and the Son to be a singular God, the understanding is false; but if you say that the Father and the Son are one substance, or one simply, so as to understand one, equal and indifferent, through all things equal, in no part dissimilar, the understanding is true. By which words he most manifestly distinguishes between personal unity and natural unity: for the Father and the Son are one in nature, not in person.

548DQUESTION XVII. Behold, now is the day of salvation, etc. (III Cor. VI). It is asked why the time of grace is called the day of salvation, since also in the time of the natural and written law many were saved? Solution. This time of grace is called the day of salvation for this reason, that in this time the victim was offered, through which alone entrance lies open into the kingdom, through which also those who went before merited salvation. Whence also it is called the time of grace, on account of the greater powers given to us through the manifestation of faith and love: whence also the powers of the devil are diminished, and because now all things are done freely, not for the sake of any earthly advantage, and because those things which in other times were promised are in this time fulfilled.

549AQUESTION XVIII. In charity unfeigned, etc. It is asked what charity is called feigned. Solution. That which does not persevere, or which is not sufficient for salvation, or that which is simulated, namely some sign of love shown outwardly, when within it is not in the heart, and this charity is not charity.

QUESTION XIX. As dying, and behold we live. It is asked, in view of these words, how the yoke of the Lord is sweet, and the burden light, since the saints suffer so many and so great hard and difficult things, and how those laboring and burdened, coming to him, find rest, since they seem to pass not from labor to rest, but rather from rest to labor. Solution. To the saints sustaining grievous and harsh things there is present the Holy Spirit, who in the corruption of the outward man renews the inward man, 549Bfrom day to day, and, spiritual rest being tasted, by the hope of future beatitude relieves all harsh things, and thus in so many hard things the burden of Christ is lighter. For the love of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ makes all savage and monstrous things easy and well-nigh nothing.

QUESTION XX. That there may be an equality, as it is written: He that had much had nothing over, etc. (II Cor. VIII.) It is asked whether the lesser, who (as it were provincials) minister stipends to the soldiers of Christ, are equal to them in merits: which the Apostle seems to mean, saying, that there may be an equality. Solution. That equality is not of piety, but because both sustain, and are sustained by, one another. For the lesser sustain the greater in carnal things, and are sustained in spiritual things. And the greater sustain the lesser, that is, the spiritual the carnal, in 549Cspiritual things, and are sustained in carnal things by the same.

QUESTION XXI. For we provide good things not only before God, etc. It is asked how the Apostle divides, namely before God, and before men, since it cannot be done before God, unless it be also done before men? Yet the outward work is not always required, namely when the faculty is lacking. But it is always required that the conscience be clean. Solution. That the Apostle may show that the conscience cannot be clean, unless good things also be provided before men, therefore he distinguishes between these two.

QUESTION XXII. It is asked: What is it to provide good things before God? Solution. So to dispose the mind, that 549Dnothing be done against God, which cannot be done, unless the scandal of the brethren be avoided outwardly; or therefore he divides between the aforesaid, that he may show that there are certain things which, as far as pertains to God, are lawful to be done, because in themselves they are good, although it seem otherwise to men, and therefore they can be passed over. What therefore is expedient and fitting, let that be done which is expedient for us unto merit, which is fitting for an example to the rest. Therefore for the sake of conscience we ought to provide good things before God. For the sake of reputation we provide good things also before men: for he who, trusting in his conscience, neglects his reputation, is cruel, which he does who cares not whether what he does please or displease, and for the scandal of the brethren omits nothing.

QUESTION XXIII. He who soweth sparingly, shall also reap sparingly. 550A(II Cor. IX.) It is asked concerning the poor, who sow sparingly, or nothing, whether they too shall therefore reap sparingly. Solution. He does not sow sparingly who bestows little, if the mind be ready to give, if he had more. He therefore is to be said to sow sparingly who has little love, whether he give more or less: and this man shall reap sparingly, that is, he shall receive a small retribution unto life eternal.

QUESTION XXIV. For we dare not insert ourselves, etc. (II Cor. II.) That is, we do not usurp to ourselves power, but we use the power given to us by God. It is asked therefore what it is to usurp power. Solution. He usurps to himself power who, not elected, or not called, takes to himself honor, who thrusts himself in, and, power not being received, wishes to domineer.

550BQUESTION XXV. But we will not glory beyond measure. It is asked: What is it to glory beyond measure? Solution. To glory more than one ought, and in that in which one ought not, which he does who extends himself into that to which he has no right. But to abuse power is to flatter, and to caress the vices of sinners. To use power is to reprove sinners, and to do the other things which pertain to edification.

QUESTION XXVI. He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord. It is asked what it is to glory in the Lord, since elsewhere he says: God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ (Galat. VI). And that: Not only do we glory in the hope of the sons of God, but also in our tribulations (Rom. V). Is it the same to glory in the Lord, and in the cross of the Lord, and in tribulations? 550CWhat is it to glory? Solution. To glory is to rejoice in praise, and to judge oneself worthy of glory. To glory in the Lord is to attribute all confidence not to oneself, but to the Lord as author, and to exult in Christ with spiritual joy. To glory in the cross of the Lord can be understood in two ways. For he is rightly said to glory in the cross of the Lord who with joy, and with hope of the future life, imitates the passion of the Lord, and this is to glory in tribulations. Someone also is said to glory in the cross of the Lord who does not judge himself worthy of salvation, except through the merit of the Lord's passion, saying with the apostle Peter: Because there is no other name under heaven whereby we must be saved (Act. IV): these things I say without prejudice to a better opinion.

550DQUESTION XXVII. For I am jealous of you with the jealousy of God, etc. (II Cor. XI.) It is asked: What is jealousy? Solution. Jealousy is a motion of the mind toward good or toward evil on account of another's state. When it is toward good, then it is of love; when it is toward evil, then it is of envy.

QUESTION XXVIII. It is asked likewise: What is it to be jealous with the jealousy of God? Solution. To love unto the honor of God, or with that jealousy which God inspires.

QUESTION XXIX. For I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you a chaste virgin to Christ. It is asked concerning this espousal of the Apostle, since not all who are in the Church are virgins, as the married, how then can he present those who are not virgins as a virgin, as it were one, and moreover chaste? Solution. Virginity is twofold: 551Aof body and of mind: the virginity of the flesh is the body untouched; the virginity of the mind is the incorrupt integrity of the inward man. But this is required of every believer, without which that which is of the flesh does not profit. But all are called one virgin on account of the unity of entire faith, of solid hope, of sincere love. Chaste, not having the heat of an evil will.

QUESTION XXX. Satan transformeth himself into an angel of light, etc. It is asked whether it is perilous to believe Satan to be an angel of light, when he says or does those things which befit the good. Solution. If, at the time when he says or does those things which are fitting, there is no error, it is not perilous; but when he begins to lead in his deceits, that no one may go after him, there is need of vigilance: which is not done without God.

551BQUESTION XXXI. [ In hunger, and thirst, etc. It is asked where is the promise of God who says: First seek the kingdom of God, and all these things shall be added unto you (Matth. VI). For the promise seems to have wavered, since the Apostle says that he labored in hunger, and thirst, in cold and nakedness. Solution. That physician, to whom we have once committed ourselves wholly, and from whom we have the promise of the present life and of the future, knows when to apply these aids, or to withdraw them, as he judges to be expedient for us.

QUESTION XXXII. Through a window in the gate by the brethren. It is asked whether this deed was praiseworthy, or worthy of reproach: which seems [so] to some, because he was not freed by the help of God. Solution. The help of God is not needed before human aid has failed; nor ought anyone to await 551Cthe help of God, while he has something he can do, lest he seem to tempt God.

QUESTION XXXIII. And thus I escaped his hands. It is asked whether the Apostle acted, in fleeing, as a good shepherd, or as a hireling. Did he not, when the wolf came, desert the sheep, and flee? and thus it seems that he was not a good shepherd, but a hireling. Solution. When any shepherd is specially sought by persecutors, it is permitted him to give way, and to avoid the fury of the persecutors, and by fleeing to preserve himself for the benefit of the whole flock, and meanwhile let the others, who are not so sought after, furnish food to their fellow-servants. But when a common peril presses upon all, let those, who need others, not be deserted by those whom they need.

QUESTION XXXIV. Whether in the body, or out of the body, 551DI know not, God knoweth, etc. (II Cor. XII.) It is asked how the Apostle could have doubted whether he was caught up in the body, or out of the body, since no one existing in this life can see God as he is; whence he says to Moses: Man shall not see me, and live (Exod. XXXIII). Likewise, if he was caught up out of the body, namely so that the soul was separated from the body, was his body meanwhile dead? Likewise, if he saw God with an intellectual vision, then he saw him truly, and had that knowledge in which is the highest beatitude, and thus he was in beatitude; but beatitude once had is never lost; or if God took from him what he had already received, it seems that God acted unjustly. Solution. Either could have happened: either that the soul separated from the body 552Asaw God in itself, or that the soul, free from the senses of the body, contemplated God thus in the body itself; and since either of these could rightly have happened, the Apostle, in doubt, says whether in the body, or out of the body. Whence, whichever of these it was, that authority will be preserved: Man shall not see me, and live, because in either way he could have put off the man. But if he was out of the body, then the body was dead, and separated from the soul, and again quickened when the soul returned. And since he had full knowledge of God, and thus was in beatitude, if again the same glory was withdrawn from him, it is not to be wondered at, nor incredible, because thus God could show beforehand to his most beloved servant the beatitude and joy to come, which he was to receive, 552Bthat he might endure more firmly in his love and service, and desire more vehemently the very time of receiving it: just as, transfigured on the mountain, he showed the glory of his humanity to his three disciples.

QUESTION XXXV. But by the third heaven, and paradise, into which he was caught up, he understands the same thing, namely the full understanding, or knowledge, of the divinity. Note the fourfold opinion concerning the three heavens. According to the first opinion, the first heaven is the airy, whence [are] the birds of heaven. The second is the firmament, whence also he called the firmament heaven. The third is the empyrean, which as soon as it was made was filled with angels, where the angels, and the holy souls, enjoy the contemplation of God. According to the second opinion, the first heaven is corporeal vision, by which 552Cheaven, and earth, and all things visible to the eyes are discerned. By the same vision certain things are sometimes seen by the gift of God, as Elisha [saw] the fiery chariots (IV Reg. II), and Balthasar the hand writing on the wall, mane, thecel, phares (Dan. V). The second heaven is imaginary, or spiritual, vision, by which are seen not bodies, but the images of them: as is wont [to happen] in dreams, or in ecstasy, as Pharaoh [saw] the ears of grain (Gen. XLI), and Peter the vessel (Act. X). The third is intellectual vision, by which neither bodies, nor images of bodies are seen, but incorporeal and immaterial things are beheld by the instinct of the mind, as substance, the Godhead, and every affection of the soul. The third opinion calls the three heavens the threefold hierarchy of angels according to Dionysius. The first, in the ascent, is that which contains the angels, and archangels, 552Dand virtues. The second, powers, principalities, and dominions; the third, thrones, and cherubim, and seraphim. This third hierarchy, therefore, in the ascent, and the first in the descent, the Apostle calls the third heaven, or paradise: to which, when he says he was caught up, he shows that he saw God immediately, face to face. The fourth opinion is, that the first heaven is called the knowledge of heavenly bodies, the second [the knowledge] of heavenly spirits, the third the knowledge of the Godhead.

QUESTION XXXVI. I know such a man, etc. It is asked how he says a man was caught up whether in the body, or out of it, since man subsists in body and soul, how then does he say that a man can be caught up out of the body. Solution. The truth of man consists there, where is 553Athe image, and likeness of God. Whence [comes] that saying: The mind of each is the man himself. By the name of man, therefore, he calls the inner man.

QUESTION XXXVII. There was given to me a thorn of my flesh, an angel, etc. It is asked by whom this thorn was given to him, whether by God, or by the devil. If by God, how is it called an angel of Satan, as though sent by him? Likewise, if sent by the devil, how is that true which follows: Lest the greatness of the revelations exalt [me], etc. Did Satan then buffet the Apostle through an angel sent by himself, lest he be exalted into pride? Solution. Both by God, and by the devil, was he sent who vexed the Apostle, but for one purpose by God, and for another by the devil. By God he was sent for this, lest the greatness of the revelations exalt him. By the devil, for this, that he might drag him to 553Bfailing. By God also he was sent for this, that virtue might be perfected in weakness.

QUESTION XXXVIII. For which thing I besought the Lord thrice, etc. The devil sought to tempt Job, and was heard (Job I). The Apostle asked that the angel of Satan might depart from him, and was not heard. Where then is divine justice? Was it just that the devil be heard, and not the Apostle? Solution. Those whom God has purposed to heal, he does not always hear according to their will, but according to their health. But some, in wrath, he sometimes hears according to their will, as the devil.

QUESTION XXXIX. Likewise, since the Apostle knew that this infirmity was given him for his profit, and for the preservation of humility, it is asked whether he reasonably prayed 553Cthat such a temptation might depart from him. Solution. Although he knew this, yet as a man he feared a fall from the affliction, 554Aand so from fear he was humbled; but humility drove out the disease of proud elation, and by this dispensation of divine providence, that thorn was given him.

QUESTION XL. And they did not do penance, etc. It is asked whether penance is necessary for one amending his morals for the better; and in what ways penance is performed. Solution. It does not suffice to change one's morals for the better, and to withdraw from evils, unless by the sorrow of penance, and the groaning of humility, and the sacrifice of a contrite heart, satisfaction be made for the fault. Likewise it is to be noted that penance is performed in three ways: before baptism, and after baptism, for the graver [sins], and daily for the lighter and more frequent, according to that saying: You have avoided great things, see that you be not crushed by the sand.

QUESTION XLI. We pray God, that you do no evil 554B(II Cor. XIII). Here the Apostle intimates that only by the grace of God is one turned aside from evil, saying: We pray, etc. For outward planting and watering avail nothing without the inward increase: which God gives by grace alone. It is asked, then, why in the sacred Scriptures we are often commanded both to turn aside from evil, and to do good: since free will is sufficient for neither of these, since it is the work of grace alone, proper to it, both this and that. Solution. The will does something, but does not do it alone. Therefore when it is commanded that this or that be done, we ought to recognize free will; but when prayer is made, the benefit of grace is sought. Concerning grace and free will it has already been said in what is above, and likewise what grace works of itself without the will, 554Cand what it does not work without it; nor is there need that the same things be repeated again.

IV. IN EPISTOLAM AD GALATAS.

  • 553

553C(Galat. I.) Paulus apostolus, etc. Hanc Epistolam Apostolus mittit Galatis: qui de Gallia venientes, in quamdam Graeciae provinciam Graecis se miscuerunt. Unde provincia illa prius Gallograecia dicta est, deinde Galatia. Unde cum Graeci acuti ingenii sint, hi stulti, et ad intelligendum tardiores, ut indociles Galli habentur. Hi prius ab Apostolo in fide, 553Det in doctrina evangelica sunt instructi, postea a pseudoapostolis multis modis sunt subversi, ut crederent gratiam Christi sine lege Moysi non sufficere ad salutem. Unde patet quae sit materia specialis, scilicet status Galatarum in quo tunc erant; generalis autem materia, communis status Ecclesiae. Intentio vero Apostoli in hac Epistola est Galatas versutiis pseudocircumventos ad veritatem fidei catholicae et doctrinae evangelicae revocare. Modus talis: salutem praemittit, ubi contra detractores, et de operibus legis gloriantes, de sua dignitate, et Christi gratia breviter tangit: commendans personam suam, quando pseudo deprimebant. Post salutationem de levitate eos redarguit: post personam suam latius commendat. Deinde legem Moysi improbat: 554Cdocens eam non esse tenendam post Christum, quia non solum non proficit ad salutem et justitiam, sed etiam officit. Post commendat Evangelium et fidem Christi, quae sufficit ad salutem.

QUAESTIO I. Qui dedit semetipsum pro peccatis nostris, ut eriperet nos de praesenti saeculo, etc. Cum mundus sive saeculum sit opus Dei qui bonorum 554Dtantum auctor est, quaeritur hic quomodo totus in maligno positus sit mundus, vel quomodo saeculum dicatur nequam. Solutio. Non solum loca, sed etiam tempora et instrumenta malorum trahunt infamiam eorum, quae in eis fiunt: unde dies pessimi, et tempora periculosa dicuntur. Saltus quoque pleni latronibus, mali dicuntur; et gladius, quo sanguis effunditur, et calix, quo venenum propinatur; et sic mundus, vel saeculum malitiae nomen sortitur propter ea quae in eo fiunt.

QUAESTIO II. Sed licet nos, vel angelus evangelizet vobis praeter id, etc. Nonne multa erant, quae nondum eis Evangelizavit quae sunt credenda et tenenda parvulis, qui lacte simplicis doctrinae sunt nutriendi? Solutio. Non ait plusquam accepistis, sed praeter 555Aid, inquit, per quod intelligit contrarium. Unde promittebat se venire ad quosdam, ut impleret ea quae eis deerant.

QUAESTIO III. Si adhuc hominibus placerem, etc. Quaestio, quae solet hic fieri, in prima Epistola ad Corinthios soluta est. Sed dicet aliquis: Quidquid alibi dictum sit, vellem audire, quomodo utrumque verum sit, si adhuc hominibus placerem, Christi servus non essem; et illud: Placete omnibus per omnia (I Cor. X). Ipse non vult placere hominibus, ut sit servus Christi. Nobis autem praecipit ut omnibus hominibus placeamus. Nunquid non vult nos non esse servos Christi, cum utrumque non possimus, et illis placere, et Christi servi esse? Unde scriptum est: Dissipavit ossa eorum, qui hominibus placent 555B(Psal. XXV). Eadem quaestio nascitur ex verbis Domini diversis. Alibi enim dicit: Luceat lux vestra coram hominibus (Matth. V); et alibi: Nolite justitiam vestram coram hominibus facere (Matth. VI). Solutio. Nihil aliud monemur, sive ex verbis Domini, sive ex verbis Apostoli, nisi ne finem bonorum operum in laude hominum ponamus, et ne eamdem quasi pro mercede bonorum operum optemus.

QUAESTIO IV. Persequebar Ecclesiam Dei, etc. Quaeritur an Apostolus persequendo Ecclesiam Dei peccaverit, cum zelum legis habuit, idque faciendo crederet propter Deum esse faciendum. Nam quisque tenetur, ut illud faciat, quod conscientia dictat 555Cesse faciendum propter Deum, et ita si non faceret, videtur Deum offendere per contemptum. Item, Ecclesiam persequi, malum esse quis dubitet? Solutio. Dicunt quidam, sive hoc sive illud faceret, peccaret. Alii vero dicunt quod zelus ille, quem habuit Apostolus, erat bonus, sed opus illud malum fuit, et erroris, scilicet persecutio Ecclesiae.

QUAESTIO V. Neminem autem aliorum apostolorum vidi, nisi Jacobum fratrem Domini. Quare Jacobus minor filius Alphaei frater Domini dicatur solet quaeri. Solutio. Dicunt nonnulli quod ideo frater Domini dictus est, quia fuit filius Joseph de alia uxore, qui pater Domini putabatur: sed hoc non est ratum, cum Joseph virgo esse credebatur; alia ergo quaerenda 555Dest solutio. Sciendum itaque quod Maria mater Domini, Joachim et Annae filia fuit, quae nupsit Joseph, et ita fuit Joseph putativus pater Domini. Mortuo autem Joachim, Cleophas frater Joseph eamdem Annam accepit uxorem, et genuit ex ea filiam quam vocavit Mariam, quae nupsit Alphaeo, qui genuit filios, scilicet Jacobum, Joseph, Simonem et Judam. Mortuo autem Cleopha, quidam Salomas eamdem Annam duxit, et ex ea filiam genuit nomine Mariam, quae nupsit Zebedaeo: et habuit ex eo filios Jacobum, qui dictus est Major, et Joannem evangelistam. Tres igitur viros Anna habuit, et tres filias. Nunc videndum est quare Jacobus Alphaei et minor dictus est frater Domini. Minor dictus est ad comparationem alterius, qui prius adhaesit Domino, 556Aet ideo major vocatus est, non secundum tempus nativitatis, sed conversionis. Frater autem Domini dictus est secundum quosdam, quia filius materterae ejus erat, vel propter similitudinem sanctitatis ejus, vel potius quia nepos fuit patrui Christi, id est Cleophae. Hebraei enim germana consanguinitate ex parte patrum conjunctos fratres vocant. Notandum quod quatuor modis in Scripturis fratres dicuntur. Natura, ut Esau et Jacob; gente, ut omnes Judaei fratres inter se dicuntur; cognatione, ut omnes illi qui sunt de eadem familia; cum ex una radice turba diffunditat, ut Abraham, et Loth, et Jacob, et Laban Scriptura vocat fratres. Affectu fratres omnes Christiani, ejusdem gratiae participes, eumdem Patrem coelestem habentes.

556BQUAESTIO VI. Cogis gentes judaizare (Galat. II), etc. De hac reprehensione quaeri solet an fuerit vera, an dispensatoria, et an peccaverit Petrus, et vere reprehensibilis fuerit? Solutio. In responsione hujus quaestionis illa duo praeclara lumina Hieronymus et Augustinus videntur dissentire. Hieronymus dicit quod reprehensio illa dispensatoria, et non vera fuit, et quod Petrus non peccavit, nec reprehensibilis fuit. Augustinus vero asserit quod vera fuit reprehensio, nec simulatoria, et quod Petrus vere reprehensibilis fuit; nec secundum veritatem Evangelii ambulavit; non in hoc, quod infirmus factus est infirmis, sed quia suo exemplo cogebat gentes judaizare: alioqui consequens erit falsum scripsisse Paulum, quod nullatenus credendum est. 556CItem de abolitione legalium post Christum, nihilominus idem magistri duo non idem sentiunt. Hieronymus enim dicit quod post Christum mortiferae sunt illae legales observantiae. Augustinus dicit quod licuit Judaeis tunc in primitiva Ecclesia eas observare, tantum non ponerent spem in eis. Ante enim Christi adventum videntur fuisse necessariae; in ipso confinio legis et gratiae indifferentes, si in eis non poneretur spes; nunc autem sunt mortiferae. Nota quod dispensatio est inferioris status concessio causa vitandi scandali, in qua minus fit malum, ut majus vitetur. Salva reverentia secretorum, B. Augustini sententiam praeferimus sententiae B. Hieronymi super praedicta reprehensione et legis abolitione. 556DUnde objectionibus B. Hieronymi sic respondemus. Prima est: Christus est finis legis, id est consummatio et plenitudo legem implens, et consummans in se, et in suis. Non tamen ita quod lex post Christi adventum per nullum temporis curriculum licite a quoquam fieret. Item, lex et prophetae usque ad Joannem. Venerande senex Hieronyme, responde mihi sensu puro, qualiter est hoc intelligendum, lex et prophetae usque ad Joannem? Nunquid sic, quod post Joannem non licuit legem servare? Quod videtur secundum tuam disputationem. Sed nonne Christus etiam post Joannem legem servavit, vetus pascha celebrando? Nunquid Christus fecit quod non decuit? Est itaque intelligendum sic: lex et prophetae usque ad Joannem, id est a Joanne gratia Novi Testamenti 557Aincoepit et praedicari et exhiberi: etex tunc Vetus Testamentum coepit cessare. Item tunc temporis non erat haeresis legales observare caeremonias, licet modo esset, maxime si quis crederet gratiam non sufficere ad salutem sine lege. Item si sunt observandae, salutem afferunt. Nonne quaedam observamus, quae salutem non conferunt, sed pro nostro arbitrio eis possumus uti, et non uti?

QUAESTIO VII. Ex operibus legis non justificabitur homo, nisi per fidem Christi. Quaeritur quomodo fides justificet et non opera, cum Deus reddat unicuique secundum opera sua. Nonne ex quo habet esse meritum et praemium, corona et justitia? Si ergo corona est ex operibus, videtur quod justitia sit ex eisdem. Solutio. In Epistola ad Romanos disputatum 557Best pro modulo nostro de hac quaestione: hic modo sufficiat dicere: fides ideo dicitur justificare, quia ex certitudine invisibilium aeterna bona diliguntur; dilectio autem justificat. Ex fide ergo dicit nos justificari, quia ipsa prima est, ex qua impetrantur caetera. Nec cum dicit nos ex fide justificari, opera bona frustrantur, sed ideo hoc dicit, quia ipsa opera sunt ex gratia fidei.

QUAESTIO VIII. Si ea, quae destruxi, iterum reaedifico, praevaricatorem me constituo. Sed dicet aliquis: Nonne fidem quam impugnabat destruxit, et iterum eam reaedificat praedicando, et sic videtur esse praevaricator? Solutio. Qui rem falsam, quae destrui potest, destruit, si eam iterum reaedificat, praevaricator est. Fides autem non potest destrui, licet 557Cpossit impugnari. Licet itaque Paulus prius conaretur nostram fidem destruere, et iterum reaedificare, non tamen praevaricator fuit.

QUAESTIO. IX. Item opponitur de eodem sic: Si ea, quae destruxi, iterum reaedifico. Ecce manifeste dicit se destruxisse legalia; alibi vero dicit: Legem ergo destruimus? Absit! sed legem statuimus (Rom. III). Quomodo ergo verum est utrumque? Solutio. Duobus modis dicitur quis legem destruere. Ille legem destruit, qui eam in statu suo ante Verbi incarnationem dicit inutilem, nec a Deo datam asserit, et hoc modo legem Paulus non destruebat. Ille etiam dicitur legem destruere, qui eam ostendit post Christi adventum secundum carnalia non esse tenendam, 557Det hoc modo Paulus legem destruebat dicens: Si circumcidamini, Christus nihil vobis proderit.

QUAESTIO X. Nunquid Christus peccati minister, cum lex bona sit, et mandatum bonum, justum, et sanctum? quomodo Christus si legem ministrat, et peccatum? Nunquid Deus, quando legem dedit, peccatum ministravit? Solutio. Lex quidem bona, tamen occasio peccati: juxta quam rationem minister legis dicitur minister peccati.

QUAESTIO XI. Per legem enim legi mortuus sum, etc., id est per auctoritatem legis eam dimisi: sed per quam auctoritatem, quaeritur. Solutio. Moyses dicit: Suscitabo vobis prophetam de fratribus vestris, quem sicut me audietis (Deut. XVIII). Et Hieremias: Consummabo testamentum novum domui Israel. Et David: 558AEt holocaustum pro peccato non postulasti: tunc dixi: Ecce venio (Psal. XXXIX). Ex hoc etiam quod in lege scriptum est: Odio habebis inimicum tuum (Matth. V), cum nullus cum odio inimici possit salvari, constat quod lex neminem justificat. Ideoque ab ea ad gratiam quae justificat fugiendum est. Et quia lex tantum manum, et non animum cohibebat de exterioribus agendo, et omnes cultores suos sub maledictione constituebat, liquet quod per ipsam ipsi moriendum est, ut in Deo vivatur.

QUAESTIO XII. Qui dilexit me, et tradidit seipsum pro me, etc. Revoca quaestionem illam ad memoriam, quomodo Pater, Filius, et Judas conveniant in traditione Filii, super Epistolam ad Romanos secundum posse nostrum pertractatam. Si enim per 558Blegem justitia, ergo Christus gratis mortuus est: sed Christus non est gratis, id est sine causa, sive utilitate, mortuus: ergo ex lege non est justitia. Lector, auctoritatem revoca ad memoriam quoties opus fuerit tibi probare quod ex lege non est justitia: hoc dico, quia sunt auctoritates quibus videtur quod possit ostendi quod ex lege sit justitia: sicut in superioribus ostensum est.

QUAESTIO XIII. Quis vos fascinavit non credere veritati, etc. Quaeritur quid sit fascinatio. Solutio. Magica ludificatio, qua oculis hominum ostenduntur aliter quaedam quam sint: fascinus, vel fascinatio vocatur: vel vulgo fascinatio, quod nocet infantibus. Oculi enim quorumdam dicuntur visu urere, et hic actus fascinatio existimatur. Sic invidia non solum 558Cinvido nocet aliena felicitate tabescenti, sed iis etiam in quibus aliqua bona incipiunt esse. Unde scriptum est: Fascinatio nugacitatis obscurat bona (Sap. IV).

QUAESTIO XIV. Qui ex fide sunt, benedicentur: qui ex operibus legis sunt, sub maledicto sunt. Quaeritur quid sit esse ex fide, quid sit esse ex operibus legis. Solutio. Illi sunt ex fide quorum esse pendet ex fide, id est qui per fidem tendunt ad verum esse, et qui per fidei gratiam quaerunt justificari. Et soli a Deo aeternae vitae benedictionem consequentur. Ex operibus autem legis esse dicuntur, qui ex eis quaerunt justificari; ideoque sub maledicto sunt, tanquam legis transgressores.

QUAESTIO XV. Maledictus omnis qui non permanserit 558Din omnibus quae scripta sunt in libro legis, ut faciat ea. Quaeritur an Deus in lege praecepit aliquid quod non possit adimpleri? Si dicatur nihil, quomodo omnes, qui sunt ex operibus legis, sub maledicto sunt? Item, si Deus praecepit aliquid homini quod ipse non vellet facere, videtur Deus injustus et crudelis. Solutio. Dicunt quidam quod nihil praeceptum est in lege quod homo non possit adimplere. Contra quos dicit expositor, quod multa praecepit Deus, quae omnia nullus potuit adimplere. Unde apostolus Petrus: Cur tentatis Deum, nobis imponere jugum, quod neque nos, neque patres nostri portare potuimus (Act. XV).

QUAESTIO XVI. Maledictus omnis qui pendet in ligno. Quaeritur an Christus sit sub hac universitate maledictionis 559Acontentus? Sed ille est qui super omnia est Deus benedictus in saecula; per quem tollitur omnis maledictio, et qui benedixit nos omni benedictione in coelestibus. Ipse enim semen Abrahae promissum, in quo fit omnium gentium benedictio. Quomodo ergo iste potest esse maledictus? Solutio. Alia est maledictio culpae, quae longe est a Christo: alia est poenae, quam Christus voluntarie suscepit, factus pro nobis maledictum, sive peccatum, id est hostia pro peccato: ut omnium maledictionem tam culpae quam poenae de medio tolleret. Potest etiam dici quod maledictus fuit Christus maledictione culpae, non vere, sed secundum opinionem hominum: unde tanquam peccator cum iniquis reputatus est.

559BQUAESTIO XVII. Si enim ex lege haereditas, non ex promissione. De hac consequentia quaeritur an vera sit. Ad sui veritatem requirit ut sint opposita haereditatem esse ex lege, et ex promissione: alioquin non sequeretur, si ex lege, non ex promissione. Quid est ergo, haereditatem esse ex lege: quid est esse ex promissione? quid etiam vocat haereditatem? Solutio. Haereditatem, vocat aeternam vitam: esse ex lege, est esse ex operibus legis, ad quorum impletionem homo videtur sibi sufficere, nec gratia Dei indigere, quod est ex meritis esse haereditatem. Ex promissione vero esse haereditatem, hoc est, esse ex gratia. Vide ergo, quod esse ex lege, et promissione sunt opposita. Unde alibi dicit Apostolus: Si ex operibus, jam non ex gratia (Rom. XI), id est, si ex debito, 559Cnon ex gratia.

QUAESTIO XVIII. Quid ergo lex? Cum priores sancti, qui ante legem fuerunt, fuerint per gratiam fidei justi, et promissionem sint consecuti, quaeritur quare lex sit data? et quid utilitatis contulerit? Solutionem hujus quaestionis Apostolus ponit dicens: Propter transgressionem lex posita est, quod duobus modis potest intelligi, scilicet propter transgressionem cohibendam, ut saltem timore cessarent homines transgredi, ut quandoque idem facerent voluntarie; vel propter transgressionem lex posita est, id est, ut faceret homines transgredi, et sic humiliarentur, et medicum quaererent, et gratiae auxilium implorarent. Data est ergo ut superbos humiliaret, et infirmitatem proderet, 559Det duris in flagellum et in signum futurorum.

QUAESTIO XIX. Quaeritur cur statim post hominis casum lex non sit data? vel quare ipse Filius illico non venerit? vel quare tot homines perire permiserit? Solutio. Magno consilio hoc factum est, ut post hominis casum non illico lex daretur, vel Filius mitteretur. Nisi enim superbia hominis prius vires experiretur sui arbitrii, libertati sufficientiam arrogaret, et legem superflue datam, et Filium frustra venisse judicaret. Nec omnes, qui tunc fuerunt, perierunt: sicut nec omnes qui modo sunt, fiunt salvi. Itaque hoc factum est, ut homo morbum infirmitatis suae agnosceret, et gratiam sibi necessariam imploraret. In lege enim naturali relictus est sibi, 560Aut sic vires naturae experiretur, et convictus est de ignorantia, et confessus est, quia defecit lumen oculorum suorum: adhuc tamen credebat se habere virtutem, qua possit implere quidquid necessarium ad salutem erat. Unde et dicebat: Non deest qui impleat, sed deest qui jubeat. Quasi diceret: Cognitione, non virtute indigeo. Data est itaque lex, quae ignorantiam illuminaret, sed infirmitatem non adjuvaret: quae peccatum detexit, sed non consumpsit, qua data invaluit morbus, et aucta est concupiscentia, non legis, sed naturae vitio, et instantia diaboli, ut ita cognita utriusque legis insufficientia, et sua infirmitate, clamaret ad medicum, et quaereret gratiae auxilium: et sic multiplicatis infirmitatibus acceleraverunt ad medicum, qui veniens in forma 560Bservi sanavit vulnera languidi. Hic est enim Samaritanus ille qui ad vulneratum, qui incidit in latrones, appropinquavit, et vulnera ejus alligavit: quem sacerdos, et levita, id est lex et sacerdotium, pertransierunt (Luc. X): quia lex ad perfectum neminem perduxit (Hebr. VII). Hic est Elisaeus, qui post missum baculum non effectivum salutis, venit ad suscitandum mortuum filium Sunamitis (IV Reg. IV). Hic est Angelus magni consilii, qui descendit in piscinam, et mota aqua sanabatur unus (Joan. V). Hic est omnipotens sermo, qui a regalibus sedibus venit, dum medium silentium omnia tenerent (Sap. XVIII). Nota tria esse silentia. Primum silentium est ignorantia languoris, quod fuit sub lege naturali. Secundum silentium est desperatio salutis, 560Cquod fuit sub scripta lege, et hoc silentium est medium. Tertium silentium est adeptio sanitatis: quod erit in gloria aeternae beatitudinis. Dum itaque omnia medium silentium tenerent, id est, de salute desperarent: summi Regis Filius de lumine coeli ad tenebras mundi vel inferni descendit. Et veniens locutus est pacem, dedit gratiam, proposuit misericordiam, promisit veniam. Et sic rupto medio silentio coeperunt aegroti pura fide, et vera confessione, quasi magnis clamoribus flagitare remedium, et accelerare ad medicum, per quem aegroti sanarentur, et vulnera curarentur.

QUAESTIO XX. Lex posita est in manu Mediatoris. Quaeritur cur Christus dicatur Mediator? Solutio. 560DQuia mediat nos, id est reconciliat Deo.

QUAESTIO XXI. Sed cum non solum Filius nos sibi reconciliet, sed etiam Deus Pater, sicut dicit Apostolus: Deus erat in Christo, mundum reconcilians sibi (II Cor. V), quaeritur cur solus Filius dicatur Mediator Dei et hominum. Solutio. Tota Trinitas virtutis usu nos sibi reconciliat: sed solus Filius impletione obedientiae, et sacramentorum susceptione nos justificat et reconciliat. Unde non immerito solus Mediator dicitur.

QUAESTIO XXII. Cum Christus Deus, et homo, Dei et hominum mediator sit, quaeritur secundum quam naturam, an secundum divinam, an secundum humanam, an secundum utramque sit Mediator. Solutio. Auctores dicunt quod non est mediator secundum 561Aquod est Deus, sed tantum secundum quod homo, per mortalitatem nobis appropinquans, Deo per justitiam.

QUAESTIO XXIII. Sed conclusit scriptura omnia sub peccato. Quaeritur quid vocet scripturam. Solutio. Legem, quam alibi vocat litteram, hic appellat Apostolus scripturam: quia tantum jubet, non adjuvat: aegrotum, qui sibi sanus videbatur, de morbo convincit, et sic ostendendo peccata, et non auferendo concludit omnia sub peccato. Data est ergo lex, ut gratia quaereretur: et gratia collata est, ut per eam lex impleretur: huic consonat quod alibi dicit: Conclusit Deus omnia in incredulitate, ut omnium misereretur (Rom. XI).

QUAESTIO XXIV. Quicunque in Christo baptizati 561Bestis, Christum induistis. Quaeritur de illo, qui ficte accedit ad baptismum, an sit in Christo baptizatus, et Christum indutus. Quod si dicatur sic, consequitur quod Christo sit conformis: si autem non est baptizatus, si poenituerit de sua fictione, poterit baptizari, sed hoc ei non conceditur: constat ergo quod si baptizatus. Solutio. In Christo baptizari, et Christum induere duobus modis intelligitur, vel sacramenti perceptione, quod commune est bonis, et malis; vel sanctificatione interiori, et vitae conformitate, quod solis bonis convenit.

QUAESTIO XXV. Quaeritur quomodo Christus sit indumentum sanctorum, et anne sancti sint indumentum Christi? Solutio. Christus dicitur indumentum sanctorum, et sancti etiam indumentum 561CChristi. Sed aliter et aliter. Christus enim dicitur indumentum sanctorum per obumbrationem Spiritus sancti, ab aestu vitiorum eos protegens: sancti vero indumentum Christi, quasi ipsum intra se habentes, et circumdantes. Etiam ipsum sua sancta conversatione honorant: sicut mali male vivendo, blasphemant.

QUAESTIO. XXVI. Si vos Christi, ergo Abrahae, etc. Christus dicitur semen Abrahae, et fideles dicuntur semen Abrahae. Unde quaeritur an secundum eamdem significationem et Christus et fideles dicantur semen Abrahae? Solutio. Christus semen Abrahae est corporaliter, quia de ejus stirpe natus: fideles semen Abrahae spiritualiter sunt, id est justi per 561Dfidem, sicut ille fuit.

QUAESTIO XXVII. Sub elementis mundi eramus servientes (Galat. IV). Si ergo Judaei etiam sub elementis serviebant, in quo a paganis distabant? Solutio. Judaei sub elementis Deo, non ipsis elementis serviebant: pagani vero non Deo, sed ipsis elementis cultum divinum exhibebant.

QUAESTIO XXVIII. Ubi venit plenitudo, etc. Quaeritur cur adventus Salvatoris dicatur plenitudo temporis? Solutio. Ideo quia hoc tempore adimplentur quae praecedentibus temporibus erant praenuntiata, et magis proprie videretur dictum tempus plenitudinis, quam plenitudo temporis, et finis saeculi idem dicitur.

QUAESTIO XXIX. Misit Filium suum, etc. Quaeritur 562Aunde et quo missus est Filius. Audi: A Patre exivi, et veni in mundum (Joan. XVI).

QUAESTIO XXX. Sed dicet aliquis: Nonne in mundo erat, et mundus per eum factus est (Joan. I). Nunquid missus est illuc, ubi prius erat. Solutio. Prius erat in mundo per potentiam, et essentiam, sed coepit aliter esse in mundo visibilis factus per servilis formae susceptionem. Sicut ergo quando a Patre exivit, Patrem non deseruit; sic in mundum venit, in quo prius erat. Quare autem missio Filii, vel Spiritus sancti, cum sit opus Trinitatis, Patri attribuatur, jam in praecedentibus dictum est.

QUAESTIO XXXI. Factum ex muliere. Cum sit natus de virgine Dominus, quaeritur cur Apostolus factum de muliere asserat? Solutio. Usus est Hebraicae 562Blocutionis modo ponentis mulierem pro femina, ut Eva in Genesi nondum passa concubitum mulier vocatur. Nota quod expositor dicit quod Creator, qui semper erat, factus est, ut creatura esset; quia factus est homo, ut fieret quod non erat; non ut periret quod erat; hoc dico propter quosdam, qui negant eum aliquid factum esse.

QUAESTIO XXXII. Factum sub lege, ut eos, qui sub lege erant, redimeret, etc. Nonne per mortem suam redemit tam eos, qui sub lege erant, quam eos, qui sine lege erant? Quomodo ergo dicit Apostolus Christum sub lege factum, ut eos, qui sub lege erant, redimeret, quasi per legis observationem eos redemerit? Solutio. Factus est sub lege, ut eam impleret, et impletam cessare faceret; et sic etiam 562CJudaeos a legis praevaricatione redimeret. Nisi enim legem observaret, in qua facta est promissio, quis crederet quod ipse esset semen Abrahae promissum Abrahae, in quo non solum Judaei, sed etiam omnes gentes benedicerentur?

QUAESTIO XXXIII. Ut adoptionem filiorum reciperemus. Quid vocat adoptionem; an bona gratuita ad praesentem justitiam, an ad futuram gloriam pertinentia, per quae efficimur filii? Solutio. Quidam distinguendum putant inter filios adoptionis et filios gratiae, ego autem arbitror eosdem esse.

QUAESTIO XXXIV. Misit Deus spiritum Filii sui, etc. Nota Trinitatem hic manifeste significari. Sunt quidam, qui dicunt, quod sicut aeterna Verbi generatio 562Da solo Patre est, sic et temporalis ipsius missio; quia secundum hos Patrem Filium mittere, est ipsum a Patre esse, et nobis in carne assumpta apparere. Similiter asserunt de Spiritu sancto, quod sicut aeterna ipsius processio a Patre, et Filio, et non a semetipso est, sic et temporalis: sed Augustinus manifeste dicit quod tam Filii quam Spiritus sancti temporalis missio opus est Trinitatis; unde ipsius Filius dicit se missum a Spiritu sancto.

QUAESTIO XXXV. Clamantem: Abba, Pater. Quaeritur, cur Apostolus duo vocabula idem significantia posuerit; videtur enim alterum superflue poni. Solutio. Ideo hoc facit, ut duos populos una fide conjunctos innueret. Hebraicum enim nomen Judaeos, Graecum vocabulum gentilem populum significat; 563Aeadem utriusque vocabuli significatio unitatem fidei et Spiritus figurat.

QUAESTIO XXXVI. His, qui natura dii non sunt. Hic innuit quod una natura est Patris, et Filii, et Spiritus sancti. Si enim Filius non est natura Deus, ergo nec colendus, nec adorandus. Sed opponitur sic nobis: Nonne humanitas Christi colitur et adoratur? nec tamen natura est Deus. Solutio. Quod est assumptum adoratur non propter se, sed propter assumentem; non ergo solam et nudam, sed Deitati unitam adoramus Salvatoris humanitatem.

QUAESTIO XXXVII. Imo cogniti sitis a Deo. Nonne Deus omnia ab aeterno novit? Quomodo ergo dicitur Deus tunc quasi primum nos cognoscere, quando incipimus in ipsum credere? Solutio. Tropica locutione 563Bquod Deo auctore agimus, ipsi attribuitur; unde dicitur: Postulat pro sanctis, quia facit eos postulare, sic cognoscere nos, quia praestat nobis sui cognitionem et quiescere, quia facit nos in seipso conquiescere.

QUAESTIO XXXVIII. Quomodo convertimini iterum ad infirma, et egena? Galatae prius legem non tenebant, quomodo ergo dicit: iterum convertimini ad egena, etc. Solutio. Ut ostendat legalem observationem post Christi adventum distare parum, vel nihil ab idololatria. Vel ideo hoc dicit, quia non solum legem servare volebant, sed ad pristinos etiam errores convertebantur; sic duplici errore a pseudo circumventi erant.

QUAESTIO XXXIX. Et septimae decadis septimum, 563Cqui jubilaeus dicitur. Quid est hoc quod dicit expositor? nonne quinquagesimus annus jubilaeus dicebatur in lege? quomodo ergo septimae decadis septimus annus jubilaeus dictus est? nam septimus septimae decadis est sexagesimus septimus. Solutio. Filii Israel aliquando captivitate pressi non potuerunt servare annum jubilaeum suo ordine. Sexagesimo sexto autem anno data est licentia redeundi a Cyro, et Dario, et ex parte redierunt, et sexagesimum septimum annum coluerunt pro jubilaeo. Sed dicet aliquis quod antequam septuaginta anni essent impleti, non sunt reversi de captivitate. Solutio. Non quidem generaliter et ex toto sunt reversi ante annum septuagesimum; tamen in anno 563Dsexagesimo sexto, ut praediximus, quibusdam indulta est licentia redeundi, quod significatur per Alleluia, quod canitur in Sabbato post Parasceven, qui sexagesimus sextus dies est septuagesimae. Sed quoniam adhuc quidam detinebantur in captivitate, sequitur tractus, qui est signum laboris, sicut alleluia est signum laetitiae. Sequenti autem Sabbato canitur etiam secundum cum primo Alleluia praefigurans generalem reversionem Judaeorum quae est completis annis septuaginta.

QUAESTIO XL. Si potuisset fieri, eruissetis, etc. Nonne illud fieri potuit quod ait Apostolus? Solutio. Sacra Scriptura illud dicit non posse fieri, quod juste non fit; unde Job ait: Utinam possem me occidere (Job X). Et Dominus ad Loth: Non possum 564Aquidquam facere, donec illo introeas (Gen. XIX). Non posse se dixit, quod sine dubio poterat per potentiam, sed non per justitiam.

QUAESTIO XLI. Abraham habuit duos filios. Nonne de Cetura post mortem Sarae plures filios habuit? Quomodo ergo dicit Apostolus eum duos habuisse quasi non plures quam duos? Solutio. Si plures quam duos, ergo duos; non enim dicit tantum duos, sed tamen potius de his quam de aliis dicit, quia Scriptura de istis singula prosequitur, innuens aliquid egregium praefigurari.

QUAESTIO XLII. Haec autem sunt duo testamenta. De hac et consimilibus locutionibus quaeritur quomodo verae sint. Nonne aliud est figura, aliud veritas; aliud significans, aliud significatum? quomodo 564Bergo nomen veritatis praedicatur de nomine figurae, cum dicitur: Haec sunt duo Testamenta, et petra erat Christus? (I Cor. X.) Solutio. Hoc verbum, esse, in hujusmodi locis, ponitur pro significare.

QUAESTIO XLIII. Item cur sacra Scriptura in tali loco utatur verbo substantivo, potest quaeri. Nonne planius esset, si diceretur: Haec autem significant duo testamenta, et petra figurabat Christum? Solutio. Vocum est significare, rerum est esse proprie. In theologia vero non solum voces habent significationem, sed etiam res in aliarum rerum ponuntur significationem, id est quaedam res aliis rebus significantur. Quoties ergo Scriptura sacra vult ostendere, quae res quam rem habeat significare, non dicit: hoc significat illud; sed hoc est illud, ut petra 564Cerat Christus; si enim diceretur petra significat Christum, videretur quod hujus nominis petra, et non hujus rei petrae demonstraretur significatio.

QUAESTIO XLIV. Nota quod superius dicit, quod Ismael natus est secundum carnem; Isaac non secundum carnem, sed per repromissionem, sed nonne Isaac sicut Ismael natus est commistione utriusque sexus? quomodo ergo non est natus secundum naturam vel secundum carnem? Solutio. Ismael natus est usitata lege naturae, scilicet ex naturalium causarum concursu; generatio vero Isaac non naturae, sed divinae virtutis, et gratiae fuit operatio. Tali enim commistioni, quae in tali aetate esse potuit inter Abraham senem, et Saram vetulam et 564Dsterilem natura non concedit filios; sed quod natura negavit, gratia contulit.

QUAESTIO XLV. Sed quomodo tunc qui secundum carnem natus est, persequebatur eum qui secundum spiritum, vel repromissionem natus est; sic et nunc. Quaeritur: Ubi hoc inveniatur quod Ismael persequeretur Isaac. In Genesi enim legitur, quod major cum minore ludebat (Gen. XXI). Quid ergo mali fecit? quid peccavit? quomodo ludendo tantum eum persequabatur? Solutio. Lusum majoris cum minore intellexit Sara esse delusionem. Unde et indignat ait: Ejice ancillam, et filium ejus. (Ibid.) Et Apostolus talem delusionem vocat persecutionem. Ita et nos magis persequuntur delusores, quam aperti persecutores.

QUAESTIO XLVI. Si circumcidamini, Christus vobis 565Anihil proderit. (Gal. V.) Nonne circumcidit Apostolus Timotheum? Ergo decepit eum, et fecit ut Christus nihil prodesset? Solutio. Hoc dicit de iis qui quaerebant justificari ex circumcisione; et ideo se circumcidebant, et sic a gratia exciderunt, quam credebant insufficientem esse. Illis autem, qui eam ex quadam reverentia susceperunt, non tamen ponentes spem in ea, non erat perniciosa secundum Augustinum, secundum vero Hieronymum omnibus suscepta nocuit, nisi fieret dispensatio. De qua controversia superius plenius dictum est.

QUAESTIO XLVII. Testificor omni circumcidenti se, quoniam debitor est universae legis faciendae. Nunquid si universam legem impleat, etiam sic poterit justitiam consequi? Quod videtur ex his verbis, sed 565Balibi manifeste habetur quod ex lege non est justitia. Item, nonne omnis homo tenetur, ut legem impleat, saltem secundum spiritum? Quid est ergo quod omnis circumcidens se hoc debet, non alius? Item: Nonne omnis tenetur, ut diligat proximum sicut seipsum? sed qui diligit proximum, totam legem adimplet. Nonne ex his videtur, quod omnis tenetur universam legem adimplere? Quid est ergo quod dicit: Testificor omni homini circumcidenti se, etc. Solutio. Qui ex circumcisione vel ex lege quaerit justificari, tenetur ad hoc, ut justitiam habeat, vel dignus sit vita, ut impleat quidquid praecipitur in lege, scilicet ut nihil concupiscat; et Deum ex toto corde diligat, in quibus duobus consistit perfecta justitia; quam, si quis haberet, non indigeret gratia 565Cfidei, sicut nec angeli Dei, quae nulli concessa est in praesenti, nisi soli Mediatori Dei et hominum: unde necesse est, ut si quis vult justificari vel beatificari, ad solam gratiam confugiat; si enim in lege quaerit justificari, hoc exigitur ab eo quod non potest ab homine solvi.

QUAESTIO XLVIII. In Christo Jesu neque valet circumcisio, neque praeputium. Dicit expositor quod iis qui sunt in Christo Jesu sunt vitia fugienda, virtutes appetendae; media vero nec fugienda, nec appetenda, in quibus ponit circumcisionem. Unde videtur quod ipsa non prodest, neque obest; sed superius dictum est quod circumcisio non solum non prodest, sed etiam obest. Et Apostolus dicit: Si circumcidamini, Christus vobis non proderit. Si ergo 565Daufert nobis Christum, multum obest. Solutio. Circumcisio simpliciter suscepta, quod in ea non ponatur causa salutis, videtur esse indifferens, et sic non prodest, nec obstet; si autem hac intentione, et hoc animo, ut ex ea quaeratur salus, obest percepta.

QUAESTIO XLIX. Omnis lex in uno sermone impletur: Diliges proximum tuum sicut teipsum. Cum duo sint praecepta dilectionis, Dei scilicet et proximi, quaeritur quomodo in dilectione proximi omnis lex impleatur? Solutio. In dilectione proximi continetur dilectio Dei; quis enim potest diligere proximum propter Deum, nisi diligat Deum? Item nemo potest diligere proximum sicut seipsum, nisi diligat 566Ase; nullus autem se diligit, nisi Deum diligat: quid est enim se diligere, nisi bonum suum amare? bonum autem verum et summum est Christus. Alioquin qui diligit iniquitatem, odit animam suam.

QUAESTIO L. Quaeritur quis sit proximus? Solutio. Omnis homo. Tenemur ergo ex praecepto omnem hominem diligere et exhibere officia pietatis omni indigenti.

QUAESTIO LI. Sicut temetipsum, etc. Quaeritur an debemus proximum quantum nosmetipsos diligere? Quod videtur, cum dicatur, sicut temetipsum. Solutio. Sicut non est quantitatis, sed qualitatis, hoc quidem tenemur aliis facere, quod volumus secundum rationem ab aliis nobis exhiberi. Nota: Cum utrumque praeceptum de dilectione in utroque 566Bcontineatur, saepe ponitur unum potius quam duo, si enim utrumque simul poneretur, videretur quod alterum sine altero haberetur, vel posset haberi.

QUAESTIO LII. Caro concupiscit adversus spiritum. Quaeritur quomodo dicatur caro concupiscere, cum sola anima concupiscat. Solutio. Quod anima facit ex carne, hoc carni attribuitur, sicut auris dicitur audire, oculus videre, cum anima haec per hujusmodi instrumenta agat.

QUAESTIO LIII. Cum ergo secundum substantiam idem sit anima et spiritus, quo anima concupiscit adversus spiritum; nunquid adversus semetipsam? Solutio. Carnem concupiscentem vocat delectationem carnalem, quam anima habet ex carne. Nomine autem Spiritus significat delectationem spiritualem. 566CEt propter has duas delectationes homo interior divisus est, et diversa sortitur vocabula. Secundum enim inferiorem delectationem, nunc caro, nunc homo, nunc anima vel animalis, vel carnalis dicitur; secundum vero superiorem dicitur spiritus, vel spiritualis, vel novus homo.

QUAESTIO LIV. Si spiritu ducimini, non estis sub lege. Quaeritur quid est esse sub lege? Solutio. Timore poenae, non amore justitiae abstinere ab omni malo opere, hoc est esse sub lege. Ut ille dicitur esse sub lege, qui ex ea quaerit justificari, qui debitor est universae legis implendae.

QUAESTIO LV. Manifesta autem sunt opera carnis, quae sunt fornicatio, etc. Quaeritur quomodo Apostolus 566Dinter opera carnis enumeret quaedam quae non sunt vitia carnis, sed potius animae, ut ira, invidia, etc. Solutio. Nomine carnis totum significat hominem, qui secundum se vivendo in haec cecidit. Credere enim omnia vitia ex carne esse, error est, ne diabolus, qui carnem non habet, ab his videatur immunis.

QUAESTIO LVI. Fructus autem spiritus sunt charitas. Dicit expositor quod Apostolus opera spiritus vocat fructus, quia propter se petenda sunt. Sed Augustinus dicit quod virtutes propter solam beatitudinem petendae sunt, propter se autem nihil amandum, nisi summum bonum, cujus fruitio nos beatos efficit. Quid ergo dicendum? quid tenendum? Solutio. Virtutes petendae sunt propter se, quia possessores 567Asuos sincera delectatione delectant, sed non tantum propter se, sed etiam propter beatitudinem, quae est finis supremus.

QUAESTIO LVII. Si praeoccupatus fuerit homo in aliquo delicto (Gal. VI), etc. Quaeritur quid sit praeoccupari, et quid vocet delictum. Solutio. Praeoccupatur, qui ideo cadit in aliquod delictum, sive peccatum, vel quia ignorat quod agendum sit vel dimittendum, vel cum cognoscit, sed tamen infirmitas ad peccandum impellit. Delictum est boni desertio, sicut peccatum mali perpetratio, vel delictum est quod ignoranter fit; peccatum quod a sciente, indifferenter tamen unum pro altero ponitur.

QUAESTIO LVIII. Unusquisque onus suum portabit, etc. Quaeritur quomodo utrumque sit verum. 567BAlter alterius onera portate, etc., et hoc, quod hic dicit: Unusquisque onus suum portabit? Solutio. Alia sunt onera participandae infirmitatis, de quibus superius egit; alia sunt reddendae Deo rationis de actibus nostris, de quibus hic agit. Verum est itaque quod in praesenti debemus subvenire invicem; et qui fortiores sunt aliorum infirmitates sustinere; et tamen in futuro unusquisque onus suum portabit, id est pro peccato suo et non pro peccato alterius.

QUAESTIO LIX. Operemur bonum ad omnes, etc. Quaeritur an praecepto teneamur officia pietatis impendere etiam inimicis? Quod videtur, cum Apostolus dicat: Operemur bonum ad omnes; et Dominus 568Ain Evangelio: Diligite inimicos vestros; benefacite iis qui oderunt vos (Luc. VI). Sed Augustinus ait: Diligere inimicos non est tantae multitudinis, quantam credo exaudiri in Dominica oratione, ubi dicitur: Dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos dimittimus debitoribus nostris (Matth. VI). Et Gregorius ait: Sufficit non odisse inimicos, id est salutem eorem velle; et si opera misericordiae non eis impendantur. Solutio. Praecepto tenemur omnium salutem velle; sed impendere etiam officia pietatis inimicis quantum ad infirmos, et minus perfectos, consilium est, quantum ad perfectos praeceptum. Diligenter ergo notandum est quid secundum consilium, quid secundum praeceptum dicatur.

QUAESTIO LX. Item quando constat, quod bonum 568Bsit benefacere malis, et peccatoribus, et impiis, quid est quod dicit Scriptura: Da misericordi, et ne suscipias peccatorem, et impiis, et peccatoribus redde vindictam, et benefac humili, et ne dederis impio (Eccles. XII). Solutio. Sensus praedictarum auctoritatum est ut nulli peccatori ideo benefacias, quia peccator est, sed quia homo, id est nullius culpam debemus fovere, sed naturam. In unoquoque diligamus quod Deus diligit, et odiamus quod ipse odit; si autem non possumus omnibus tam bonis quam malis subvenire, famulis Dei bona, quae possumus, debemus impendere; unde Apostolus: Maxime autem ad domesticos fidei.

IV. ON THE EPISTLE TO THE GALATIANS.

  • 553

553C(Galat. I.) Paul the apostle, etc. This Epistle the Apostle sends to the Galatians: who, coming from Gaul, mingled themselves with the Greeks in a certain province of Greece. Whence that province was first called Gallograecia, then Galatia. Whence, since the Greeks are of sharp intellect, these [being] foolish, and slower to understand, are held to be like the unteachable Gauls. These were first instructed by the Apostle in the faith, 553Dand in evangelical doctrine, [and] afterwards were subverted in many ways by false apostles, so that they believed the grace of Christ did not suffice for salvation without the law of Moses. Whence it is plain what the special matter is, namely the state of the Galatians in which they then were; but the general matter [is] the common state of the Church. But the intention of the Apostle in this Epistle is to recall the Galatians, deceived by the tricks of the false [apostles], to the truth of the catholic faith and of evangelical doctrine. The manner [is] such: he prefaces a greeting, where against the detractors, and those glorying in the works of the law, he briefly touches upon his own dignity, and the grace of Christ: commending his own person, when the false [apostles] disparaged [him]. After the salutation he reproves them for their fickleness: afterwards he commends his own person more fully. Then he disproves the law of Moses: 554Cteaching that it is not to be kept after Christ, because not only does it not profit unto salvation and justice, but even hinders. Afterwards he commends the Gospel and the faith of Christ, which suffices for salvation.

QUESTION I. Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from the present world, etc. Since the world or age is the work of God, who is the author of good things 554Donly, it is asked here how the whole world is set in evil, or how the age is called wicked. Solution. Not only places, but also times and instruments of evils contract the infamy of those [evils] which are done in them: whence [there are] evil days, and perilous times [so] called. Woodland passes too, full of robbers, are called evil; and the sword, by which blood is shed, and the cup, by which poison is administered; and thus the world, or age, obtains the name of wickedness on account of the things which are done in it.

QUESTION II. But although we, or an angel, preach to you beside that, etc. Were there not many things which he had not yet preached to them, which are to be believed and held by little ones, who are to be nourished with the milk of simple doctrine? Solution. He does not say more than you have received, but beside 555Athat, he says, by which he understands the contrary. Whence he promised he would come to some, that he might fulfill the things that were lacking to them.

QUESTION III. If I yet pleased men, etc. The question, which is wont to be raised here, has been resolved in the first Epistle to the Corinthians. But someone will say: Whatever has been said elsewhere, I would like to hear how both are true, if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ; and that: Please all men in all things (I Cor. X). He himself does not wish to please men, that he may be the servant of Christ. But to us he commands that we please all men. Does he not wish us not to be servants of Christ, since we cannot [do] both, both please them, and be servants of Christ? Whence it is written: He hath scattered the bones of them that please men 555B(Psal. XXV). The same question arises from the diverse words of the Lord. For in one place he says: Let your light shine before men (Matth. V); and in another: Do not your justice before men (Matth. VI). Solution. We are admonished nothing else, whether by the words of the Lord, or by the words of the Apostle, save that we place not the end of good works in the praise of men, and that we not desire the same as it were for the reward of good works.

QUESTION IV. I persecuted the Church of God, etc. It is asked whether the Apostle sinned by persecuting the Church of God, since he had zeal for the law, and in doing this believed it ought to be done for God's sake. For everyone is bound to do that which conscience dictates 555Cought to be done for God's sake, and so if he did not do it, he seems to offend God by contempt. Likewise, who would doubt that to persecute the Church is evil? Solution. Some say that, whether he did this or that, he would sin. But others say that the zeal, which the Apostle had, was good, but that work was evil, and of error, namely the persecution of the Church.

QUESTION V. But I saw none other of the apostles, save James the brother of the Lord. Why James the less, son of Alphaeus, is called the brother of the Lord is wont to be asked. Solution. Some say that he was called the brother of the Lord because he was the son of Joseph by another wife, who was thought to be the father of the Lord: but this is not established, since Joseph was believed to be a virgin; another solution therefore is to be sought. 555DIt is to be known, then, that Mary the mother of the Lord was the daughter of Joachim and Anna, who married Joseph, and so Joseph was the putative father of the Lord. But when Joachim was dead, Cleophas the brother of Joseph took the same Anna to wife, and begot of her a daughter, whom he called Mary, who married Alphaeus, who begot sons, namely James, Joseph, Simon, and Jude. But when Cleophas was dead, a certain Salomas married the same Anna, and begot of her a daughter by name Mary, who married Zebedee: and had of him sons, James, who was called the Greater, and John the evangelist. Three husbands, therefore, Anna had, and three daughters. Now it is to be seen why James [son] of Alphaeus was also called the less, [and] the brother of the Lord. He was called the less in comparison with the other, who first clung to the Lord, 556Aand therefore was called the greater, not according to the time of birth, but of conversion. But he was called the brother of the Lord, according to some, because he was the son of his maternal aunt, or on account of the likeness of his sanctity, or rather because he was the nephew of the paternal uncle of Christ, that is, of Cleophas. For the Hebrews call those joined by natural consanguinity on the fathers' side brothers. It is to be noted that in the Scriptures men are called brothers in four ways. By nature, as Esau and Jacob; by nation, as all the Jews are called brothers among themselves; by kinship, as all those who are of the same family; when from one root a multitude spreads out, as Scripture calls Abraham, and Lot, and Jacob, and Laban brothers. By affection, all Christians [are brothers], partakers of the same grace, having the same heavenly Father.

556BQUESTION VI. Thou compellest the Gentiles to judaize (Galat. II), etc. Concerning this rebuke it is wont to be asked whether it was true, or dispensatory, and whether Peter sinned, and was truly reprehensible. Solution. In the answering of this question those two illustrious lights, Jerome and Augustine, seem to disagree. Jerome says that that rebuke was dispensatory, and not true, and that Peter did not sin, nor was reprehensible. But Augustine asserts that the rebuke was true, and not feigned, and that Peter was truly reprehensible; nor did he walk according to the truth of the Gospel; not in this, that he became weak to the weak, but because by his example he compelled the Gentiles to judaize: otherwise the consequence will be that Paul wrote what was false, which is by no means to be believed. 556CLikewise concerning the abolition of the legal [observances] after Christ, the same two masters nonetheless do not think the same. For Jerome says that after Christ those legal observances are deadly. Augustine says that it was permitted the Jews then, in the primitive Church, to observe them, only let them not put hope in them. For before the coming of Christ they seem to have been necessary; on the very border of law and grace [they were] indifferent, if hope be not put in them; but now they are deadly. Note that a dispensation is the concession of an inferior state for the sake of avoiding scandal, in which a lesser evil is done, that a greater may be avoided. Saving the reverence of [these] secret [matters], we prefer the opinion of blessed Augustine to the opinion of blessed Jerome upon the aforesaid rebuke and abolition of the law. 556DWhence to the objections of blessed Jerome we answer thus. The first is: Christ is the end of the law, that is, the consummation and fullness fulfilling the law, and consummating [it] in himself, and in his own. Yet not so that through no interval of time could the law, after the coming of Christ, lawfully be kept by anyone. Likewise, the law and the prophets until John. Venerable old man Jerome, answer me with pure understanding, how is this to be understood, the law and the prophets until John? Is it thus, that after John it was not lawful to keep the law? Which seems [to follow] according to your disputation. But did not Christ even after John keep the law, celebrating the old pasch? Did Christ do what was not fitting? It is therefore to be understood thus: the law and the prophets until John, that is, from John the grace of the New Testament 557Abegan both to be preached and to be shown forth: and from then the Old Testament began to cease. Likewise at that time it was not heresy to observe the legal ceremonies, though it would be now, especially if anyone believed that grace did not suffice for salvation without the law. Likewise if they are to be observed, they bring salvation. Do we not observe certain things, which do not confer salvation, but which we can, at our own discretion, use, and not use?

QUESTION VII. Man shall not be justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Christ. It is asked how faith justifies and not works, since God renders to each according to his works. Is there not, from the fact that there is merit and reward, [also] crown and justice? If then the crown is from works, it seems that justice is from the same. Solution. In the Epistle to the Romans it has been disputed 557Baccording to our measure concerning this question: here let it now suffice to say: faith is said to justify for this reason, because from the certitude of things invisible the eternal goods are loved; and love justifies. He says therefore that we are justified from faith, because it is first, from which the rest are obtained. Nor, when he says that we are justified from faith, are good works made void, but he says this for the reason that the works themselves are from the grace of faith.

QUESTION VIII. If I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a prevaricator. But someone will say: Did he not destroy the faith which he assailed, and again build it up by preaching, and thus seem to be a prevaricator? Solution. He who destroys a false thing, which can be destroyed, if he build it again, is a prevaricator. But faith cannot be destroyed, though 557Cit can be assailed. Although, therefore, Paul first tried to destroy our faith, and again to build it up, yet he was not a prevaricator.

QUESTION IX. Likewise it is objected concerning the same thing thus: If I build again the things which I destroyed. Behold he manifestly says that he destroyed the legal [observances]; but elsewhere he says: Do we then destroy the law? God forbid! but we establish the law (Rom. III). How then is each true? Solution. In two ways is anyone said to destroy the law. He destroys the law who says it useless in its state before the incarnation of the Word, and asserts it was not given by God, and in this way Paul did not destroy the law. He also is said to destroy the law, who shows that after the coming of Christ it is not to be kept according to the carnal [sense], 557Dand in this way Paul did destroy the law, saying: If you be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.

QUESTION X. Is Christ then the minister of sin, since the law is good, and the commandment good, just, and holy? how [is] Christ [the minister of sin], if he administers the law, and [that] sin? Did God, when he gave the law, administer sin? Solution. The law indeed [is] good, yet the occasion of sin: according to which reasoning the minister of the law is called the minister of sin.

QUESTION XI. For through the law I am dead to the law, etc., that is, through the authority of the law I have dismissed it: but by what authority, it is asked. Solution. Moses says: I will raise up for you a prophet from your brethren, whom you shall hear as me (Deut. XVIII). And Jeremiah: I will complete a new testament with the house of Israel. And David: 558AAnd holocaust for sin thou didst not require: then said I: Behold I come (Psal. XXXIX). From this too, that it is written in the law: Thou shalt hate thine enemy (Matth. V), since no one can be saved with hatred of an enemy, it is established that the law justifies no one. And therefore from it one must flee to the grace which justifies. And because the law restrained only the hand, and not the mind, in the doing of outward things, and set all its worshippers under a curse, it is clear that through it one must die to it, that one may live in God.

QUESTION XII. Who loved me, and delivered himself for me, etc. Recall to memory that question, how the Father, the Son, and Judas concur in the delivering up of the Son, treated upon the Epistle to the Romans according to our ability. For if 558Bjustice [is] through the law, then Christ died in vain: but Christ did not die in vain, that is, without cause, or benefit: therefore justice is not from the law. Reader, recall the authority to memory as often as it is needful for you to prove that justice is not from the law: this I say, because there are authorities by which it seems it could be shown that justice is from the law: as was shown above.

QUESTION XIII. Who hath bewitched you that you should not believe the truth, etc. It is asked what bewitching is. Solution. Magical mockery, by which things are shown to the eyes of men otherwise than they are: [this] is called a bewitching, or bewitchment: or commonly [it is called] fascination, which harms infants. For the eyes of certain [persons] are said to burn by their gaze, and this act is reckoned a bewitching. Thus envy harms not only 558Cthe envious man, pining away at another's happiness, but also those in whom some good things begin to be. Whence it is written: The bewitching of trifling obscureth good things (Sap. IV).

QUESTION XIV. They who are of faith shall be blessed: they who are of the works of the law are under a curse. It is asked what it is to be of faith, [and] what it is to be of the works of the law. Solution. They are of faith whose being depends on faith, that is, who through faith tend to true being, and who through the grace of faith seek to be justified. And these alone shall obtain from God the blessing of eternal life. But they are said to be of the works of the law, who seek to be justified from them; and therefore they are under a curse, as transgressors of the law.

QUESTION XV. Cursed is everyone who abideth not 558Din all things which are written in the book of the law, to do them. It is asked whether God commanded anything in the law which cannot be fulfilled? If it be said nothing, how are all, who are of the works of the law, under a curse? Likewise, if God commanded man something which he himself would not [be willing to] do, God seems unjust and cruel. Solution. Some say that nothing was commanded in the law which man cannot fulfill. Against whom the expositor says, that God commanded many things, all of which no one could fulfill. Whence the apostle Peter: Why tempt you God, to put upon us a yoke, which neither we, nor our fathers were able to bear (Act. XV).

QUESTION XVI. Cursed is everyone that hangeth on a tree. It is asked whether Christ is contained under this universality of the curse 559A? But he is the one who is over all things God blessed forever; through whom every curse is taken away, and who blessed us with every blessing in the heavenly [places]. For he himself [is] the promised seed of Abraham, in whom is [made] the blessing of all nations. How then can he be cursed? Solution. There is one curse of fault, which is far from Christ: there is another of punishment, which Christ voluntarily took upon himself, made for us a curse, or sin, that is, a victim for sin: that he might take away from the midst the curse both of fault and of punishment. It can also be said that Christ was cursed with the curse of fault, not truly, but according to the opinion of men: whence he was reputed as a sinner with the wicked.

559BQUESTION XVII. For if the inheritance [be] from the law, [it is] not from the promise. Concerning this consequence it is asked whether it is true. For its truth it requires that to be from the law and [to be] from the promise be opposites: otherwise it would not follow, if from the law, [then] not from the promise. What is it, then, [for] the inheritance to be from the law: what is it to be from the promise? what also does he call the inheritance? Solution. By inheritance he calls eternal life: to be from the law, is to be from the works of the law, for the fulfilling of which man seems to himself to suffice, nor to need the grace of God, which is [for] the inheritance to be from merits. But for the inheritance to be from the promise, this is, to be from grace. See then, that to be from the law, and [to be] from the promise are opposites. Whence elsewhere the Apostle says: If from works, [then] now not from grace (Rom. XI), that is, if from debt, 559C[then] not from grace.

QUESTION XVIII. What then [is] the law? Since the former saints, who were before the law, were just through the grace of faith, and obtained the promise, it is asked why the law was given? and what usefulness it conferred?
