Non dico quod Christus, nisi moreretur, immortalis et impassibilis non fieret; sed dico quod tale meritum tali praemio erat dignum.

QUAESTIO VII. Quaeritur quomodo simul in eadem anima potuerit esse summa beatitudo et tristitia: ante enim passionem haec duo fuerunt in Christo. Quod enim ibi fuerit beatitudo secundum mentem 578Bex quo fuit homo, credendum est: alioquin, quomodo esset verus Deus, non video. Item quod ibi fuerit tristitia constat, cum ipse dicat: Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem (Matth. XXVI). Solutio. Sicut in Paulo fuit vis inferior et vis superior, sic in Christo fuit vis inferior, animae scilicet motus, vel affectus quidam, qui mortem horrebat: ratio tamen superior in sua beatitudine libera vigebat. Non enim affectus carnis in ipso, sicut in caeteris, rationem impediebat in aliquo, ut minus divinitate contemplaretur.

QUAESTIO VIII. Item quaeritur quomodo majorem beatudinem non habuit post resurrectionem, quando immortalitatem et impassibilitatem induit? Solutio. Non tunc habuit plus quantum ad mentem, sed quod 578Cprius habuit, tunc quietius possedit, sicut rex quietius et securius regnum suum possidet cessantibus infestare inimicis.

QUAESTIO IX. Propter quod donavit, etc. Nonne prius habuit nomen, quod est super omne nomen? Quomodo ergo dicit, Propter quod donavit? non solum enim secundum quod Deus est, datum est ei hoc nomen ab aeterno secundum naturam, sed etiam secundum quod est homo a sui conceptione datum est illud homini assumpto secundum gratiam. Solutio. Tunc res dicitur fieri, quando innotescit: quod enim prius habuit, tunc primum post resurrectionem hominibus et daemonibus innotuit.

QUAESTIO X. Item quaeritur cui datum sit hoc nomen, 578Dan Deo, an homini? Solutio. Augustinus dicit quod homini et non Deo datum est nomen quod est super omne nomen (Philipp. II), scilicet ut sit Deus et Filius Dei per gratiam non participationis, sed unionis, et totum habeat homo assumptus per gratiam, quod habet Deus genitus per naturam. Per gratiam itaque homo habet, ut sit filius, non filius gratiae, sed filius naturae. Aliter dicit Ambrosius quod Deo non homini datum est nomen, quod est super omne nomen.

QUAESTIO XI. Sed nunquid Augustinus, et Ambrosius, super hoc contraria sentiunt? Solutio. Alia est donatio gratuita, de qua Augustinus; alia naturalis, 579Ade qua loquitur beatus Ambrosius. Datum est homini, ut sit Deus per personalem unionem statim in sui conceptione: quando enim Deus factus est homo per dignationem, et homo factus est Deus per gratiam, non Deus adoptivus, sed Deus naturalis, Deus aeternus, Deus omnipotens. Deo autem genito datum est ab aeterno esse Deum per naturam. Itaque nulla est in intelligentia contrarietas inter doctores veritatis.

QUAESTIO. XII. Qui spiritui servimus Deo, etc. (Philip. III.) Quaeritur qua servitute. Nota quod servitus, quae soli Deo debetur, dicitur latria; unde et idololatra, qui Dei culturam exhibet idolis, et abominatio dicitur idololatria, et domus idolium, et sacrificium idolothytum. Sed servitus, qua per charitatem 579Bjubemur servire invicem, Graece dulia dicitur: utraque vero servitus sermone Latino nuncupatur.

QUAESTIO XIII. Hebraeus ex Hebraeis, secundum legem Pharisaeus. Quaeritur unde dicti sint Hebraei. Solutio. Hebraei dicuntur ab Heber, non ab Abraham, ut visum est beato Augustino aliquando, quod postea retractavit: quod inde patet, quia ipse Abraham est Hebraeus in quodam loco dictus: quod non esset, si hoc nomen ab ipso derivatum esset. Item Abraham interpretatur pater multarum gentium; Hebraei, transeuntes. Constat ergo verum esse quod Hebraei non ab Abraham dicti sunt, sed ab Heber: qui solus in divisione linguarum Hebraicam retinuit 579Clinguam.

QUAESTIO XIV. Secundum justitiam, quae in lege est. Quaeritur quomodo dicat se conversatum secundum justitiam, quae in lege est, sine querela, cum alibi dicat se cum aliis in desideriis carnis, dum esset in lege, ambulasse, unde et filium irae se nominat? Solutio. Utrumque verum est, et quod secundum desideria carnis ambulavit, et tamen secundum justitiam, quae in lege erat, quae timore poenae, non amore servire facit; quae manum, non animum comprimit, conversatus sit sine querela: talis erat justitia in lege.

QUAESTIO XV. Non habens justitiam meam, etc. Nonne Deus legem dedit, et ei obedire praecepit? 579Dquomodo ergo justitiam, quae est ex lege, dicit suam? Solutio hujus quaestionis in superioribus continetur. Dum enim erat in lege quaerens ex operibus legis justificari: in hoc quod credebat propriis viribus posse adimplere ipsam legem, justitiam legis suam faciebat.

QUAESTIO XVI. In fide ad cognoscendum, etc. Hoc de fide non habente tempus operandi intelligitur, sed diligere nonne est opus fidei? Sed fides sine dilectione, postquam aliquis est adultus, nunquam valet. Quomodo ergo dicit expositor quod hoc debet intelligi de fide non habente tempus operandi, quod ipsa valeat ad Deum cognoscendum, et ad alia? Solutio. Hoc ideo dicitur, ne quis putet 580Asufficere hoc ad salutem, scilicet credere, et habere fidem sine operibus, cum habet bene operandi facultatem.

QUAESTIO XVII. Quorum nomina sunt scripta, etc. Quaeritur quid sit liber vitae. Solutio. Liber vitae est praedestinatio Dei, in qua omnes salvandi scripti sunt, vel saltem per solam praedestinationem, vel etiam per justitiam et praedestinationem.

QUAESTIO XVIII. Gaudete in Domino semper (Philipp. IV), etc. Dicit expositor quod gaudium in saeculo, et gaudium in Deo contraria sunt, nec in eodem simul esse possunt. Sed nonne aliquis est qui divisus est, et partim gaudet in saeculo, et partim in Domino, sicut partim diligit mundum, et partim diligit Deum? Solutio. Illo gaudio dicitur 580Bquilibet gaudere, quod in illo cognoscitur praeponderare, et illam partem hominis interioris quam occupat gaudium mundi, non tenet gaudium quod est in Domino, quia non possunt esse in eodem circa idem.

QUAESTIO XIX. Petitiones vestrae innotescant apud Deum, etc. Nonne Deus omnia plene et perfecte novit antequam eveniant? quomodo ergo dicit Apostolus, Ut petitiones innotescant apud Deum? Solutio. Sensus est: Petitiones vestrae adeo sint vehementes et non tepidae, ut dignae sint exaudiri et impleri. Cum enim adimplentur, nobis innotescunt, quod ad Deum perveniunt.

QUAESTIO XX. Dicit expositor quod angeli offerunt 580Corationes nostras Deo: ideo quaeritur qualiter haec oblatio sit intelligenda. Solutio. Salva reverentia secretorum, dicimus quod ab angelis nostras orationes Deo offerri, nihil aliud est quam per eos dignas fieri, ut a Deo exaudiantur. Item angeli medii sunt inter nos et Deum: sicut enim divina secreta nobis annuntiant, sic ea, quae apud nos hic aguntur, Deo nuntiare dicuntur.

QUAESTIO XXI. Sed cum Deo sua perfectio ad omnia cognoscenda sufficiat, quaeritur ad quid angeli ei aliquid nuntiant? Solutio. Non ut eum doceant, sed ut aeternam et incommutabilem veritatem ejus consulant, et ut sciant quid sibi sit faciendum, quid, et quibus et quando sit annuntiandum.

580DQUAESTIO XXII. Non quaero datum, sed fructum, etc. Quaeritur quid distet inter datum et fructum. Solutio. Datum vocat id quod datur, ut cibus, nummus, vestis. Fructus vero intentio datoris: quae ideo dicitur fructus, quia secundum eam opus judicatur utile et fructiferum. Vel fructum vocat mercedem ipsam. Unde opus bonum dicitur flos, ex quo fructus aeternae vitae nascitur. Nota quod per corvum, qui pavit Eliam, intelligitur donum, ubi opus bonum fuit sine intentione bona. Per viduam, quae eumdem prophetam pavit, intelligitur fructus; ubi fuit bonum opus cum intentione bona.

VI. ON THE EPISTLE TO THE PHILIPPIANS.

  • 575

575C(Philip. I.) Paul and Timothy, etc. This epistle the Apostle writes to the Philippians, who are Macedonians. For Philippi is a metropolis city in Macedonia, which is a certain province in Greece, which Philip the father of Alexander built, calling it by his own name. But these, having received the word of preaching from the Apostle, were firm in the faith, and did not receive the false apostles. These therefore he fortifies against a twofold war, namely of tribulations and of false preachers. And so the intention of the Apostle in this epistle is to exhort the Philippians to patience against tribulations, and to constancy against the false apostles. The mode is such: after the customary manner he sends a salutation beforehand. Then he gives thanks for them, imploring for them greater goods, that growing in virtues they may come to perfection. Then 575Dhe admonishes them to the patience of tribulations by his own example and Christ's. Afterward, that they beware of the cunning of the false apostles. At last he interposes an admonition of mortality, and near the end he says that he rejoices concerning the grace which the Romans had sent him through Epaphroditus.

QUESTION I. For what? so that by every means, whether by occasion or by truth, Christ be announced. It is asked how the Apostle permits the wicked to preach the evangelical doctrine, since elsewhere it is written: To the sinner God hath said: Why dost thou declare my justices (Psal. XLIX)? etc. Likewise: Praise is not comely in the mouth of a sinner (Eccli. XV). Likewise: He whose life is despised, it remains that his preaching be neglected. Solution. In such a case the preacher is rebuked on his own account, not on account of others. For what he preaches profits not himself, but others: 576Cwhence the praise of God in the mouth of sinners is not comely. The hirelings therefore are to be tolerated. Whence the Lord: Upon the chair of Moses have sat the Scribes and Pharisees: what they say, do ye (Matth. XXV), etc. And so the preachers who preach for the truth are to be loved; the hirelings, who from occasion and temporal advantage announce the truth, are to be permitted; thieves and robbers, or wolves, are to be guarded against, nay, to be fled from.

QUESTION II. What I shall choose, I know not, etc. It is asked how the Apostle is in doubt which he should choose, whether to remain in the flesh, or to be dissolved and to be with Christ (Philipp. I), since he knows that the stronger the fight, the greater the crown. Did he not know that it is of greater merit to fight than to rest? Solution. Affection drew him to both: therefore he says that he knows not which 576Dhe should choose. The Apostle therefore doubts from affection, not from ignorance. But then it is asked: How does he say that it is much better to be dissolved and to be with Christ. Solution. "Better" is here set down for "sweeter" and "safer."

QUESTION III. To you it is given not only that you believe in him, but also that you suffer for him, etc. It is asked whether to suffer itself is a good, and whether it is a gift of God? for if it is, it is to be desired. Solution. From him who is the faith of believers is the endurance of the suffering. But the punishment itself in itself is not good, nor to be desired for its own sake, nor ought it to be numbered among the gifts of God. Yet to suffer for Christ is good and to be desired; because it has great merit. Nor does the Apostle say simply: To you it is given to suffer; 577Abut thus: To you it is given to suffer for Christ.

QUESTION IV. Who being in the form of God (Philipp. II). It is asked what "form" here denotes. Solution. Form is sometimes set down for representation, sometimes for the truth of the thing, as here: Who being in the form of God, that is, in the truth of the divine essence and in the equality of substance; for as a man begets a man, a dog a dog, so God begot God, equal in all things, not unequal: whence the Son also is said to be this which the Father is; and since this can be understood according to person and nature, Augustine shows the understanding of this saying, saying: The Son is therefore said to be that which the Father is, because as the Father is God, so also the Son, and as the Father is omnipotent, so also the Son, and as the Father is immutable, so also the 577BSon. For therefore the Father and the Son are one, and supremely one, of whom there is no diversity of nature or of will. Scripture therefore says both: that the Son is equal to the Father, and that the Father is greater than the Son, but this according to the form of a servant, and that according to the form of God.

QUESTION V. And in habit found as a man, etc. In how many ways is something had? Solution. In four ways something accedes to another so as to be had: either so as to change and not be changed, as wisdom; or so as to change and be changed, as food; or so as neither to change nor be changed, as a ring; or so as not to change but to be changed, not from its own nature, but from some prior form, as a garment when it is put on; it does not change the man, but is changed; not from its own nature, but it receives an appearance and form which 577Ccast aside it did not have; according to which comparison and likeness the incarnation is understood: for the form of a servant so acceded to the form of God that it did not change or convert it, but the form of a servant itself was changed, not from its own nature, but into a more excellent and worthier state than it had been before. All this therefore which Augustine says of habit he adduces for this reason, to show that when the Word was made flesh it was not changed or converted into man; just as neither is a man changed into a garment when he puts it on. But this, which certain ones add of their own, that as a man when he puts on his garment does not become something, so neither did God, when he took the form of a servant, become something: this, I say, they do not have from the words of Augustine, 577Dnor of any other saint, since it is false: for if they wish to hold the likeness adduced from the garment in all respects, they must concede that, as a man does not become a garment when he puts it on, so neither did God become man when he clothed himself with the form of a servant. For if Christ is nothing but that which he was from eternity, he had no being common with his mother: therefore not consubstantial with his mother; because nothing substantial is said of both. For when it is said: Christ is man, and the Virgin mother of the Lord is man, the same is not signified by this name, man, according to these new heretics. Of these things it has been spoken more fully upon the Epistle to the Romans.

578AQUESTION VI. Who humbled himself, becoming obedient, etc. It is asked whether Christ merited anything. Solution. He merited for us, not for himself. For we by his merit were made worthy of eternal life; but he by his death acquired for himself nothing of which he was not worthy before. Yet it can be said: Truly by the humility of his passion he merited the brightness of the resurrection, namely impassibility and immortality. I do not say that Christ, unless he died, would not become immortal and impassible; but I say that such a merit was worthy of such a reward.

QUESTION VII. It is asked how at the same time in the same soul there could be the highest beatitude and sadness: for before the passion these two were in Christ. For that there was beatitude according to the mind 578Bfrom the time he was man, is to be believed: otherwise, how he would be true God, I do not see. Likewise that there was sadness is established, since he himself says: My soul is sorrowful even unto death (Matth. XXVI). Solution. As in Paul there was a lower power and a higher power, so in Christ there was a lower power, namely a motion of the soul, or a certain affection, which shrank in horror from death: yet the higher reason, free in its beatitude, flourished. For the affection of the flesh in him, as in the rest, did not impede the reason in anything, so as to contemplate the divinity less.

QUESTION VIII. Likewise it is asked how he did not have greater beatudinem after the resurrection, when he put on immortality and impassibility? Solution. He did not then have more as to the mind, but what 578Che had before, he then possessed more tranquilly, just as a king possesses his kingdom more tranquilly and securely when the enemies cease to harass it.

QUESTION IX. For which cause he gave, etc. Did he not have before the name which is above every name? How then does he say, For which cause he gave? for not only according to that he is God was this name given to him from eternity according to nature, but also according to that he is man it was given from his conception to the man assumed according to grace. Solution. A thing is then said to be made, when it becomes known: for what he had before, then first after the resurrection became known to men and demons.

QUESTION X. Likewise it is asked to whom this name was given, 578Dwhether to God, or to man? Solution. Augustine says that to man and not to God was given the name which is above every name (Philipp. II), namely that he be God and the Son of God by the grace not of participation, but of union, and that the man assumed have by grace all that God begotten has by nature. By grace therefore the man has it that he is a son, not a son of grace, but a son of nature. Ambrose says otherwise, that to God and not to man was given the name which is above every name.

QUESTION XI. But do Augustine and Ambrose think contrary things upon this? Solution. One is the gratuitous giving, of which Augustine speaks; another the natural, 579Aof which the blessed Ambrose speaks. It was given to the man that he be God by personal union immediately in his conception: for when God was made man by condescension, the man too was made God by grace, not an adoptive God, but a natural God, an eternal God, an omnipotent God. But to God begotten it was given from eternity to be God by nature. And so there is no contrariety in understanding between the doctors of truth.

QUESTION XII. We who serve God in spirit, etc. (Philip. III.) It is asked with what service. Note that the service which is owed to God alone is called latria; whence also one is called an idolater who exhibits to idols the worship of God, and the abomination is called idolatry, and the house an idol-temple, and the sacrifice an idol-offering. But the service by which through charity 579Bwe are bidden to serve one another is in Greek called dulia: yet both are named by the Latin word "service."

QUESTION XIII. A Hebrew of Hebrews, according to the law a Pharisee. It is asked whence the Hebrews are so called. Solution. The Hebrews are called from Heber, not from Abraham, as it once seemed to the blessed Augustine, which he afterward retracted: which is clear from this, that Abraham himself is in a certain place called a Hebrew: which would not be, if this name were derived from him. Likewise Abraham is interpreted father of many nations; the Hebrews, those passing over. It is established therefore to be true that the Hebrews are called not from Abraham, but from Heber: who alone in the division of tongues retained the Hebrew 579Clanguage.

QUESTION XIV. According to the justice which is in the law. It is asked how he says that he conversed according to the justice which is in the law, without complaint, since elsewhere he says that he walked with others in the desires of the flesh while he was under the law, whence he also names himself a child of wrath? Solution. Both are true, both that he walked according to the desires of the flesh, and yet that he conversed without complaint according to the justice which was in the law — which makes one serve through the fear of punishment, not through love; which restrains the hand, not the mind: such was the justice in the law.

QUESTION XV. Not having my own justice, etc. Did not God give the law, and command obedience to it? 579Dhow then does he call the justice which is from the law his own? The solution of this question is contained in the foregoing. For while he was under the law, seeking to be justified from the works of the law: in this, that he believed he could fulfill the law itself by his own powers, he made the justice of the law his own.

QUESTION XVI. In faith unto knowing, etc. This is understood of the faith which has not the time of working; but is not to love a work of faith? But faith without love, after one is grown, is never of avail. How then does the expositor say that this ought to be understood of the faith which has not the time of working, that it avails for knowing God, and for other things? Solution. This is said for this reason, lest anyone think it 580Asuffices for salvation, namely to believe and to have faith without works, when he has the faculty of working well.

QUESTION XVII. Whose names are written, etc. It is asked what the book of life is. Solution. The book of life is the predestination of God, in which all who are to be saved are written, whether at least through predestination alone, or also through justice and predestination.

QUESTION XVIII. Rejoice in the Lord always (Philipp. IV), etc. The expositor says that joy in the world and joy in God are contrary, and cannot be at the same time in the same person. But is there not someone who is divided, and rejoices partly in the world and partly in the Lord, just as he loves partly the world and partly God? Solution. Anyone is said 580Bto rejoice with that joy which is known to preponderate in him; and that part of the inner man which the joy of the world occupies, the joy which is in the Lord does not hold, because they cannot be in the same person concerning the same thing.

QUESTION XIX. Let your petitions be made known with God, etc. Does not God know all things fully and perfectly before they come to pass? how then does the Apostle say, That the petitions be made known with God? Solution. The sense is: Let your petitions be so vehement and not lukewarm that they be worthy to be heard and fulfilled. For when they are fulfilled, it becomes known to us that they reach to God.

QUESTION XX. The expositor says that the angels offer 580Cour prayers to God: therefore it is asked how this offering is to be understood. Solution. Saving the reverence due to hidden things, we say that for our prayers to be offered to God by the angels is nothing other than for them to be made worthy through them, that they may be heard by God. Likewise the angels are intermediaries between us and God: for as they announce the divine secrets to us, so the things which are done here among us they are said to announce to God.

QUESTION XXI. But since God's own perfection suffices for knowing all things, it is asked to what end the angels announce anything to him? Solution. Not that they may teach him, but that they may consult his eternal and unchangeable truth, and that they may know what is to be done by them, what, and to whom, and when it is to be announced.

580DQUESTION XXII. I seek not the gift, but the fruit, etc. It is asked what difference there is between gift and fruit. Solution. He calls the gift that which is given, as food, coin, garment. But the fruit is the intention of the giver: which is therefore called fruit, because according to it the work is judged useful and fruitful. Or he calls the fruit the reward itself. Whence a good work is called a flower, from which is born the fruit of eternal life. Note that by the raven which fed Elijah is understood the gift, where the good work was without a good intention. By the widow who fed the same prophet is understood the fruit; where there was a good work with a good intention.

VII. IN EPISTOLAM AD COLOSSENSES.

  • 581

581A(Coloss. I) Paulus apostolus, etc. Hanc epistolam scribit Apostolus ad Colossenses, qui sunt Asiani: quibus non ipse Apostolus praedicavit, sed ejus discipuli, scilicet Archippus et Epaphras. Sed Archippus ministerium in eos acceperat; Epaphras vero ex eis oriundus fuit, et ab Apostolo instructus doctrinam Archippi confirmavit. Postea vero pseudoapostolis supervenientibus, et carnales observantias praedicantibus, in dubium illis venerat quibus esset credendum. Unde Apostolus, cujus auctoritas celebris erat, quasi medius judicat, quae pars potius sit tenenda, scribens eis ab Epheso. Intentio itaque Apostoli est in hac epistola confirmare Colossenses in ea fide et doctrina, quam a discipulis ejus acceperunt, et non in aliquo praeter 581BChristum spem ponendam esse docet. Modus tractandi talis est: more solito salutem praemittit; deinde gratias agit de bonis eorum, fidem et dilectionem eorum commendans. Orat ut perficiantur in Christo, cujus beneficia, et secundum utramque naturam primatum commendat, et post ministerii sui dignitatem commemorat, et monet ne per philosophiam, vel legis caeremonias seducti a Christo recedant. Tandem omnes simul, et separatim, scilicet sexus, et aetates, et conditiones moraliter instituit. In fine monet Archippum sollicitum esse ministerii sui.

QUAESTIO I. Gratias agentes, etc. Dicit expositor quod hic incipit Apostolus ostendere quod lex 581Cnon prodest, sed nocet. Nonne lex bona, et a Deo data, et non solum non nocuit, sed profuit in statu suo? quomodo ergo verum est quod non prodest, sed nocet? Solutio. Verum est quod lex ante gratiam profuit; sed post gratiam inutilis fuit. Cui solutioni sic objicitur: Nonne lex modo perhibet testimonium veritati, et per illam illuminamur in cognitione Deitatis? ergo etiam nunc tempore gratiae nobis prodest lex. Quomodo ergo verum est: Lex non prodest, sed nocet? Solutio. Lex lecta, et spiritualiter intellecta prodest, et non nocet: secundum vero litteram observata non prodest, sed nocet.

QUAESTIO II. Qui dignos nos fecit in partem sortis sanctorum. Quaeritur quid vocet sortem, cujus 581Dparticipes facti sumus. Solutio. Futuram haereditatem, quae sorte, id est divina gratia et voluntate, sine meritis datur, hic vocat Apostolus sortem.

QUAESTIO III. Item quaeritur quomodo sine meritis futura haereditas detur sanctis, cum per fidem, et dilectionem, et bona opera eam mereantur. Solutio. 582ASine meritis praecedentibus fidem intelligendum est, non sine subsequentibus: quae sunt ex gratia, et ideo non excluduntur, cum dicitur quod sola gratia datur futura gloria. De his jam diximus superius.

QUAESTIO IV. Transtulit nos in regnum Filii. Quaeritur quid dicat regnum Filii Dei. Solutio. Regnum coelorum, vel Filii, pluribus modis accipitur, scilicet pro futura gloria, ut ibi: Adveniat regnum tuum (Matth. VI); vel pro praesenti Ecclesia, ut ibi: Cum tradet regnum Deo et Patri (I Cor. XV); vel pro fide Christi, ut ibi: Regnum Dei intra vos est (Matth. XII); vel pro sacra Scriptura, ut ibi: Auferetur a vobis regnum coelorum, et dabitur genti facienti fructum (Matth. XXI).

582BQUAESTIO V. Filii dilectionis suae. Nonne Spiritus sanctus est dilectio, qua Pater diligit Filium, et Filius Patrem, et Christus est filius dilectionis? Videtur ergo, quod sit filius Spiritus sancti: quod fides non recipit. Solutio. Dilectio communiter accipitur pro divina natura, sive substantia, sive essentia, cum dilectionis filius esse praedicatur. Est enim Filius naturae, substantiae, et essentiae Patri consubstantialis, et coessentialis. Quid autem dilectio significet, cum dicitur: Spiritus sanctus est dilectio, qua Pater diligit Filium, et e diverso alibi expositum est. De redemptione item, et imagine, et de eo quod Christus dicitur caput Ecclesiae, jam dictum: nec oportet, ut acta agamus.

582CQUAESTIO VI. Quaeritur autem an Christus secundum humanitatem fuerit caput sanctorum incarnationem praecedentium. Videtur quod sic: sed qui nondum secundum humanitatem erat, quomodo potuit esse caput eorum? Vel si, quomodo potuerunt habere, quod nondum caput erat? Solutio. Christus etiam secundum humanitatom potest dici caput eorum qui fuerunt ab Abel, quia per fidem futuri omnes salvati quotquot salvati sunt. Nota quod Christus ejusdem naturae esse cum Patre praedicatur, ubi filius dilectionis esse ostenditur. Ubi vero imago, non solum ejusdem substantiae identitas, sed etiam personalis proprietas insinuatur. Ubi primogenitus omnis creaturae esse dicitur, ibi Patri coaeternus asseritur. Ubi 582Dquod omnia per ipsum condita sunt legitur, omnipotentia ipsius declaratur. Ubi dicitur quod omnia in ipso constant (Coloss. I), immensitas ejus manifestatur, cujus aeternitas in Joanne insinuatur, ubi scriptum est: In principio erat Verbum (Joan. I); et personalis proprietas cum subjungitur: Et Verbum erat apud Deum (ibid.); et substantiae identitas, 583Acum dicitur: Et Deus erat Verbum (Joan. I). Est itaque Filius Patri coaeternus, consubstantialis, coomnipotens; alius in persona, idem cum Patre omnium creaturarum principium.

QUAESTIO VII. Et ipse, Christus scilicet, est caput Ecclesiae. Dicitur quod Ecclesia coepit primo ab Abel, qui primus fuit justus, sed nonne Adam fuit justus? Creditur enim quod post lapsum per poenitentiam, et fidem sit justificatus: quare ergo non dicitur Ecclesia incoepisse ab Adam? Solutio. Ab Adam maculam originalis peccati contraxit Ecclesia, ab Abel nullam, et ideo ab Abel melius incoepisse dicitur quam ab Adam; quia Scriptura de peccato Adam, et non de justitia facit mentionem, et de justitia Abel, et non de peccato. Christus 583Bergo semper caput omnium, qui fuerunt ab initio, sicut eorum, qui secuti sunt eum: per quem solum accessum habemus ad Patrem.

QUAESTIO VIII. Videte, ne quis vos decipiat per philosophiam, et inanem fallaciam (Coloss. II), etc. Nonne cognitio rerum naturalium, quam tradiderunt philosophi, utilis fuit ad Dei invisibilia cognoscenda? Per visibiles enim rerum visibilium formas, quarum doctrina docetur in mathematica, venitur ad invisibiles rerum visibilium causas, quas docet physica: per quas venitur ad cognoscendas invisibiles substantias, et invisibilium substantiarum invisibiles naturas. Quomodo ergo Apostolus talem cognitionem vocat inanem fallaciam? Solutio. Apostolus non reprehendit philosophos de 583Choc, quod naturas rerum inquirebant; sed de hoc, quod potentiam Dei cum sit infinita, sub causis naturalibus coarctare conabantur, dicentes Deum nihil facere contra naturam. Unde Deum creaturam fieri, virginem parere, mortuum revivere, dicebant esse impossibile. Hunc ergo errorem eorum jure reprehendit Apostolus: non veram, quam habebant, de naturis cognitionem.

QUAESTIO IX. In quo habitat omnis plenitudo divinitatis. Cum una et simplex plenitudo divinitatis sit, quomodo dicat omnis plenitudo divinitatis, cum omnis soleat colligere multitudinem? Solutio. Omnis plenitudo divinitatis dicitur, ut I otetur: quod omni modo inhabitandi ibi est, etiam personaliter. Vel aliter: Omnis plenitudo dicitur ut insinuetur 583Dquod in ipso est plenitudo non solum scientiae, sed etiam potentiae et bonitatis. In quo destruitur error eorum qui dicunt quod homo assumptus habet omnem scientiam per gratiam, quam habet Verbum per naturam, sed non omnem potentiam.

QUAESTIO X. Plenitudo divinitatis corporaliter. Cum divinitas sit incorporea, quaeritur quomodo possit habitare corporaliter in Christo. Solutio. Corporaliter dicit, id est, completive, solide et veraciter, respiciens ad legales figuras, quae fuerunt umbra futurorum, quarum corpus, id est, impletio et veritas est Christus. Vel aliter: Corporaliter non significat naturam rei existentis, sed potius 584Amodum existendi. Sicut enim corpus sic habet esse naturaliter in uno loco, quod simul non potest esse in alio: sic plenitudo divinitatis habet esse in homine assumpto: quo modo in nulla alia est creatura. In omni creatura est per essentiam, in justis per gratiam, in solo Christo secundum personalem proprietatem. Hoc est ergo Deitatem habitare in Christo corporaliter, id est personaliter. Sicut corpus est in pluribus locis, simul non corporaliter sed spiritualiter. Hoc dicens non nego veritatem, et essentiam corporis Dominici esse simul in pluribus altaribus, sed per hoc insinuo quod modum illum existendi non habet communem corporibus aliis, vel ex natura corporis, sed potius communem cum spiritu, non creato, sed increato. Utrumque 584Bmirum, et verum; quod spiritus creatus alicubi est corporaliter, et corpus Christi sacramentale in pluribus locis spiritualiter.

QUAESTIO XI. Delens chirographum decreti, quod erat contrarium vobis, etc. Quaeritur quid vocet decretum, quid chirographum. Solutio. Decretum nominat vel ipsam legem Moysi, vel Dei praeceptum, quod primo homini dedit in paradiso, dicens: De ligno scientiae boni et mali ne comedas (Gen. II); chirographum utriusque decreti violati memoriam: omnium autem culparum chirographa deleta sunt fuso sanguine sine culpa.

QUAESTIO XII. Quae sunt umbra futurorum, corpus autem Christi. Quaeritur quomodo distinguatur umbra, corpus, spiritus. Solutio. Aliud est umbra, 584Caliud corpus, aliud spiritus: quae tria aliis nominibus dicuntur figura, res, veritas, ut idem sit umbra et figura; idem corpus et res; idem spiritus et veritas. Legales caeremoniae umbra, et figura futurorum dicebantur. Sacramenta gratiae corpus, sive res illarum umbrarum vel figurarum sunt: spiritus vel veritas dicitur gratia spiritalis scilicet quam conferunt sacramenta Novi Testamenti, et significant: sacramenta vero Veteris Testamenti, tantum gratiam spiritualem significant, et non conferunt: et haec differentia inter haec et illa sacramenta. Item sciendum est quod illa, quae tempore legis fuerunt praecepta, nunc tempore gratiae non sunt praecepta; sed tantum veritatis testimonia, unde tunc peccatum erat non 584Dobservare etiam unum. Nunc autem non est peccatum ea non custodire; imo qui custodit, offendit.

QUAESTIO XIII. Mortificate membra vestra (Coloss. III), etc. Quaeritur quid, vel quae vocet membra, quae sunt mortificanda. Nunquid oculus, manus, pes sunt mortificandi? Solutio. Membra hic vocat Apostolus concupiscentiam membrorum, sicut ipse subjungit, et exponit fornicationem, etc.

QUAESTIO XIV. Avaritiam, quae est idolorum servitus, etc. Nonne aliud est avaritia, aliud idololatria? quomodo ergo avaritiam vocat idolorum servitutem? Solutio. Ideo avaritiam comparat idololatriae, quia non est dispar malitia. Sicut enim idololatra colit truncum, sic avarus nummum. Et sicut idololatra nititur auferre Deo honorem suum, sic avarus res 585Aquas Deus communiter pro omnibus creavit, sibi usurpat soli.

QUAESTIO XV. Exspoliantes veterem hominem, etc. Quaeritur quid hic vocet veterem hominem. Solutio. Dicitur quandoque vetus homo Adam primus homo, qui peccando se, et totam posteritatem suam induit tunica vetustatis. Dicitur quandoque vetus homo, quilibet homo, qui portat imaginem terreni; quandoque vero dicitur vetus homo ipsa vetustas, quae consistit in culpa et in poena; quandoque vetus homo habitus vitiorum nuncupatur, ut hic, secundum expositorem.

QUAESTIO XVI. Et induite novum hominem. Quaeritur similiter quid hic vocet novum hominem? Nam novus homo quandoque dicitur Christus, a quo 585Best omnis novitas; quandoque novus homo dicitur quilibet in Christo renovatus; quandoque etiam habitus virtutum; quandoque specialiter mens rationis. Sed superius, quod homo interior vocatur, mens, dictum est; hic autem dicitur quod mens interior dicitur novus homo: quod videtur esse contrarium, cum aliud sit novus homo, aliud interior, ut jam ostensum est. Solutio. Dicit expositor quod novum hominem vocat rationalem mentem, nec est contrarium ad id quod superius dictum est, quod mens interior homo dicitur: idem enim propter diversas proprietates diversa sortitur vocabula.

QUAESTIO XVII. Qui renovatur in agnitionem Dei secundum imaginem ejus, etc. Item quaeritur quomodo 585Cmens dicatur renovari secundum imaginem Dei, cum ipsa sit imago Dei, nunquid renovari potest secundum seipsam? Solutio. Eadem est imago quae renovatur, et illa secundum quam renovatur, sicut dicimus aliquem mortuum esse secundum corpus, id est corpore non secundum spiritum. Mens itaque secundum semetipsam, id est in semetipsa renovatur. In Epistola tamen ad Ephesios dicitur, quod ipsa renovatio fit secundum Deum: ideo secundum Deum, ne secundum creaturam esse dicatur. Per talem enim renovationem Deo consimilis et conformis efficitur: ideo secundum ipsam esse dicitur. Nota quod haec imago, quae in cognitione Dei renovatur, aeque in viro et in femina invenitur: quae alia 586Aest ab illa, de qua superius dictum est: Vir est imago Dei, et mulier viri.

QUAESTIO XVIII. Donantes vobis metipsis, si quis adversus aliquem habet querelam. Hoc idem praecepit Dominus, dicens: Debitoribus vestris dimittite (Matth. VI), sed quid est quod a nobis dimitti possit? quod est debitum, quod a nobis possit exigi ab illo, qui nobis injuriam intulit? Solutio. Hoc est dimittere injuriam illatam, pro nobis nullo modo satisfactionem propter injuriam postulare: quaedam alia super hoc alibi a nobis dicta sunt.

QUAESTIO XIX. Dicit expositor quod qui ab illicitis abstinet laudem habet; qui vero a licitis temperat, laudem et praemium quasi diceret: Ille vitat poenam, hic etiam meretur coronam. Sed nonne etiam ille, 586Bqui abstinet ab illicitis, non solum laudem, sed etiam mercedem habet? Solutio. Qui abstinet ab illicitis semper vitat poenam, sed non semper meretur coronam, nisi tunc tantum, quando tentatur et impugnatur.

QUAESTIO XX. Omnia in nomine Domini facite. Per omnia, non intelligit nisi bona, quae sunt a nobis facienda. Unde quaeritur an omnia facienda praecipiat propter Deum fieri. Nunquid ex praeceptis constringor dare pallium meum pauperi, quem indigere video, et sciam hoc Deo placere. Nam si dimitto, videor contemnere: quod scio illum velle fieri. Solutio. Sic debet intelligi: Omnia facite in nomine Domini, id est nihil contra Deum faciatis, et in bonis non gloriam vestram, sed Dei quaeratis. Non 586Ctamen in omnibus quae agimus meremur; quia quaedam sunt indifferentia, ut sedere, stare, spiritum ducere, manum claudere, oculos aperire, et hujusmodi. Quaedam vero talia sunt, quae sic habent meritum, si fiant; et non sint peccatum, si non fiant, ut pallium dare pauperi, et omnia vendere, et dare pauperibus: quod perfectorum est, qui nudi Christum sequuntur.

QUAESTIO XXI. Dicite Archippo: Vide ministerium quod accepisti in Domino, ut illud impleas (Coloss. IV). Quaeritur an subditi praelatos monere possint. Solutio. Ecce auctoritas, ut subditi praelatos moneant, ne pigri sint in praevidendis his, quae ad salutem spectant.

VII. ON THE EPISTLE TO THE COLOSSIANS.

  • 581

581A(Coloss. I) Paul an apostle, etc. The Apostle writes this epistle to the Colossians, who are Asians: to whom the Apostle himself did not preach, but his disciples, namely Archippus and Epaphras. But Archippus had received a ministry among them; Epaphras indeed was sprung from them, and, instructed by the Apostle, confirmed the teaching of Archippus. But afterward, when false apostles came in and preached carnal observances, it had come into doubt among them whom they ought to believe. Whence the Apostle, whose authority was renowned, judges as it were a mediator which side ought rather to be held, writing to them from Ephesus. The intention therefore of the Apostle in this epistle is to confirm the Colossians in that faith and doctrine which they received from his disciples, and he teaches that hope is to be placed in nothing besides 581BChrist. The manner of treatment is such: after his wonted fashion he sends greeting beforehand; then he gives thanks for their good things, commending their faith and love. He prays that they may be perfected in Christ, whose benefits, and primacy according to both natures, he commends, and afterward recounts the dignity of his own ministry, and warns them not, seduced by philosophy or by the ceremonies of the law, to depart from Christ. Finally he instructs all together, and separately — namely the sexes, and ages, and conditions — morally. At the end he warns Archippus to be solicitous of his ministry.

QUESTION I. Giving thanks, etc. The expositor says that here the Apostle begins to show that the law 581Cdoes not profit, but harms. Is not the law good, and given by God, and did it not only not harm, but profit in its own state? how then is it true that it does not profit, but harms? Solution. It is true that the law before grace profited; but after grace it was useless. To which solution it is thus objected: Does not the law even now bear witness to the truth, and through it are we not illuminated in the knowledge of the Deity? therefore even now in the time of grace the law profits us. How then is it true: The law does not profit, but harms? Solution. The law read, and spiritually understood, profits, and does not harm: but observed according to the letter it does not profit, but harms.

QUESTION II. Who hath made us worthy to be partakers of the lot of the saints. It is asked what he calls the lot, of which 581Dwe have been made partakers. Solution. The future inheritance, which is given by lot — that is, by divine grace and will — without merits, the Apostle here calls the lot.

QUESTION III. Likewise it is asked how the future inheritance is given to the saints without merits, since through faith, and love, and good works they merit it. Solution. 582AIt is to be understood without merits preceding faith, not without those following: which are of grace, and therefore are not excluded, when it is said that by grace alone future glory is given. Of these we have already spoken above.

QUESTION IV. He hath translated us into the kingdom of the Son. It is asked what he means by the kingdom of the Son of God. Solution. The kingdom of heaven, or of the Son, is taken in several ways, namely for future glory, as there: Thy kingdom come (Matth. VI); or for the present Church, as there: When he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God and the Father (I Cor. XV); or for the faith of Christ, as there: The kingdom of God is within you (Matth. XII); or for Holy Scripture, as there: The kingdom of heaven shall be taken away from you, and shall be given to a nation yielding fruit (Matth. XXI).

582BQUESTION V. Of the Son of his love. Is not the Holy Spirit the love by which the Father loves the Son, and the Son the Father, and is Christ the son of love? It seems therefore that he is the son of the Holy Spirit: which faith does not receive. Solution. Love is commonly taken for the divine nature, or substance, or essence, when he is proclaimed to be the son of love. For the Son is consubstantial and coessential with the Father in nature, substance, and essence. But what love signifies, when it is said: The Holy Spirit is the love by which the Father loves the Son, and conversely, has been expounded elsewhere. Concerning redemption likewise, and the image, and that Christ is called the head of the Church, it has been already said: nor is it needful that we do things already done.

582CQUESTION VI. It is asked, however, whether Christ according to his humanity was the head of the saints who preceded the incarnation. It seems that he was: but he who was not yet [head] according to his humanity, how could he be their head? Or if [he was], how could they have [a head] that was not yet head? Solution. Christ even according to humanitatom can be called the head of those who were from Abel, because through faith all who are to be saved, as many as are saved, [are saved]. Note that Christ is proclaimed to be of the same nature with the Father, where he is shown to be the son of love. But where [he is called] the image, not only the identity of the same substance, but also personal property is intimated. Where he is said to be the firstborn of every creature, there he is asserted to be coeternal with the Father. Where 582Dit is read that all things were founded through him, his omnipotence is declared. Where it is said that all things consist in him (Coloss. I), his immensity is made manifest, whose eternity is intimated in John, where it is written: In the beginning was the Word (Joan. I); and personal property when it is subjoined: And the Word was with God (ibid.); and identity of substance, 583Awhen it is said: And the Word was God (Joan. I). And so the Son is coeternal, consubstantial, and co-omnipotent with the Father; another in person, the same with the Father the beginning of all creatures.

QUESTION VII. And he, namely Christ, is the head of the Church. It is said that the Church began first from Abel, who was the first just man, but was not Adam just? For it is believed that after the fall he was justified through penance and faith: why then is the Church not said to have begun from Adam? Solution. From Adam the Church contracted the stain of original sin, from Abel none, and therefore it is better said to have begun from Abel than from Adam; because Scripture makes mention of the sin of Adam, and not of his justice, and of the justice of Abel, and not of his sin. Christ 583Btherefore is always the head of all who have been from the beginning, as of those who followed him: through whom alone we have access to the Father.

QUESTION VIII. See that no one deceive you through philosophy and vain deceit (Coloss. II), etc. Was not the knowledge of natural things, which the philosophers handed down, useful for knowing the invisible things of God? For through the visible forms of visible things, the teaching of which is taught in mathematics, one comes to the invisible causes of visible things, which physics teaches: through which one comes to know invisible substances, and the invisible natures of invisible substances. How then does the Apostle call such knowledge vain deceit? Solution. The Apostle does not reprehend the philosophers for 583Cthis, that they inquired into the natures of things; but for this, that they endeavored to confine the power of God, though it be infinite, under natural causes, saying that God does nothing against nature. Whence they said that for God to become a creature, for a virgin to bear, for a dead man to live again, was impossible. This error of theirs therefore the Apostle rightly reprehends: not the true knowledge which they had concerning natures.

QUESTION IX. In whom dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead. Since the fulness of the Godhead is one and simple, how does he say all the fulness of the Godhead, since 'all' is wont to gather a multitude? Solution. It is said 'all the fulness of the Godhead,' that I otetur: that it is there in every mode of indwelling, even personally. Or otherwise: All the fulness is said, that it may be intimated 583Dthat in him is the fulness not only of knowledge, but also of power and goodness. Whereby is destroyed the error of those who say that the man assumed has all the knowledge through grace which the Word has through nature, but not all the power.

QUESTION X. The fulness of the Godhead bodily. Since the Godhead is incorporeal, it is asked how it can dwell bodily in Christ. Solution. He says 'bodily,' that is, completively, solidly, and truly, with regard to the legal figures, which were the shadow of things to come, whose body — that is, fulfillment and truth — is Christ. Or otherwise: 'Bodily' signifies not the nature of the existing thing, but rather 584Athe mode of existing. For just as a body so has being naturally in one place that it cannot at the same time be in another: so the fulness of the Godhead has being in the man assumed: in which mode it is in no other creature. In every creature it is by essence, in the just by grace, in Christ alone according to personal property. This then is for the Godhead to dwell bodily in Christ, that is, personally. Just as a body is in several places at once, not bodily but spiritually. In saying this I do not deny the truth and the essence of the Lord's body to be at once in several altars, but by this I intimate that it does not have that mode of existing common with other bodies, or from the nature of a body, but rather common with a spirit — not created, but uncreated. Both are 584Bwonderful, and true: that a created spirit is somewhere bodily, and that the sacramental body of Christ is in several places spiritually.

QUESTION XI. Blotting out the handwriting of the decree, which was contrary to you, etc. It is asked what he calls the decree, what the handwriting. Solution. By 'decree' he names either the law of Moses itself, or the precept of God which he gave to the first man in paradise, saying: Of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil thou shalt not eat (Gen. II); by 'handwriting,' the record of each violated decree: and the handwritings of all faults have been blotted out by the blood shed without fault.

QUESTION XII. Which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is Christ's. It is asked how shadow, body, and spirit are distinguished. Solution. One thing is shadow, 584Canother body, another spirit: which three are called by other names figure, thing, truth, so that the same is shadow and figure; the same body and thing; the same spirit and truth. The legal ceremonies were called the shadow and figure of things to come. The sacraments of grace are the body, or thing, of those shadows or figures: the spiritual grace, namely, which the sacraments of the New Testament confer and signify, is called the spirit or truth: but the sacraments of the Old Testament only signify spiritual grace, and do not confer it: and this is the difference between these sacraments and those. Likewise it is to be known that those things which in the time of the law were precepts, now in the time of grace are not precepts; but only testimonies of truth, whence then it was a sin not to 584Dobserve even one. But now it is not a sin not to keep them; nay, he who keeps them, offends.

QUESTION XIII. Mortify your members (Coloss. III), etc. It is asked what, or what things, he calls members, which are to be mortified. Are the eye, the hand, the foot to be mortified? Solution. Here the Apostle calls members the concupiscence of the members, as he himself subjoins, and expounds fornication, etc.

QUESTION XIV. Covetousness, which is the service of idols, etc. Is not covetousness one thing, idolatry another? how then does he call covetousness the service of idols? Solution. He therefore compares covetousness to idolatry, because the malice is not unlike. For just as the idolater worships a block, so the covetous man his coin. And just as the idolater strives to take away from God his honor, so the covetous man usurps to himself alone the things 585Awhich God created in common for all.

QUESTION XV. Putting off the old man, etc. It is asked what he here calls the old man. Solution. The old man is sometimes called Adam the first man, who by sinning clothed himself and all his posterity with the tunic of oldness. The old man is sometimes called any man who bears the image of the earthly; but sometimes the old man is called oldness itself, which consists in fault and in punishment; sometimes the old man is named the habit of vices, as here, according to the expositor.

QUESTION XVI. And put on the new man. It is asked likewise what he here calls the new man? For the new man is sometimes called Christ, from whom 585Bis all newness; sometimes the new man is called anyone renewed in Christ; sometimes also the habit of virtues; sometimes specially the mind of reason. But above, that which is called the inner man was said to be the mind; here, however, it is said that the inner mind is called the new man: which seems to be contrary, since the new man is one thing, the inner another, as has already been shown. Solution. The expositor says that he calls the rational mind the new man, nor is it contrary to what was said above, that the inner mind is called man: for the same thing, on account of diverse properties, obtains diverse names.

QUESTION XVII. Who is renewed unto the knowledge of God according to his image, etc. Likewise it is asked how 585Cthe mind is said to be renewed according to the image of God, since it is itself the image of God — can it be renewed according to itself? Solution. It is the same image which is renewed, and that according to which it is renewed, just as we say that someone is dead according to the body, that is, in body, not according to the spirit. And so the mind is renewed according to itself, that is, in itself. In the Epistle to the Ephesians, however, it is said that this very renewal is made according to God: therefore according to God, lest it be said to be according to a creature. For through such a renewal it is made like and conformed to God: therefore it is said to be according to him. Note that this image, which is renewed in the knowledge of God, is found equally in the man and in the woman: which is other 586Athan that of which it was said above: The man is the image of God, and the woman of the man.

QUESTION XVIII. Forgiving one another, if any have a complaint against another. This same thing the Lord commanded, saying: Forgive your debtors (Matth. VI), but what is it that can be forgiven by us? what is the debt that can be exacted by us from him who has done us injury? Solution. This is to forgive the injury inflicted, to demand for ourselves in no way satisfaction on account of the injury: certain other things upon this have been said by us elsewhere.

QUESTION XIX. The expositor says that he who abstains from unlawful things has praise; but he who tempers himself from lawful things, praise and reward — as if he said: The one avoids punishment, the other also merits a crown. But does not also he 586Bwho abstains from unlawful things have not only praise, but also reward? Solution. He who abstains from unlawful things always avoids punishment, but does not always merit a crown, except only then, when he is tempted and assailed.

QUESTION XX. Do all things in the name of the Lord. By 'all things' he understands nothing but good things, which are to be done by us. Whence it is asked whether he prescribes that all things to be done be done for God's sake. Am I by the precepts constrained to give my cloak to a poor man whom I see to be in need, and which I know to please God? For if I withhold it, I seem to despise what I know he wishes to be done. Solution. It is to be understood thus: Do all things in the name of the Lord, that is, do nothing against God, and in good things seek not your own glory, but God's. Not 586Chowever in all things that we do do we merit; because certain things are indifferent, as to sit, to stand, to draw breath, to close the hand, to open the eyes, and the like. But certain things are such as have merit if they be done; and are not a sin if they be not done, as to give a cloak to a poor man, and to sell all things, and give to the poor: which is of the perfect, who follow Christ naked.

QUESTION XXI. Say to Archippus: Take heed to the ministry which thou hast received in the Lord, that thou fulfil it (Coloss. IV). It is asked whether subjects may admonish prelates. Solution. Behold authority, that subjects may admonish prelates, lest they be slothful in foreseeing those things which pertain to salvation.

VIII. IN EPISTOLAM I AD THESSALONICENSES.

  • 585

585D(I Thess. I.) Paulus et Silvanus, etc. Hanc epistolam scribit Apostolus Thessalonicensibus. Thessalonica metropolis est Macedoniae, quae est provincia Graecorum. Thessalonicenses ergo sunt Macedones, sive Graeci, qui ab Apostolo conversi, et nec per tribulationes, nec per pseudopraedicatores potuerunt moveri a fidei veritate. Hos collaudat Apostolus, 586Dquia tantae fidei imbiberant spiritum, ut spe etiam futurorum a civibus suis non credentibus pericula devoto animo pro nomine Christi sustineret. Erant tamen aliqui inter eos otiosi, et curiosi; aliqui etiam minus recte de resurrectione sentientes, et ideo nimis de amicorum morte tenere dolentes. Hos ergo corrigit Apostolus in hac epistola, et monet perfectos 587Anon cedere adversis, et pseudoapostolis, et ut alios corrigant. Scripsit autem ab Athenis. Et est intentio Apostoli in hac Epistola pravos et incorrectos corrigere, et bonos ad perseverantiam, aliorumque correctionem cohortari. Modus talis, more suo salutem praemittit: qua praemissa de bonis eorum gratias agit, commemorans non fidem et opera, sed etiam conversionis modum et malorum sustinentiam ut ad perseverandum provocet; de suis quoque laboribus, et Evangelii veritate, et prudenti inter eos conversatione, et quanto affectu desideret eos videre interserit. Deinde pravos, ut a luxuria, et otio, et curiositate contineant, obsecrat, et mortuos resurrecturos confirmat. Circa finem est moralis instructio. Dicit itaque Paulus et Sylvanus, etc. 587BTimotheus, etc. Nota quod mos erat Apostoli eos in salutatione sibi adjungere, qui secum apud illos vel fuerant, vel futuri erant.

QUAESTIO I. Deo vivo et vero, etc. Quaeritur quare dicat, vero. Solutio. Unus est naturaliter Deus; multi participatione: ad quorum differentiam dicitur verus Deus, utpote si ex se non aliunde Deus est. Alii enim non ex eo quod sunt, dii sunt, sed ex eo quod acceperunt.

QUAESTIO II. Pervenit enim ira Dei super illos. (I Thess. II). Quaeritur quomodo propter peccata sua ira Dei, et poena super eos pervenerit, id est ante mortem. Nunquid poena aeterna allevatur per poenam temporalem? si enim non allevatur, videtur Deus immisericors, qui hic punit, et ibi. Item, si allevatur 587Caeterna per temporalem, videtur quod talis poena non procedat ex ira Dei, sed ex misericordia; et ideo non ira, sed misericordia dicenda. Solutio. Magna quidem Dei misericordia est per poenam temporalem vocare ad poenitentiam; sed ipsi nolentes poenitere, Dei misericordiam vertunt sibi in iram, et poena inflicta, quae potuit esse salutis medium, fit illis aeternae poenae initium.

QUAESTIO III. Festinamus videre faciem vestram cum multo desiderio, etc. Dicit expositor in quo mala eis fierent; sed quaeritur quomodo ex praesentia Doctoris fierent mala discipulis: cum potius bona quam mala ex ea fieri videantur: unde ipse desiderabat videre eos propter utilitatem praesentiae 587Dsuae, scilicet ut eos confirmaret, et ea quae deerant, superadderet. Solutio. Major corona, et laudabilior victoria, si starent immobiles, absente magistro: tamen Apostolus humane timuit ne caderent, et ideo ad eos venire desiderabat.

QUAESTIO IV. In adventu ejus, scilicet Domini. Quaeritur in quo adventu. Solutio. Triplex est adventus Domini, unus in carnem, unus in spiritu, unus in carne. In carnem venit factus homo. In spiritu venit quando Spiritum suum spiritui nostro infudit, ipsum sanans et justificans. In carne veniet in judicio. Occulte etiam venit unicuique in morte, vel ut eos purget, vel ut januam regni aperiat: malis, ut eos puniat.

QUAESTIO V. Ut non contristemini sicut caeteri, 588Aqui spem non habent. (I Thess. IV). Quaeritur an contristari et flere pro morte amicorum sit peccatum, cum Apostolus dicat: Ut non contristemini? Solutio. Necesse est ut cum mors occupat dilectum, ut contristet dilectionis affectum; non ergo culpa, si contristemur necessitate amittendi; si consolamur spe recipiendi: unde Apostolus non dicit simpliciter, ut non contristemini, sed ait, ut non contristemini sicut caeteri, qui spem non habent, quasi diceret: Licet contristari, sed cum spe.

QUAESTIO VI. Quaeritur quomodo Dominus flebat Lazarum mortuum continuo, eo jubente, victurum? Solutio. Non mortuum, sed mortem, quam non meruit peccando, deflebat: ad quam Lazarus, et miserias mundi iterum erat revocandus: et inde Dominus 588Best motus

QUAESTIO VII. Quaeritur an orationes, eleemosynae, sacrificia altaris, omnibus prosint, pro quibus fiunt. Solutio. His solum prosunt praedicta post mortem, qui ita vixerunt ante mortem ut digni sint, ut haec utilia sint eis post mortem: his enim, qui sine fide per dilectionem operantem ab hac vita exierunt, non prosunt; quia hic viventes salutis pignore caruerunt, scilicet ad salutem.

QUAESTIO VIII. Cum Christus omnia possit, quaeritur cur fidelibus suis non donaverit statim immortalitatem, ut omnino mortem nunquam experirentur. Solutio. Si hoc fieret, carni quidem daretur quaedam felicitas, sed fidei minueretur fortitudo. Nemo tunc ad Christi gratiam propter futuram 588Cvitam festinaret; sed tamen propter mortis molestiam fugiendam, et sic quodammodo delicate crederetur in Christum. Ubi igitur tunc esset gloriosus triumphus martyrum?

QUAESTIO IX. Et eos qui dormierunt. Quaeritur, cum Christum, qui jam vivit, dicat mortuum, cur fideles mortuos non mortuos, sed dormientes appellat? Solutio. Ideo dicit Christum mortuum, et surrexisse, ut, dum hoc audimus, idem speremus, scilicet nos resurrecturos per virtutem Deitatis. Electos vero ideo dicit dormientes; quia nemo tam facile potest excitari a sommo, quam facile eos omnes excitabit Deus a sommo mortis.

QUAESTIO X. In voce archangeli, etc. De hac voce 588Dquaeritur, an materialis erit. Solutio. Dicunt quidam quod materialis erit ministerio angelorum formata, sicut illa materialis fuit, quae audita est baptizato Domino, quae ideo dicitur Dei; quia efficaciam ei dabit Deus, ut per illam mortui resurgant. Alii dicunt, quod aliquod evidens signum erit. De incerto ambigua solutio. Omnia enim futura in novissimo, nobis incerta.

QUAESTIO XI. Deinde nos, qui vivimus. Quaeritur quomodo dicat Apostolus, quod illi primi resurgent, qui jam dudum mortui fuerunt, et deinde illi, qui tunc vivi inventi fuerint, cum ipse alibi dicat; quod resurrectio erit in ictu oculi et in momento (I Cor. XV); ubi nec prius, nec posterius sit aliquid, sed omnia simul? Solutio. Potest dici, quod ideo simul 589Afieri dicitur mortuorum resurrectio, quia parva mora erit.

QUAESTIO XII. Quaeri autem solet utrum illi, quos vivos inveniet Christus, sint morituri, an sine morte ad immortalitatem transituri? Solutio. De hoc nihil certum habemus; videtur tamen quibusdam, quod in ipso raptu moriantur, et reviviscant, cum alibi dicat Apostolus: in Christo omnes vivificabuntur (I Cor. XV), et alibi: quod seminas, non vivificatur, nisi prius moriatur (ibid.). Nec incredibile hoc videri debet, cum in momento, et in ictu oculi, communis et generalis resurrectio futura esse credatur.

QUAESTIO XIII. Rapiemur obviam Christo in aera. Quaeritur an id de omnibus dicatur? Solutio. Boni quasi leves Christo occurrent in aera; mali vero 589Bquasi ponderosi non obviam in aera Christo, sed terrae, quam semper amaverunt, adhaerebunt. Nota quatuor esse genera eorum, qui ad judicium venient; quidam enim venient, ut judicent tantum, ut valde boni, non ut judicentur, de quorum salute constat. Alii sunt minus perfecti, de quorum salute nondum constat; hi venient ad judicium, ut judicentur. Sic malorum duo sunt genera; alii venient ad judicium, ut judicentur, ut minus mali de quorum damnatione non constat. Alii vero, non ut judicentur; 590Aquia jam judicati sunt, quia de eorum damnatione jam certum est. Quare ergo venient? nunquid ut judicent? absit! Quare ergo? ut audiant cum diabolo. Ite, maledicti in ignem aeternum (Matth. XXV), etc. De modo judicii jam dictum est in prima epistola ad Corinthios; quomodo scilicet sancti judicaturi, an sola comparatione, an etiam potestate.

QUAESTIO XIV. Dies Domini sicut fur in nocte ita veniet (I Thess. V), etc. Cum nemo sciat, an die, an nocte Dominus venturus sit ad judicium, quaeritur quomodo Apostolus tempus adventus Domini vocet diem. Solutio. Dies in tali loco non ponitur pro illuminatione aeris sicut alibi; sed pro revelatione, id est manifestatione, quia tunc omnia manifestata erunt. Sciet enim unusquisque, quare se, vel alium 590BDominus salvet vel damnet.

QUAESTIO XV. Sine intermissione orare. Quaeritur quomodo hoc praeceptum Apostoli impleri possit. Quis enim potest semper orare? Nonne oportet quandoque dormire? Solutio. Sic intelligitur: Sine intermissione certarum horarum. Vel per orationem intelligitur sanctum desiderium, et pius affectus, et sic justus nunquam desinit orare, nisi desinat justus esse; qui enim semper bene agit, semper bene orat.

VIII. ON THE FIRST EPISTLE TO THE THESSALONIANS.

  • 585

585D(I Thess. I.) Paul and Silvanus, etc. The Apostle writes this epistle to the Thessalonians. Thessalonica is the metropolis of Macedonia, which is a province of the Greeks. The Thessalonians therefore are Macedonians, or Greeks, who, converted by the Apostle, could be moved from the truth of the faith neither by tribulations nor by false preachers. These the Apostle praises together, 586Dbecause they had drunk in the spirit of so great a faith that, even in the hope of things to come, with devoted mind for the name of Christ he sustained perils from his fellow-citizens who did not believe. Yet there were some among them idle and curious; some also thinking less rightly about the resurrection, and therefore grieving too tenderly over the death of their friends. These therefore the Apostle corrects in this epistle, and warns the perfect 587Anot to yield to adversities and false apostles, and to correct others. He wrote, moreover, from Athens. And the intention of the Apostle in this epistle is to correct the depraved and the uncorrected, and to exhort the good to perseverance and to the correction of others. The manner is such: after his own fashion he sends greeting beforehand: which sent beforehand, he gives thanks for their good things, recounting not their faith and works only, but also the manner of their conversion and their endurance of evils, that he may provoke them to persevere; and he inserts also somewhat concerning his own labors, and the truth of the Gospel, and his prudent conduct among them, and with how great affection he desires to see them. Then he beseeches the depraved to restrain themselves from luxury, and idleness, and curiosity, and he confirms that the dead shall rise again. Toward the end is moral instruction. And so he says, Paul and Sylvanus, etc. 587BTimothy, etc. Note that it was the custom of the Apostle to join to himself in the salutation those who either had been with him among them, or were to be.

QUESTION I. To the living and true God, etc. It is asked why he says, true. Solution. There is one God naturally; many by participation: to distinguish from whom he is called the true God, inasmuch as he is God of himself, not from elsewhere. For the others are gods not from the fact that they are, but from the fact that they have received.

QUESTION II. For the wrath of God is come upon them. (I Thess. II). It is asked how, on account of their sins, the wrath of God and punishment came upon them, that is, before death. Is eternal punishment lightened by temporal punishment? for if it is not lightened, God seems merciless, who punishes here, and there. Likewise, if the eternal 587Cis lightened by the temporal, it seems that such punishment proceeds not from the wrath of God, but from mercy; and therefore it is to be called not wrath, but mercy. Solution. Great indeed is the mercy of God to call to penance through temporal punishment; but they, unwilling to repent, turn the mercy of God for themselves into wrath, and the punishment inflicted, which could have been a means of salvation, becomes for them the beginning of eternal punishment.

QUESTION III. We hastened to see your face with much desire, etc. The expositor says wherein evils would come upon them; but it is asked how from the presence of the Teacher evils would come upon the disciples: since rather good things than evils seem to come from it: whence he himself desired to see them for the profit of his own presence, 587Dnamely that he might confirm them, and add over what was lacking. Solution. Greater is the crown, and more praiseworthy the victory, if they should stand immovable, the master being absent: yet the Apostle humanly feared lest they fall, and therefore desired to come to them.

QUESTION IV. At his coming, namely of the Lord. It is asked, at what coming. Solution. Threefold is the coming of the Lord, one in the flesh, one in the spirit, one in the flesh. He came in the flesh made man. He comes in the spirit when he pours his Spirit into our spirit, healing and justifying it. He shall come in the flesh at the judgment. He comes also secretly to each one at death, either to purge them, or to open the gate of the kingdom: to the evil, to punish them.

QUESTION V. That you be not sorrowful, even as the rest 588Awho have no hope. (I Thess. IV). It is asked whether to be sorrowful and to weep for the death of friends is a sin, since the Apostle says: That you be not sorrowful? Solution. It is necessary that, when death seizes one beloved, it sadden the affection of love; it is therefore not a fault, if we be saddened by the necessity of losing, if we be consoled by the hope of receiving again: whence the Apostle does not say simply, that you be not sorrowful, but says, that you be not sorrowful as the rest who have no hope, as if he said: It is lawful to be sorrowful, but with hope.

QUESTION VI. It is asked how the Lord wept for Lazarus, dead but presently, at his own bidding, about to live? Solution. Not the dead man, but death, which he had not deserved by sinning, did he bewail: to which, and to the miseries of the world, Lazarus was again to be recalled: and thence was the Lord 588Bmoved.

QUESTION VII. It is asked whether prayers, alms, the sacrifices of the altar, profit all for whom they are done. Solution. The aforesaid profit after death only those who so lived before death that they are worthy that these be profitable to them after death: for they profit not those who went forth from this life without faith working through love; because, living here, they lacked the pledge of salvation, namely unto salvation.

QUESTION VIII. Since Christ can do all things, it is asked why he did not straightway grant immortality to his faithful, that they should never at all experience death. Solution. If this were done, a certain felicity indeed would be given to the flesh, but the fortitude of faith would be diminished. No one then would hasten to the grace of Christ for the sake of the future 588Clife; but only for the sake of fleeing the trouble of death, and so in a certain manner delicately would men believe in Christ. Where then would be the glorious triumph of the martyrs?

QUESTION IX. And those who have slept. It is asked, since he calls Christ, who now lives, dead, why he calls the faithful dead not dead, but sleeping? Solution. He therefore says Christ died, and rose again, that, while we hear this, we may hope the same, namely that we shall rise again through the power of the Godhead. But the elect he therefore calls sleeping; because no one can be so easily wakened from sommo, as easily as God will waken them all from the sommo of death.

QUESTION X. At the voice of the archangel, etc. Concerning this voice 588Dit is asked, whether it will be material. Solution. Some say that it will be material, formed by the ministry of angels, just as that was material which was heard when the Lord was baptized, which is therefore called God's; because God will give it efficacy, that through it the dead may rise. Others say that it will be some evident sign. Concerning the uncertain, an ambiguous solution. For all things future at the last day are uncertain to us.

QUESTION XI. Then we who live. It is asked how the Apostle says that those first shall rise who were dead long since, and then those who shall then be found alive, since he himself elsewhere says that the resurrection shall be in the twinkling of an eye and in a moment (I Cor. XV); wherein there is nothing prior, nor posterior, but all things at once? Solution. It can be said that the resurrection of the dead is therefore said 589Ato be made at once, because there will be a little delay.

QUESTION XII. It is wont, however, to be asked whether those whom Christ shall find alive are to die, or to pass without death to immortality? Solution. Concerning this we have nothing certain; yet it seems to some that in the very rapture they die, and revive, since elsewhere the Apostle says: In Christ all shall be made alive (I Cor. XV), and elsewhere: that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it first die (ibid.). Nor ought this to seem incredible, since in a moment, and in the twinkling of an eye, the common and general resurrection is believed to be about to be.

QUESTION XIII. We shall be caught up to meet Christ in the air. It is asked whether this is said of all? Solution. The good, as it were light, shall run to meet Christ in the air; but the evil, 589Bas it were weighty, shall cleave not to meet Christ in the air, but to the earth, which they always loved. Note that there are four kinds of those who shall come to the judgment; for some shall come to judge only, as the very good, not to be judged, of whose salvation it is settled. Others are the less perfect, of whose salvation it is not yet settled; these shall come to the judgment, to be judged. So there are two kinds of the evil; some shall come to the judgment, to be judged, as the less evil, of whose damnation it is not settled. But others, not to be judged; 590Abecause they are already judged, since concerning their damnation it is already certain. Why then shall they come? shall it be to judge? God forbid! Why then? that they may hear with the devil: Go, ye cursed, into everlasting fire (Matth. XXV), etc. Concerning the manner of the judgment it has already been said in the first epistle to the Corinthians; namely how the saints shall judge, whether by comparison alone, or also by power.

QUESTION XIV. The day of the Lord shall so come as a thief in the night (I Thess. V), etc. Since no one knows whether by day or by night the Lord shall come to the judgment, it is asked how the Apostle calls the time of the Lord's coming day. Solution. Day in such a place is not put for the illumination of the air as elsewhere; but for revelation, that is, manifestation, because then all things shall be manifested. For each one shall know why the Lord saves or damns him 590Bor another.

QUESTION XV. To pray without ceasing. It is asked how this precept of the Apostle can be fulfilled. For who can always pray? Is it not needful sometimes to sleep? Solution. It is thus understood: Without ceasing at the fixed hours. Or by prayer is understood holy desire, and pious affection, and so the just man never ceases to pray, unless he cease to be just; for he who always does well, always prays well.

IX. IN EPISTOLAM II AD THESSALONICENSES.

  • 589

589CPaulus, et Silvanus (II Thess. I), etc. Hanc Epistolam scribit Apostolus Thessalonicensibus. Orta enim apud eos graviori tribulatione monet eos ad patientiam, ostendens justum Dei judicium, ut boni gloriam consequantur, mali poenam. Et quia in prima epistola quaedam dicit de Adventu Domini et de resurrectione mortuorum, unde putabatur dies Domini instare; nunc alteram scribit epistolam, in qua significat, licet obscure (nec enim aperte potest), de abolitione regni Romani, de Antichristi apparentia, et damnatione, et de quorumdam fratrum inquietudine. Scribit etiam non instare diem Domini sicut occasione prioris Epistolae quibusdam videtur. Est itaque intentio Apostoli in hac epistola, bonos et quietos ad patientiam movere, et inquietos 589Dcorrigere; et quae obscure dixerat in priori epistola, hic aliquatenus aperire. Modus talis, primo salutat, deinde gratias agit de bonis eorum; postea monet ad patientiam, et ad constantiam; inde asserit, quod adventum Christi praeveniet Antichristus, et aliqua adventus Antichristi signa licet obscure denuntiat, agens de abolitione Romani regni et de interfectione Antichristi. Circa finem vero, ut curiosos atque otiosos corripiant, obsecrat.

QUAESTIO I. In flamma ignis dantis vindictam iis, qui non noverunt Deum. Quaeritur, an Dominus in 590Cigne circumdatus venturus sit ad judicium? Solutio. In flamma ignis dicitur venturus, quia terribilis impiis apparebit, ut eos exurat atque cruciet. Ignis quidem ejus adventum praecedet, quo elementa solventur, ut renoventur.

QUAESTIO II. Quaeritur quomodo vivi reservabuntur illi, quos vivos inveniet Dominus. Solutio. Sicut tres pueros in camino fornacis, ignis non laesit; sic ille ignis praecedens adventum judicis bonos non laedet.

QUAESTIO III. Quaeritur quas poenas animae impiorum nunc patiuntur apud inferos, an materiales, an tantum conscientiae tortiones? Solutio. Creditur, quod poenas materiales, ut ignem et frigus patiantur. Unde dicitur: Transibunt de aquis nivium ad 590Dcalorem nimium (Job. XXIV).

QUAESTIO IV. Item quaeritur quomodo his poenis torquentur, cum res spirituales a corporeis contingi nequeant. Solutio. Fieri potest ut per ea puniantur, a quibus non continguntur, velut quis horrorem magnum ex aliquo viso vel imaginato contrahit, etsi ab illo non contingatur.

QUAESTIO V. Item resumptis corporibus, cum illa deinceps immortalia futura sint, quomodo in illis punientur, cum dissolvi nequeant? Solutio. Erunt quidem corpora malorum immortalia, sed passibilia, 591Aid est talia in quibus mali patiantur, sine tamen laesione naturalis quantitatis, vel essentiae ipsorum corporum.

QUAESTIO VI. Nisi venerit discessio primum (II Thess. II), etc. Quaeritur: quomodo quod dicit de discessione fiet? Solutio. Hoc quatuor modis potest intelligi, vel de terreno Romano imperio vel de spirituali imperio Romanae Ecclesiae, vel de fide, vel de Antichristo. Cum alia translatio dicit Refuga. Nota quod legitur quod Antichristus nascetur in Babylone de tribu Dan. Juxta quod Jacob ait: Fiat Dan coluber in via, et cerastes in semita (Gen. XLIX). Qui cum primum se manifestabit veniet Hierosolymam, et circumcidet, se dicens: Ego sum Christus Judaeis promissus.

591BQUAESTIO VII. Qui extollitur super omne, quod dicitur Deus, ut dii gentium vel sancti; aut quod colitur, ut Deus Trinitas. Sed quaeritur quomodo poterit se extollere super Deum trinitatem? Nonne haec erit maxima ejus superbia et extollentia quod dicet se Christum esse, et ita Deo aequalem, non enim majorem se dicet; quomodo ergo extollitur super omne quod colitur Deus? Solutio. Ut mihi videtur in hoc intelligitur haec extollentia, quod ille iniquus, homo peccati, filius perditionis, venerationem et culturam soli Deo Trinitati debitam, faciet sibi exhiberi et non Deo. Legitur quod sicut in Christo habitavit plenitudo divinitatis, ita in Antichristo plenitudo malitiae, et omnis iniquitatis, et, ut ita dicam, plenitudo diabolitatis erit.

591CQUAESTIO VIII. Unde potest quaeri an erit homo simpliciter, an diabolus personaliter eum assumet, ut Deus hominem. Solutio. Non potest diabolus sic hominem assumere, ut sibi personaliter unitus sit; erit ergo purus homo, quem tamen diabolus sic possidebit, ut omni virtute nequitiae suae, et omni iniquitate impleat, ut prorsus deditus illi et devotus nihil velit, nihil possit nisi quod diabolus vult et potest.

QUAESTIO IX. Mysterium jam operatur iniquitatis. Dicit expositor, quod in Nerone et in aliis malis occulte operatur jam diabolus, qui in Antichristo aperte saeviet. Unde quaeritur quomodo occulte operetur in Nerone. Nonne Nero Christum negavit, et 591Daperte eos, qui Christum praedicabant, persecutus est? Solutio. Ideo dicitur in Nerone operari occulte; quia hoc fecit Nero fraudulenta quorumdam suggestione. Vel, quod melius est, ideo dictus est diabolus operari occulte in Nerone, non quia manifesta esset illa persecutio, sed quia illa est umbra, et figura, et imago quaedam illius, quae fiet per Antichristum quae multo gravior erit omnibus, quae praecesserunt. Regnabit enim tribus annis, et dimidio; et sedens in papilione in monte Oliveti interficietur virtute Spiritus sancti per Michaelem, ut ipsum Dominum vel alium angelum, ut dicunt doctores.

QUAESTIO X. Quem Dominus destruet illustratione adventus sui etc. Nonne Antichristus prius interficietur 592Aantequam Dominus veniat ad judicium? Ex libro enim Danielis intelligitur, quod concedentur electis quadraginta duo dies ad poenitentiam post mortem Antichristi. Quanto vero post venturus sit Dominus, penitus nescitur non solum ab hominibus, sed etiam ab angelis. Quomodo ergo dicit apostolus: Illustratione adventus sui (cum ante adventum sit interficiendus) destruet illum Dominus? Solutio.
