Interficietur quidem, ut creditur, ante adventum Domini Antichristus corporis, et animae solutione; Dominus tamen destruet illum jam resuscitatum cum toto corpore, illustratione adventus sui damnando, et in ignem aeternum mittendo, dicens illi et aliis reprobis: Ite, maledicti, in ignem aeternum (Matth. XXV).

592BQUAESTIO XI. Secundum operationem Satanae, etc. Dicit expositor, non tamen sine sensu, ut phrenetici, qui culpam non habent de malis quae agunt. Unde potest quaeri, si totum faciet Antichristus diabolo instigante et cooperante, et quodammodo compellente, quare ei imputetur potius quam phreneticis, vel si phrenetici hoc faciunt diabolo instigante, quare eis non imputatur. Et quomodo sunt sine culpa de malis quae agunt, potius quam ille iniquus? Solutio. Phrenetici, qui sunt sine sensu magis dicendi sunt aliquid pati quam aliquid agere; et mala fiunt potius per eos quam ab ipsis; quoniam ipsi non sunt auctores, cum voluntatem ad hoc non applicent. Antichristus vero sic diabolo instigante omnia faciet, quod voluntatem suam omnem et 592Csensum ad eumdem applicabit; et ideo ei omnia imputabuntur ad poenam aeternam.

QUAESTIO XII. Signis, et prodigiis mendacibus, etc. Quaeritur de signis illis, quae per diabolum faciet Antichristus, an ideo dicta sint mendacia, quia non vera ut videntur, sed phantastica erunt; id est quia mortales sensus per phantasmata decepturus est, vel ideo dicta sunt mendacia, quia Dei permissione ad mendacium trahent? Solutio. Videtur nobis verisimile esse, quod omnia signa illa, quae diabolus poterit facere, et Antichristus faciet vere. Illa vero, quae diabolus non habet in sua potestate, nec ille iniquus faciet vere, sed per solam magicam artem deludet oculos mortalium ut videatur facere, quae 592Dvere non faciet. Unde Apostolus dicit: Cujus adventus erit in omni virtute, quantum ad ea, quae vere faciet, et in omni seductione, quantum ad ea quae non vere faciet. Omnia tamen valent ad seductionem impiorum. Quae autem sunt illa, quae diabolus poterit et quae non potestati ejus subjacent, non est nostrae parvitatis evolvere.

QUAESTIO XIII. Mittet illis Deus operationem erroris, ut credant mendacio, ut judicentur, etc. Quaeritur autem de illis qui signis et prodigiis illius iniqui permoti credent ipsum esse bonum, et Dei Filium: an habeant aliquam excusationem? Si enim ei non divinum cultum exhibebunt, cum conscientia eorum dictet eis, ipsum tanquam Deum adorandum, ad mortem peccabunt, et ita videntur inexcusabiles 593Aesse. Solutio. Apostolus dicit quia non receperunt claritatem veritatis, ut salvi fierunt, id est Christum prius manifeste praedicatum, mittet illius Deus operationem erroris, ut credant mendacio et judicentur: ubi satis docet quod propter praecedentia peccata non habebunt excusationem, etsi arbitrentur se obsequium praestare Christo, id est vero Deo, credendo in Antichristum

QUAESTIO XIV. Dicit Augustinus quod posse habere fidem, vel charitatem, natura fidelium est: habere fidem, vel charitatem, gratia Dei. Unde potest quaeri quomodo hoc debeat intelligi. Nonne quod naturale est, nobis in nostra facultate est? sed cum habere fidem, vel charitatem sine gratia non possumus, quomodo posse habere fidem, natura 593Best fidelium? Solutio. Posse habere fidem, id est potentia habendi, naturalis est; sed hujus potentiae usum habere, solius gratiae est, et non naturae.

QUAESTIO XV. Qui non vult operari, non manducet 594A(II Thess. III). Quaeritur de quo opere hic agatur. Si enim de exteriori, quomodo praecipit ne manducet qui non vult operari? Multi enim digni sunt manducare, licet non operentur. Solutio. Augustinus dicit quod Apostolus vult servos Dei corporaliter operari, ut non compellantur egestate, necessaria petere; non tamen male agunt, qui opera exteriora pro spiritualibus postponunt cum habeant unde vivant, quia Maria optimam partem elegit (Luc. X). Illi vero, qui curiositati dediti operari nolunt, reprehenduntur; non qui minora bona pro majoribus deserunt.

QUAESTIO XVI. Si quis non obedierit verbo nostro per Epistolam, hunc notate, et non commisceamini cum illo, ut confundatur. Dicit ita Apostolus, quod ille 594Bqui admonitioni Ecclesiae resistit excommunicandus est. Unde quaeri potest qualiter id faciendum est. Et certum quod magna discretione faciendum est, ne Ecclesia detrimentum incurrat, nec levi causa talis vindicta exercenda est.

IX. ON THE SECOND EPISTLE TO THE THESSALONIANS.

  • 589

589CPaul, and Silvanus (II Thess. I), etc. The Apostle writes this epistle to the Thessalonians. For, a graver tribulation having arisen among them, he warns them to patience, showing the just judgment of God, that the good may attain glory, the evil punishment. And because in the first epistle he says certain things concerning the Coming of the Lord and concerning the resurrection of the dead, whence the day of the Lord was thought to be at hand; now he writes another epistle, in which he signifies, though obscurely (for he cannot do so openly), concerning the abolition of the Roman kingdom, concerning the appearing of Antichrist, and his damnation, and concerning the disquiet of certain brethren. He writes also that the day of the Lord is not at hand, as by occasion of the former epistle it seemed to some. And so the intention of the Apostle in this epistle is to move the good and the quiet 589Dto patience, and to correct the unquiet; and to open somewhat here what he had said obscurely in the former epistle. The manner is such: first he salutes, then he gives thanks for their good things; afterward he warns to patience, and to constancy; thence he asserts that Antichrist shall forestall the coming of Christ, and announces some signs of the coming of Antichrist, though obscurely, treating of the abolition of the Roman kingdom and of the slaying of Antichrist. But toward the end he beseeches them to rebuke the curious and the idle.

QUESTION I. In a flame of fire, giving vengeance to them who have not known God. It is asked, whether the Lord 590Cshall come to the judgment surrounded in fire? Solution. He is said to be about to come in a flame of fire, because he shall appear terrible to the ungodly, to burn and to torment them. Fire indeed shall precede his coming, by which the elements shall be dissolved, that they may be renewed.

QUESTION II. It is asked how those shall be kept alive whom the Lord shall find alive. Solution. Just as the fire did not hurt the three children in the furnace of the oven; so that fire preceding the coming of the judge shall not hurt the good.

QUESTION III. It is asked what punishments the souls of the ungodly now suffer among those below, whether material, or only tortures of conscience? Solution. It is believed that they suffer material punishments, as fire and cold. Whence it is said: They shall pass from the waters of snows to 590Dexcessive heat (Job. XXIV).

QUESTION IV. Likewise it is asked how they are tormented by these punishments, since spiritual things cannot be touched by bodily. Solution. It can come about that they be punished by those things by which they are not touched, just as one contracts a great horror from something seen or imagined, although he be not touched by it.

QUESTION V. Likewise, their bodies being resumed, since these shall thereafter be immortal, how shall they be punished in them, since they cannot be dissolved? Solution. The bodies of the evil shall indeed be immortal, but passible, 591Athat is, such in which the evil may suffer, yet without harm to the natural quantity, or essence, of the bodies themselves.

QUESTION VI. Except there come a departure first (II Thess. II), etc. It is asked: how shall that which he says concerning the departure come to pass? Solution. This can be understood in four ways, either of the earthly Roman empire, or of the spiritual empire of the Roman Church, or of the faith, or of Antichrist. For another translation says the Runaway. Note that it is read that Antichrist shall be born in Babylon of the tribe of Dan. According to which Jacob says: Let Dan be a serpent in the way, and a horned snake in the path (Gen. XLIX). Who, when he shall first manifest himself, shall come to Jerusalem, and shall circumcise himself, saying: I am Christ promised to the Jews.

591BQUESTION VII. Who is lifted up above all that is called God, as the gods of the nations or the saints; or that is worshipped, as God the Trinity. But it is asked how he shall be able to lift himself up above God the Trinity? Will not this be his greatest pride and self-exaltation, that he shall say himself to be Christ, and thus equal to God — for he will not say himself greater; how then is he lifted up above all that is worshipped as God? Solution. As it seems to me, this self-exaltation is understood in this, that that wicked one, the man of sin, the son of perdition, shall cause the veneration and worship due to God the Trinity alone to be exhibited to himself and not to God. It is read that just as in Christ dwelt the fulness of the Godhead, so in Antichrist there shall be the fulness of malice, and of all iniquity, and, so to say, the fulness of devilishness.

591CQUESTION VIII. Whence it can be asked whether he will be a man simply, or whether the devil will assume him personally, as God man. Solution. The devil cannot so assume a man that he be personally united to himself; he will therefore be a pure man, whom nevertheless the devil will so possess that he shall fill him with all the power of his wickedness, and with all iniquity, so that, utterly given over and devoted to him, he shall wish nothing, be able to do nothing, save what the devil wishes and is able to do.

QUESTION IX. The mystery of iniquity already worketh. The expositor says that in Nero and in other evil men the devil already works secretly, who in Antichrist shall openly rage. Whence it is asked how he works secretly in Nero. Did not Nero deny Christ, and 591Dopenly persecute those who preached Christ? Solution. He is therefore said to work secretly in Nero; because Nero did this by the fraudulent suggestion of certain men. Or, which is better, the devil is therefore said to work secretly in Nero, not because that persecution was not manifest, but because it is a shadow, and figure, and a certain image of that which shall be done through Antichrist, which shall be much graver than all which have gone before. For he shall reign three years and a half; and, sitting in a pavilion on the Mount of Olives, he shall be slain by the power of the Holy Spirit through Michael, as the doctors say, or the Lord himself, or some other angel.

QUESTION X. Whom the Lord shall destroy with the brightness of his coming, etc. Shall not Antichrist first be slain 592Abefore the Lord come to the judgment? For from the book of Daniel it is understood that forty-two days shall be granted to the elect for penance after the death of Antichrist. But how long after the Lord shall come is utterly unknown not only to men, but even to the angels. How then does the Apostle say: With the brightness of his coming (since before the coming he is to be slain) the Lord shall destroy him? Solution. Antichrist shall indeed be slain, as is believed, before the coming of the Lord, by the dissolution of body and soul; yet the Lord shall destroy him, now raised again with his whole body, with the brightness of his coming, damning him, and sending him into everlasting fire, saying to him and to the other reprobate: Go, ye cursed, into everlasting fire (Matth. XXV).

592BQUESTION XI. According to the working of Satan, etc. The expositor says, yet not without sense, as the frenzied, who have no fault for the evils which they do. Whence it can be asked, if Antichrist shall do the whole with the devil instigating and cooperating, and in a manner compelling, why it is imputed to him rather than to the frenzied, or if the frenzied do this with the devil instigating, why it is not imputed to them. And how are they without fault for the evils which they do, rather than that wicked one? Solution. The frenzied, who are without sense, are rather to be said to suffer something than to do something; and evils are done rather through them than by them; since they themselves are not the authors, seeing they do not apply the will to this. But Antichrist shall so do all things, with the devil instigating, that he shall apply his whole will and 592Csense to the same; and therefore all things shall be imputed to him unto eternal punishment.

QUESTION XII. With signs, and lying wonders, etc. It is asked concerning those signs which Antichrist shall do through the devil, whether they are therefore called lying, because they are not true as they seem, but phantastic; that is, because he is about to deceive mortal senses through phantasms, or whether they are therefore called lying, because by God's permission they shall draw men to a lie? Solution. It seems to us to be probable, that all those signs which the devil shall be able to do, Antichrist shall also do truly. But those which the devil has not in his power, neither shall that wicked one do truly, but by magic art alone he shall delude the eyes of mortals, that he may seem to do what 592Dhe shall not truly do. Whence the Apostle says: Whose coming shall be in all power, as regards those things which he shall do truly, and in all seduction, as regards those things which he shall not do truly. Yet all avail unto the seduction of the ungodly. But what those things are which the devil shall be able [to do], and what things lie not subject to his power, it is not for our littleness to unfold.

QUESTION XIII. God shall send them the operation of error, to believe a lie, that they may be judged, etc. It is asked, however, concerning those who, moved by the signs and wonders of that wicked one, shall believe him to be good, and the Son of God: whether they have any excuse? For if they do not exhibit divine worship to him, since their conscience dictates to them that he is to be adored as God, they shall sin unto death, and thus they seem to be inexcusable 593A. Solution. The Apostle says that because they received not the brightness of the truth, that they were saved — that is, Christ formerly manifestly preached — God shall send them the operation of error, that they may believe a lie and be judged: wherein he sufficiently teaches that, on account of their preceding sins, they shall have no excuse, even if they judge themselves to render obedience to Christ, that is, to the true God, by believing in Antichrist.

QUESTION XIV. Augustine says that to be able to have faith, or charity, is of the nature of the faithful: to have faith, or charity, is of the grace of God. Whence it can be asked how this ought to be understood. Is not that which is natural in our own faculty? but since we cannot have faith, or charity, without grace, how is to be able to have faith of the nature 593Bof the faithful? Solution. To be able to have faith, that is, the potency of having, is natural; but to have the use of this potency is of grace alone, and not of nature.

QUESTION XV. He that will not work, let him not eat 594A(II Thess. III). It is asked of what work he here treats. For if of the outward, how does he prescribe that he not eat who will not work? For many are worthy to eat, though they work not. Solution. Augustine says that the Apostle wills the servants of God to work bodily, that they be not compelled by want to seek necessaries; yet they do not act ill who postpone outward works for spiritual ones when they have whereof to live, because Mary hath chosen the best part (Luc. X). But those who, given over to curiosity, will not work, are reprehended; not those who forsake lesser goods for greater.

QUESTION XVI. If any obey not our word by an epistle, note that man, and do not keep company with him, that he may be confounded. The Apostle says thus, that he 594Bwho resists the admonition of the Church is to be excommunicated. Whence it can be asked in what manner this is to be done. And it is certain that it is to be done with great discretion, lest the Church incur detriment, nor is such punishment to be exercised for a light cause.

X. IN EPISTOLAM I AD TIMOTHEUM.

  • 593

593CPaulus apostolus (I Tim. I), etc. Hanc Epistolam scribit Apostolus Timotheo, qui fuit filius cujusdam mulieris fidelis patre gentili procreatus: et cum non esset circumcisus, et ipse esset gentilis, et de eo darent bonum testimonium fratres, qui erant in Listris et Iconio, hunc voluit Paulus proficisci secum: et ideo eum circumcidi propter Judaeos qui in locis illis erant. Eratque eruditus tam divinis Scripturis quam liberalibus artibus. Hunc Apostolus episcopum creavit: ideo eum, relictum in Asia instruit in hac Epistola de officio episcopali, scilicet quomodo pseudoapostolis resistat et quomodo Ecclesiam instruat, quales presbyteros vel diaconos ordinet; quales viduas honoret, et quomodo in Ecclesia se habeat, vel quomodo eam regat. Et est intentio 593DApostoli in hac Epistola instruere Timotheum de episcopalis dignitatis officio. Modus talis: primo salutat eum; deinde monet ut pseudo resistat; postea instruit de episcopali officio, docens quales debeat ordinare presbyteros et diaconos. Deinde quales viduas recipere debeat; postea de modo correptionis instruit eum; in fine autem monet ut vitet profanas novitates.

QUAESTIO I. Dei patris Salvatoris nostri, etc. Cum Filius frequenter dicatur in Scriptura Salvator, qui solus pro salute nostra mortuus est, non Pater, non Spiritus sanctus, quaeritur cur Apostolus salutem nostram ad Deum Patrem referat, dicens hic: Dei Patris Salvatoris nostri. Solutio. Deus pater in hoc, quod dignatus est nobis Filium suum mittere, et Spiritum sanctum in sacramentis Novi Testamenti 594Ctribuere, auctor est salutis nostrae et ideo Salvator dicitur.

QUAESTIO II. Et Jesu Christi spei nostrae. Item quaeritur quare spem specialiter ad Filium referat, dicens, et Jesu Christi spei nostrae, cum in totam Trinitatem speremus et credamus. Solutio. Ideo spem nostram ad Christum, quia ipse a mortuis resurrexit, et ad coelos ascendit, referimus; quia per ejus resurrectionem speramus ad gloriam resurrectionis futurae pertingere.

QUAESTIO III. Gratia, misericordia et pax, etc. Quaeritur cur praeter solitum, Apostolus in hac salutatione tria ponat dicens, gratia, misericordia, et pax. Solutio. Novem praecedentes Epistolas scripsit communiter ad Ecclesias. Hanc autem specialiter Timotheo 594Dcoepiscopo; ideo tria ponit. Per misericordiam idem intelligens, quod in aliis per gratiam scilicet remissionem peccatorum; per pacem tranquillitatem et praelibationem futurae vitae; per gratiam vero intelligit donationem Spiritus sancti, qua armantur ministri Christi.

QUAESTIO IV. Ut non intenderent fabulis, etc. Quaeritur quid hic per fabulas intelligat Apostolus? nunquid legis verba, et divina eloquia sic vocat in hoc loco? et alibi dicit: Profanas et aniles fabulas devita (I Tim. IV). Solutio. Fabulas hic dicit doctrinam illorum, qui legem cum gratia praedicant esse necessariam. Vel fabulas hic dicit traditiones, quas Judaei non scriptas tenent, et alter in alterum transfundit loquendo, quas deuterosin vocant: ubi dicunt, et credunt duas uxores Deum primo creasse, ex quibus 595Ahominum texunt genealogias infinitas parientes infructuosas quaestiones. De quibus traditionibus a sacris Scripturis alienis, Dominus dicit in Evangelio: Quare irritum fecistis mandatum Dei propter traditiones vestras? (Matth. XV.).

QUAESTIO V. Finis autem praecepti est charitas, de corde puro, et conscientia bona, et fide non ficta. Hic definit Apostolus charitatem, ut dicit expositor. Unde potest quaeri quae sit definitio hic data, an hoc finis praecepti? an hoc de corde puro, et conscientia bona, et fide non ficta? Solutio. Definitio charitatis est, esse de corde puro, et conscientia bona, et fide non ficta.

QUAESTIO VI. Item potest quaeri an haec definitio conveniat omni charitati. Quod si concedatur, nullus 595Best habens charitatem, qui non sit perfectus, quia legem consummans et perficiens; quia charitas finis est praecepti, id est perfectio et consummatio. Si enim finis ponitur pro consummatione in hoc loco. Alibi autem ponitur pro consumptione, ut cum dicitur, panis finitur. Alibi pro termino, ut cum dicitur: Hic finitur ager. Item, quis potest habere cor purum et conscientiam bonam sine charitate? nonne cordis munditia, et bona conscientia procedit ex charitate? quomodo ergo charitas procedit de corde puro? Solutio. Videtur mihi quod hic definitio perfectae et consummatae charitatis assignatur, et ita non convenit haec definitio imperfectae charitati. Primum datur dilectio, quae cor mundat, et ex qua bona 595Copera fiunt, et ex quibus nascitur bona conscientia, tandem corde mundato, et bona conscientia comparata perficitur charitas et consummatur, quae est finis praecepti. Haec dico sine praejudicio melioris sententiae.

QUAESTIO VII. Bona est lex, si quis ea legitime utatur. Quaeritur quid sit legitime uti? Solutio. Ut dicit expositor, ille utitur legitime lege, qui eam spiritualiter intelligens per eam cognoscit morbum, et quaerit medicum, et qui scit eam ad tempus datam, et deserit eam propter Christum. Notandum quod injustus legitime utitur lege, cum intelligit quare data sit, et ejus timore fugit ad gratiam Christi, ut fiat justus. Justus autem legitime utitur lege, cum eam terrendo imponit injustis.

595DQUAESTIO VIII. Lex non est posita justo. Nonne David et alii justi, qui sub lege erant, tenebantur legem custodire, quomodo ergo lex non est justo posita? Solutio. Lex non imponitur justo, ut ei dominetur, et eum timore coerceat, et justus non est sub lege, sed potius cum ipsa, tanquam legis amicus.

QUAESTIO IX. Quia ignorans feci, etc. Dicit expositor quod istud, quia potest causam notare vel consecutionem. Ssd quaeritur quomodo ignorantia, quae culpa est, possit esse causa divinae misericordiae. Solutio. Est quaedam ignorantia ex infirmitate: ex qua si quis zelo bono agat contra Deum, ex affectu, quem habet, meretur ab illa ignorantia liberari.

596AQUAESTIO X. Venit in hunc mundum peccatores salvos facere, etc. Quaeritur de parvulis, qui sunt nati ex parentibus baptizatis, an pertineant ad peccatores, propter quos salvandos venit Jesus in mundum. Hi enim peccatum actuale non habent, et originale quomodo contrahere possunt a parentibus, quod ipsi non habent; quia est eis dimissum. Solutio. Sciendum est quod originale peccatum sic dimittitur in baptismo, non ut omnino non sit, sed ut culpa non sit. Manet vero corruptionis vitium etiam in baptizatis, qui generant, non ex eo quo sunt renati, sed ex vetustate corruptionis, per quam transit culpa originalis in parvulos: unde et ipsi indigent remedio. Unde et ipse medicus ait: Parvulos sinite venire ad me (Marc. X).

596BQUAESTIO XI. Quorum ego primus sum. Nonne Cain et Saul priores Paulo fuerunt? quomodo ergo Paulus inter peccatores primus? Solutio. Primus erat Paulus non ordine temporis, sed magnitudine iniquitatis. Cui solutioni sic objicitur: Nonne Paulus peccavit per ignorantiam, et multi alii scienter? sed majus peccatum est peccare scienter quam per ignorantiam: non ergo Paulus primus erat inter peccatores magnitudine iniquitatis, cum alii, maxime illi, qui peccaverunt in Spiritum sanctum, multo pejores sint Paulo etiam secundum statum primum, in quo fuit blasphemus, persecutor, contumeliosus. Solutio. Paulus magnitudinem delictorum suorum considerans omnibus peccatoribus judicavit se pejorem, 596Clicet in oculis Dei aliter fuit.

QUAESTIO. XII. Regi autem saeculorum immortali, invisibili, soli Deo, honor et gloria in saecula saeculorum. Amen. Dicit expositor quod homo assumptus a Verbo ex eo tempore rex est saeculorum, ex quo assumptus est a Verbo; sed si homo assumptus non est homo, nec Deus, nec persona, ut quidam ausi sunt profiteri, quomodo homo assumptus ex quo est assumptus, et non ante, rex est saeculorum? Nos autem dicimus quod homo assumptus a Verbo est homo et Deus: ipsum Verbum a quo assumptus est, et coepit in tempore esse rex saeculorum, quando videlicet coepit assumi a Verbo. Quando enim coepit esse Deus homo, coepit et homo esse Deus, sicut multae auctoritates protestantur.

596DQUAESTIO XIII. Qui omnes homines vult salvos fieri (I Tim. II). Cum Deus sit omnipotens, et divinae voluntati nullus resistere possit, quomodo non omnes salvi fiunt, cum Deus omnes velit salvos fieri? Vel nunquid voluntas ejus est, ut reprobi salventur? Ambrosius sic solvit: Deus vult omnes salvos fieri, si ipsi velint. Sed nonne multi volunt salvi fieri, qui tamen non salvantur? quomodo ergo verum est, Deus vult omnes salvos fieri? Ideoque alii sic exponunt: Deus vult, etc., placeret ipsi, si omnes salvarentur, vel omnes, id est de omni genere hominum aliqui. Vel sic: Omnibus gratiam offert, per quam si volunt salvari possunt. Sed haec solutio quomodo vera? Nonne multi sunt et fuerunt, qui ne verbum quidem praedicationis audierunt? Vel omnes vult salvos fieri, 597Aid est facit sanctos velle, ut omnes salvi fiant. Vel sic: Vult omnes salvos fieri, id est nullus fit salvus, nisi ipse velit. Simili modo intelligitur illud: Qui illuminat omnem hominem (Joan. I), id est nullus illuminatur, nisi ab ipso, et omnes in Christo vivificantur, juxta eumdem modum oportet intelligi. Sic de ambiguo diversae sententiae dantur.

QUAESTIO XIV. Unus mediator Dei, et hominum homo Christus Jesus. De mediatore jam superius ex parte dictum est. Hic autem illud sufficiat intueri quod dicit expositor, quod in quantum est homo, est medius, non in quantum Verbum. Sed nonne inter angelos, et Deum Patrem, et etiam inter Spiritum sanctum medius est in quantum est Verbum, licet aliter inter angelos et Deum Patrem, et aliter in Spiritum 597Bsanctum medius sit et Patrem? Solutio. Bene concedi potest quod, in quantum est Verbum, medius inter rationales creaturas et Deum Patrem est; sed non est medius inter Deum Trinitatem, et homines in quantum Verbum est, sed in quantum est homo similis Deo in justitia, hominibus in mortalitate. Si enim in quantum est Verbum, esset medius inter homines et Deum Trinitatem, jam aliquid esset medium inter seipsum et aliud, quia verbum inter se et homines; quod non est concedendum. Dicet aliquis: Jam Christus non est mortalis, quomodo ergo est medius inter homines mortales, et Deum immortalem, cum ideo medius dictus sit; quia similis est hominibus per mortalitatem, et Deo per justitiam? Solutio. Adhuc nos Christus Deo Patri tanquam 597Cmediator optimus reconciliat per id quod pro nobis fecit in diebus carnis suae, id est mortalitati.

QUAESTIO XV. Adam non est seductus, sed mulier. Quaeritur uter plus peccaverit, an Adam, an Eva? Solutio. Dicunt doctores, quod mulier non solum peccavit; sed etiam virum peccare fecit. Cui solutioni sic objicitur: Adam est seductus, quia non credidit verum esse, quod hostis persuasit; mulier vero est seducta credens verum esse, quod serpens dicebat; et sic consequens est quod ille scienter, et illa per ignorantiam peccavit; sed gravius est scienter peccare, quam per ignorantiam. Unde consequens est quod plus peccaverit vir quam mulier. Solutio. 597DIgnorantia illa non habuit excusationem, quia ex culpa processit, dubitando enim respondit dicens. Ne forte moriamur (Gen. III). Vir autem cogitavit de Dei misericordia, et poenitentia; et ideo minus peccavit.

QUAESTIO XVI. Quaeritur quomodo verum sit, quod non est seductus? Nonne credidit commissum esse veniale, quod erat mortale? Ergo et ipse aliquo modo est deceptus. Solutio. Non est seductus prior, et in eo, in quo mulier, ut dicit auctoritas. Sed nunquid non est seductus, si prior non est seductus, et in eo in quo mulier? Si enim quis non est vulneratus in capite, ergo non est vulneratus? Nunquid ad negationem determinatam sequitur simplex negatio? Solutio. Doctores Novi Testamenti quandoque dicunt 598Aaliquod non fuisse, quod Scriptura Veteris Testamenti non dicit fuisse. Unde quia scriptura Geneseos loquens de seductione mulieris, nihil dicit de aliqua seductione viri, ideo Apostolus dicit: Adam non est seductus, sed mulier. Juxta eumdem modum loquendi, alibi idem Apostolus, quod Melchisedech non habuit principium, neque finem, non patrem, non prolem asserit, cum tamen in veritate principium, et finem, et patrem, et forsitan prolem habuerit, sed quia scriptura sic inducit eum, ut nec de ejus genealogia, nec nativitate, nec morte aliquid dixerit, ideo Apostolus asserit omnia praedicta non habuisse, Et Ambrosius dicit quod vir cum prima muliere benedicitur, et non cum secunda, quasi diceret: In sacra Scriptura legimus benedictionem viri cum 598Bprima muliere, sed non legimus, ubi Deus benedicat virum cum secunda.

QUAESTIO XVII. Salvabitur autem mulier per filiorum generationem. Si generatio filiorum salvet, quid faciet continens vel virgo? nunquid non salvabitur, quia non habet filios? quid est quod alibi ait Apostolus: Beatior autem erit, sive vidua, sive virgo, si sic permanserit? Solutio. Non ponit causam salutis in filiorum generatione; sed potius in fide et dilectione, unde subjungit: Si permanserit in fide et dilectione. Et est sensus, et si mulier fuerit causa peccati, tamen salvabitur non solum continens, vel virgo, sed etiam nupta, etsi nunquam a filiorum generatione cessans, sed per filiorum generationem incedens ab hoc mundo exierit, si tamen permanserint 598Cin fide et dilectione. Vel augmentum salutis valebit ei, si filii ejus per doctrinam, et industriam ipsius permanserint in fide et dilectione, Vel mystice potius intelligitur. Mulier typus est carnis, quae alibi signatur per turturem. Adam est figura rationis, quae per passerem figuratur. Filii sunt bona opera, quae per pullos turturis intelliguntur, qui in nido Catholicae fidei tantum vivunt; extra non vigent, imo conculcantur, quia bona opera non prosunt paganis, Judaeis, haereticis, schismaticis. Unde dicit hic: Si permanserit in fide et dilectione, scilicet filii mulieris, pulli turturis, bona opera.

QUAESTIO XVIII. Si quis episcopatum desiderat, bonum opus desiderat (I Tim. III), etc. Sed iste ambitiosus 598Ddesiderat episcopatum, nunquid potest inferri, ergo desiderat bonum opus? Solutio. Episcopatus est intentio super suam, et aliorum vitam, et sic nomen est operis, quod desiderat bonus, qui intermissa, sed non relicta, Rachele decora facie, cum Jacob intrat ad Liam oculis lippam, propter filiorum fecunditatem, de monte contemplationis cum Moyse descendit ad campos actionis, Non enim sic debet quisquam esse otiosus, ut in eodem otio non cogitet utilitatem proximi, nec sic actuosus, ut contemplationem Dei non requirat. Episcopatus etiam nomen est dignitatis, quam desiderat ambitiosus, qui vult potius praeesse quam prodesse.

QUAESTIO XIX. Unius uxoris virum, etc. Quaeritur an monogamus debeat dici, et possit ordinari, qui 599Aante baptismum habuit uxorem; et ea dimissa renatus est in Christo et post fidelem duxit. Solutio. Dicit Hieronymus quod talis non est bigamus, et quod potest ordinari; cui jam novo nec stupra, nec alia imputantur. Sed Augustinus dicit, quod monogamus non est, nec debet ordinari, licet ei non obsit, quod prius fecerat; propter mysterium quod in ordinandis servari debet; quod in praedicto non potest servari.

QUAESTIO XX. Sed nunquid Hieronymus, et Augustinus, in solutione praedictae quaestionis contraria sentiunt? Solutio. Hieronymus dicit quod talis monogamus est quantum ad meritum, nec est peccatum si ordinetur. Augustinus vero dicit, quod monogamus non est quantum ad vim sacramenti, nec potest 599Bordinari, ubi sacramentum monogamiae servetur; nec exigitur, ut in quolibet ordinando servetur, alioquin virgo non possit ordinari, cum non sit unius uxoris vir. Ecclesia est convocatio multorum ad unius Dei cultum.

QUAESTIO XXI. Magnum pietatis sacramentum, etc. Quaeritur quid hic dicatur sacramentum. Quandoque enim sacramentum dicitur rei sacrae signum, ut sacramentum baptismi et altaris, quandoque dicitur aliquid occultum et secretum, sive mysterium. Solutio. Sacramentum vocatur Christus secundum deitatem occultus, qui causa est totius religionis, et verae culturae. Quis enim unquam fuit pius et devotus in fide, nisi sacramenti hujus prius percepta cognitione?

QUAESTIO XXII. Quod manifestatum est in carne, etc. 599CQuaeritur de qua manifestatione hic agatur. Solutio. De illa, quae facta est praedicatione, virtutibus, et signis in carne assumpta ostensis.

QUAESTIO XXIII. Justificatum in spiritu. Nonne sermo praecessit de Verbo Dei? hoc autem non est justificatum, sed potius ab aeterno justum natum. Solutio. Cum sermo fit de Christo, diligenter intuendum est quod dicatur, et secundum quid; hoc ergo, justificatum in spiritu, intelligitur Christus secundum assumptum hominem, secundum quem immunis est ab omni peccato, omnimodam habens justitiam.

QUAESTIO XXIV. Apparuit angelis. Hic habemus auctoritatem, quod angeli proficiunt in scientia per 599Dea, quae fiunt in Ecclesia, quod jam superius super locum; ut multiformis sapientia innotescat, etc., diligenter prosecuti sumus, et expositor idem testatur in hoc loco.

QUAESTIO XXV. Nihil rejiciendum, quod cum gratiarum actione percipitur (I Tim. IV). Quaeritur an hoc sit contrarium legali doctrinae, quae discernit quosdam cibos, dicens alios mundos, alios immundos? Solutio. In lege quaedam animalium dicta sunt immunda non natura, sed significatione: ut si de porco, et agno requiratur, utrumque mundum in natura, quia omnis creatura bona est; in significatione tamen agnus mundus est, porcus immundus.

QUAESTIO XXVI. Pietas ad omnia utilis est, promissionem 600Ahabens vitae, quae nunc est, etc. Quaeritur quid vocet promissionem praesentis vitae; nam de promissione futurae constat. Solutio. Temporalium sufficientiam et spiritualium abundantiam. Utrumque enim Deus promittit cultoribus. Sufficientia temporalium promittitur, ubi dicitur; Primum quaerite regnum Dei et haec omnia adjicientur vobis (Matth. VI). Abundantia spiritualium ubi scriptum est: Quicunque haec, vel illa reliquerit propter me, centuplum accipiet (Matth. XIX), id est in praesenti spiritualium bonorum jucunditas temporalium bonorum affluentiam tantum excedit, quantum centenarius unitatem superat.

QUAESTIO XXVII. Quae data est tibi per prophetiam, etc. Quaeritur, quid vocet prophetiam? Solutio. 600BProphetiam vocat electionem sanctorum qui elegerunt eum in pontificem. Vel potius Spiritus sancti inspirationem, per quam cognovit Apostolus ipsum esse dignum episcopatu.

QUAESTIO XXVIII. Cum impositione manuum. Quid ea est? Solutio. Impositionem manuum vocat verba mystica, quibus confirmatur ad hoc opus electus, auctoritatem accipiens, conscientia sua teste, ut audeat vice Domini sacrificia offerre.

QUAESTIO XXIX. Dignus est operarius mercede sua (I Tim. V), etc. Quaeritur, an id, quod a plebe datur praedicatori, sit debita merces et condigna; et an peccet, si pro ea praedicat, et an qui hoc facit vendat Evangelium. Solutio. Quis audeat dicere non esse mercedem, quod ipsa veritas vocat mercedem? 600CNon tamen pro tali mercede debet praedicare, sed ut aeternam mercedem accipiat a Domino. Necessitatis itaque est accipere unde vivitur, charitatis est praebere, imo debitum, ut qui accipiunt spiritalia, ministrent carnalia. Praedicator debet accipere, ut praedicet; non praedicare, ut accipiat.

QUAESTIO XXX. Peccantes vero coram omnibus argue. Huic videtur esse contrarium, quod Dominus dicit in Evangelio: Si frater tuus peccaverit in te, corripe eum inter te et ipsum solum (Matth. XVIII). Nunquid tam bonus discipulus discordat a tam bono Magistro? Solutio. Utrumque verum est, et aliquando illud, quod Dominus ait proprio ore scilicet quando tu solus sis, faciendum est; culpa enim occulta 600Dsecreto debet argui, ut Joseph justus fecit de Maria, solus suspicans adulterium; alioquin, si aliter feceris, eris proditor, non corrector. Aliquando etiam faciendum est, quod Veritas dixit ore Pauli scilicet quando palam peccatur. Publica enim offensa publica indiget satisfactione.

QUAESTIO XXXI. Modico vino utere. Quaeritur quomodo id consuluit. Solutio. Speciale dat consilium, ut semetipsum salubri regat doctrina, prudenter enim vult Deus serviri sibi, non ut nimia abstinentia debiles fiant, et post medicorum suffragia requirant sui.

QUAESTIO XXXII. Languens circa quaestiones, et pugnas verborum (I Tim. VI), etc. Quaestio erat, an aliquis esset servus, cum omnes ex eisdem patribus 601Asint orti, et omnes Christus redemerit. Item pugna verborum liberaverit, quia Dominus dicit: Si Filius vos liberavit, vere liberi estis (Joan. VIII), quae et similia videntur dissentire a doctrina apostolica, quae hortatur servos subjectos esse dominis suis, et similiter verbis Domini dicentis: Reddite ergo quae sunt Caesaris Caesari, etc. (Luc. XX.) Sic autem solvenda est talis controversia verborum; hoc, si Filius vos liberaverit, vere liberi estis, intelligendum est de spiritali libertate, non de carnali. Paulus autem loquitur de libertate et servitute carnali quam non tollit spiritalis.

QUAESTIO XXXIII. Radix omnium malorum est cupiditas. Alibi dicit Scriptura: Initium omnis peccati est superbia (Eccle. X). Hic autem, quod avaritia vel 601Bcupiditas. Si enim avaritia habetur species pro genere, quomodo utrumque verum est? si enim superbia initium est omnibus peccati, ergo cupiditatis; et si cupiditas radix est omnium malorum, ergo super biae; et sic idem causa est et effectus ejusdem. Solutio. Cum dicitur quod radix omnium malorum est cupiditas, vel omnis peccati initium superbia, si genera singula intelliguntur, falsum est, si autem genera singulorum, verum est. Nullum enim genus peccati est, quod non quandoque ex superbia, quandoque ex cupiditate nascantur. Nam sunt aliqui qui divitias cupiunt, ut per eas ad culmen honoris pertingere valeant; sunt alii, qui ideo dignitatem appetunt, ut ditiores fiant.

QUAESTIO XXXIV. Solus potens. Nonne angeli potentes 601Csunt, unde et virtutes, et potestates vocantur? Solutio. Solus Deus potens per naturam ex eo quod est; angeli vero per gratiam ex eo quod acceperunt, potentes sunt.

QUAESTIO XXXV. Qui solus habet immortalitatem, etc. Nonne animae et angeli etiam per naturam sunt immortales? Solutio. Solus Deus habet immortalitatem, id est immutabilitatem, quia nec potuit, nec potest, nec poterit peccare. Hanc immortalitatem non habent nec angeli, nec animae sanctorum, licet enim sint immortales per gratiam, tamen mutabiles per naturam vere esse creduntur.

QUAESTIO XXXVI. Qui lucem habitat inaccessibilem. Propheta dicit: Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini (Psal. XXXIII): nonne ipse Deus est ipsa lux, quam dicitur inhabitare? quomodo monemur accedere 602Aad hanc lucem, si ipsa est inaccessibilis? Solutio. Nemo ex se accedit ad eam, sed cui datur dono ejus.

QUAESTIO XXXVII. Quem nemo hominum vidit, nec videre potest. Nonne Abraham vidit Deum, et Moyses, et caeteri patres? Quomodo ergo verum, quod nemo Deum vidit unquam? Item, nonne et nos ejus visionem speramus? Sed quomodo, si nemo potest eum videre? Solutio. Deus in natura sua est invisibilis oculo carnis illae vero visiones sanctis patribus in creatura subjecta exhibitae sunt. Unde Moyses post figuras illas, in quibus Deus videbatur, ait: Domine, ostende mihi faciem tuam (Exod. XXXIII). In futuro autem videbitur Deus a mundo corde, et nunc videtur a sanctis angelis.

602BQUAESTIO XXXVIII. Devitans profanas vocum novitates, etc. Quaeritur an omnes vocum novitates sint vitandae. Solutio. Non, quia non omnes sunt profanae, ut hoc ipsum nomen Christianum, homousion, mandatum novum, et testamentum novum, et canticum novum, novitates vocant non profanas, sed sacras, et religioni congruentes. Hypostasis autem tempore haereticorum notabat profanam novitatem, quo nomine haeretici utebantur, nunc in significatione personae, nunc in significatione substantiae, ad deceptionem simplicium, ut si concederent Trinitatem esse hypostasim unam, inferrent: Ergo sunt una persona; sin autem dicerent Patrem, Filium et Spiritum sanctum esse tres hypostases, concluderent: Ergo sunt tres substantiae. Nunc autem 602Choc vocabulum non notat profanam novitatem, quia redactum est ad significationem personae. Unde concedimus modo simpliciter Trinitatem esse tres hypostases, et non unam; quod non erat concedendum sine determinatione olim, quando adhuc retinebat multiplicem significationem.

QUAESTIO XXXIX. Et oppositiones falsi nominis scientiae, etc. Quaeritur quid vocet Apostolus scientiam falsi nominis. Nunquid logicam? sed si hoc est, quomodo Augustinus vocat dialecticam scientiam scientiarum, quae non solum facit scientem, sed etiam demonstrat scientem? Solutio. Ut arbitror, scientiam falsi nominis vocat artem sophisticam, cujus oppositiones devitandae sunt a piis et mansuetis: quia non valent, nisi ad subversionem simplicium.

X. ON THE FIRST EPISTLE TO TIMOTHY.

  • 593

593CPaul an apostle (I Tim. I), etc. The Apostle writes this epistle to Timothy, who was the son of a certain faithful woman, begotten of a gentile father: and since he was not circumcised, and was himself a gentile, and the brethren who were in Lystra and Iconium gave good testimony of him, Paul wished this man to set out with him: and therefore that he be circumcised on account of the Jews who were in those places. And he was learned as well in the divine Scriptures as in the liberal arts. This man the Apostle created bishop: therefore, leaving him in Asia, he instructs him in this epistle concerning the episcopal office, namely how he should resist false apostles and how he should instruct the Church, what sort of priests or deacons he should ordain; what sort of widows he should honor, and how he should conduct himself in the Church, or how he should rule it. And the intention of the 593DApostle in this epistle is to instruct Timothy concerning the office of the episcopal dignity. The manner is such: first he salutes him; then he warns him to resist the false ones; afterward he instructs him concerning the episcopal office, teaching what sort of priests and deacons he ought to ordain. Then what sort of widows he ought to receive; afterward he instructs him concerning the manner of correption; but at the end he warns him to avoid profane novelties.

QUESTION I. Of God the Father our Saviour, etc. Since the Son is frequently called in Scripture Saviour, who alone died for our salvation, not the Father, not the Holy Spirit, it is asked why the Apostle refers our salvation to God the Father, saying here: Of God the Father our Saviour. Solution. God the Father, in that he deigned to send us his Son, and to bestow the Holy Spirit in the sacraments of the New Testament, 594Cis the author of our salvation and therefore is called Saviour.

QUESTION II. And of Jesus Christ our hope. Likewise it is asked why he refers hope specially to the Son, saying, and of Jesus Christ our hope, since we hope and believe in the whole Trinity. Solution. We therefore refer our hope to Christ, because he rose from the dead, and ascended into the heavens; because through his resurrection we hope to attain to the glory of the future resurrection.

QUESTION III. Grace, mercy and peace, etc. It is asked why, beyond his wont, the Apostle in this salutation puts three, saying, grace, mercy, and peace. Solution. The nine preceding epistles he wrote in common to the Churches. But this one specially to Timothy 594Dhis fellow-bishop; therefore he puts three. By mercy understanding the same thing which in the others he understood by grace, namely the remission of sins; by peace, the tranquillity and foretaste of the future life; but by grace he understands the donation of the Holy Spirit, wherewith the ministers of Christ are armed.

QUESTION IV. That they should not attend to fables, etc. It is asked what the Apostle here understands by fables? does he perhaps so call the words of the law, and the divine oracles in this place? and elsewhere he says: Avoid profane and old wives' fables (I Tim. IV). Solution. By fables he here means the doctrine of those who preach that the law with grace is necessary. Or by fables he here means the traditions which the Jews hold unwritten, and one transfuses into another by speaking, which they call deuterosis: wherein they say, and believe, that God first created two wives, from whom 595Athey weave infinite genealogies of men, bringing forth unfruitful questions. Concerning which traditions, foreign to the sacred Scriptures, the Lord says in the Gospel: Why have you made void the commandment of God for your traditions? (Matth. XV.).

QUESTION V. Now the end of the commandment is charity, from a pure heart, and a good conscience, and faith unfeigned. Here the Apostle defines charity, as the expositor says. Whence it can be asked what is the definition here given, whether this: the end of the commandment? or this: from a pure heart, and a good conscience, and faith unfeigned? Solution. The definition of charity is, to be from a pure heart, and a good conscience, and faith unfeigned.

QUESTION VI. Likewise it can be asked whether this definition fits all charity. Which if it be granted, no one 595Bis having charity who is not perfect, because consummating and perfecting the law; because charity is the end of the commandment, that is, perfection and consummation. For if 'end' is here put for consummation. But elsewhere it is put for consumption, as when it is said, the bread is finished. Elsewhere for a boundary, as when it is said: Here the field ends. Likewise, who can have a pure heart and a good conscience without charity? does not cleanness of heart, and a good conscience, proceed from charity? how then does charity proceed from a pure heart? Solution. It seems to me that here the definition of perfect and consummated charity is assigned, and thus this definition does not fit imperfect charity. First is given love, which cleanses the heart, and from which good 595Cworks are done, and from which is born a good conscience; at length, the heart being cleansed, and a good conscience procured, charity is perfected and consummated, which is the end of the commandment. These things I say without prejudice to a better opinion.

QUESTION VII. The law is good, if a man use it lawfully. It is asked what it is to use lawfully? Solution. As the expositor says, he uses the law lawfully who, understanding it spiritually, through it recognizes the disease, and seeks the physician, and who knows it to have been given for a time, and forsakes it for Christ. It is to be noted that the unjust man uses the law lawfully, when he understands why it was given, and by fear of it flees to the grace of Christ, that he may become just. But the just man uses the law lawfully, when by terrifying he imposes it upon the unjust.

595DQUESTION VIII. The law is not made for the just man. Were not David and other just men, who were under the law, bound to keep the law, how then is the law not made for the just? Solution. The law is not imposed upon the just man, so as to have dominion over him, and to coerce him by fear, and the just man is not under the law, but rather with it, as a friend of the law.

QUESTION IX. Because I did it ignorantly, etc. The expositor says that this 'because' can note the cause or the consequence. Ssd it is asked how ignorance, which is a fault, can be the cause of divine mercy. Solution. There is a certain ignorance from infirmity: from which if anyone act against God out of good zeal, out of the affection which he has, he merits to be freed from that ignorance.

596AQUESTION X. He came into this world to save sinners, etc. It is asked concerning little ones, who are born of baptized parents, whether they pertain to the sinners for whose saving Jesus came into the world. For these have no actual sin, and how can they contract original sin from parents, which the parents themselves have not; because it is forgiven them? Solution. It is to be known that original sin is so forgiven in baptism, not that it be not at all, but that it be not a fault. But the vice of corruption remains even in the baptized, who beget, not from that whereby they are reborn, but from the oldness of corruption, through which original fault passes into the little ones: whence they too need a remedy. Whence also the physician himself says: Suffer the little ones to come unto me (Marc. X).

596BQUESTION XI. Of whom I am the first. Were not Cain and Saul before Paul? how then is Paul the first among sinners? Solution. Paul was first not in order of time, but in greatness of iniquity. To which solution it is thus objected: Did not Paul sin through ignorance, and many others knowingly? but it is a greater sin to sin knowingly than through ignorance: therefore Paul was not the first among sinners in greatness of iniquity, since others, especially those who sinned against the Holy Spirit, are much worse than Paul even according to his first state, in which he was a blasphemer, a persecutor, and contumelious. Solution. Paul, considering the greatness of his own offenses, judged himself worse than all sinners, 596Calthough in the eyes of God it was otherwise.

QUESTION XII. Now to the king of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, honor and glory for ever and ever. Amen. The expositor says that the man assumed by the Word is king of ages from that time in which he was assumed by the Word; but if the man assumed is not man, nor God, nor person, as certain men have dared to profess, how is the man assumed, from the time that he is assumed, and not before, king of ages? But we say that the man assumed by the Word is man and God: the Word itself, by whom he was assumed, both began in time to be king of ages, namely when he began to be assumed by the Word. For when God began to be man, man also began to be God, as many authorities attest.

596DQUESTION XIII. Who will have all men to be saved (I Tim. II). Since God is omnipotent, and no one can resist the divine will, how are not all saved, since God wills all to be saved? Or is it perhaps his will that the reprobate be saved? Ambrose thus resolves it: God wills all to be saved, if they themselves will. But do not many will to be saved, who nevertheless are not saved? how then is it true, God wills all to be saved? And therefore others thus expound: God wills, etc., it would please him, if all were saved, or all, that is, of every kind of men some. Or thus: To all he offers grace, through which, if they will, they can be saved. But how is this solution true? Are there not many who are and were, who did not even hear the word of preaching? Or he wills all to be saved, 597Athat is, he makes the holy to will that all be saved. Or thus: He wills all to be saved, that is, no one is made saved, unless he himself will it. In like manner is understood that: Who enlighteneth every man (Joan. I), that is, no one is enlightened except by him, and all are made alive in Christ, according to the same manner it behooves to be understood. Thus concerning the ambiguous diverse opinions are given.

QUESTION XIV. One mediator of God and men, the man Christ Jesus. Concerning the mediator it has already in part been said above. But here let it suffice to consider this which the expositor says, that in so far as he is man, he is mediator, not in so far as he is Word. But is he not mediator between the angels and God the Father, and also between the Holy Spirit, in so far as he is Word, though otherwise between the angels and God the Father, and otherwise between the Holy 597BSpirit and the Father? Solution. It can well be granted that, in so far as he is Word, he is mediator between the rational creatures and God the Father; but he is not mediator between God the Trinity and men in so far as he is Word, but in so far as he is man like to God in justice, to men in mortality. For if, in so far as he is Word, he were mediator between men and God the Trinity, then there would already be something mediate between himself and another, because the Word between himself and men; which is not to be granted. Someone will say: Christ is now not mortal, how then is he mediator between mortal men and the immortal God, since he was therefore called mediator; because he is like to men through mortality, and to God through justice? Solution. Even now Christ reconciles us to God the Father as the best 597Cmediator, through that which he did for us in the days of his flesh, that is, of his mortality.

QUESTION XV. Adam was not seduced, but the woman. It is asked which of the two sinned more, whether Adam or Eve? Solution. The doctors say that the woman not only sinned, but also made the man sin. Against which solution it is thus objected: Adam was seduced, because he did not believe to be true what the enemy urged; but the woman was seduced, believing to be true what the serpent was saying; and thus it follows that he sinned knowingly, and she through ignorance; but it is graver to sin knowingly than through ignorance. Whence it follows that the man sinned more than the woman. Solution. 597DThat ignorance did not have excuse, because it proceeded from fault; for doubting she answered, saying: Lest perhaps we die (Gen. III). But the man thought of the mercy of God, and of penitence; and therefore he sinned less.

QUESTION XVI. It is asked how it is true that he was not seduced? Did he not believe that to be committed as venial, which was mortal? Therefore he too was in some way deceived. Solution. He was not seduced first, and in that in which the woman was, as the authority says. But is he not seduced, if he was not seduced first, and in that in which the woman was? For if someone is not wounded in the head, is he therefore not wounded? Does a simple negation follow upon a determinate negation? Solution. The doctors of the New Testament sometimes say 598Athat something was not, which the Scripture of the Old Testament does not say was. Whence, because the scripture of Genesis, speaking of the seduction of the woman, says nothing of any seduction of the man, therefore the Apostle says: Adam was not seduced, but the woman. According to the same manner of speaking, elsewhere the same Apostle asserts that Melchisedech had no beginning, nor end, no father, no offspring, although in truth he had a beginning, and an end, and a father, and perhaps offspring; but because the scripture so introduces him that it said nothing either of his genealogy, or birth, or death, therefore the Apostle asserts that he had none of the aforesaid things. And Ambrose says that the man is blessed with the first woman, and not with the second, as if he were to say: In Holy Scripture we read the blessing of the man with the 598Bfirst woman, but we do not read where God blesses the man with the second.

QUESTION XVII. But the woman shall be saved through the generation of children. If the generation of children saves, what will the continent woman or the virgin do? Will she not be saved, because she has no children? What is it that elsewhere the Apostle says: But she will be more blessed, whether widow or virgin, if she so remain? Solution. He does not place the cause of salvation in the generation of children, but rather in faith and love, whence he adds: If she remain in faith and love. And the sense is: even if the woman was the cause of sin, nevertheless she shall be saved — not only the continent woman, or the virgin, but even the married woman, though, never ceasing from the generation of children, but going forward through the generation of children, she should depart from this world, provided that they remain 598Cin faith and love. Or it will avail her for an increase of salvation, if her children, through her teaching and diligence, remain in faith and love. Or rather it is understood mystically. The woman is a type of the flesh, which elsewhere is signified by the turtledove. Adam is a figure of reason, which is figured by the sparrow. The children are good works, which are understood by the young of the turtledove, which live only in the nest of the Catholic faith; outside they do not thrive, nay they are trodden down, because good works do not profit pagans, Jews, heretics, schismatics. Whence he says here: If she remain in faith and love, namely the children of the woman, the young of the turtledove, the good works.

QUESTION XVIII. If any man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work (I Tim. III), etc. But this ambitious man 598Ddesires the episcopate; can it be inferred, therefore he desires a good work? Solution. The episcopate is the attention over one's own and others' life, and thus it is the name of a work, which the good man desires, who, Rachel of beautiful countenance being set aside for a time, but not abandoned, with Jacob enters in to Leah bleary-eyed, on account of the fruitfulness of children, and descends from the mountain of contemplation with Moses to the fields of action. For no one ought so to be at leisure that in that same leisure he does not think of the profit of his neighbor, nor so busy that he does not seek the contemplation of God. The episcopate is also the name of a dignity, which the ambitious man desires, who wishes rather to preside than to profit.

QUESTION XIX. The husband of one wife, etc. It is asked whether he ought to be called a monogamist, and can be ordained, who 599Abefore baptism had a wife; and, she being dismissed, was reborn in Christ and afterward married a believing woman. Solution. Jerome says that such a man is not a bigamist, and that he can be ordained; to whom, now made new, neither debaucheries nor other things are imputed. But Augustine says that he is not a monogamist, nor ought to be ordained, although what he had done before does not stand against him; on account of the mystery which ought to be preserved in those to be ordained; which in the aforesaid man cannot be preserved.

QUESTION XX. But do Jerome and Augustine hold contrary opinions in the solution of the aforesaid question? Solution. Jerome says that such a man is a monogamist as regards merit, and it is not a sin if he be ordained. But Augustine says that he is not a monogamist as regards the force of the sacrament, nor can he be 599Bordained, where the sacrament of monogamy is to be preserved; nor is it required that it be preserved in every one to be ordained, otherwise a virgin could not be ordained, since he is not the husband of one wife. The Church is the convocation of many to the worship of the one God.

QUESTION XXI. Great is the sacrament of piety, etc. It is asked what is here called a sacrament. For sometimes a sacrament is called a sign of a sacred thing, as the sacrament of baptism and of the altar; sometimes it is called something hidden and secret, or a mystery. Solution. Christ, hidden according to his deity, is called a sacrament, who is the cause of all religion, and of true worship. For who was ever pious and devout in faith, except the knowledge of this sacrament having first been received?

QUESTION XXII. Which was manifested in the flesh, etc. 599CIt is asked of what manifestation this treats. Solution. Of that which was made by preaching, by powers, and by signs shown in the assumed flesh.

QUESTION XXIII. Justified in the spirit. Did not the discourse precede concerning the Word of God? but this was not justified, but rather born just from eternity. Solution. When discourse is made about Christ, it must be diligently observed what is said, and in respect of what; this therefore, justified in the spirit, is understood of Christ according to the man assumed, according to whom he is free from all sin, having justice in every mode.

QUESTION XXIV. He appeared to the angels. Here we have authority that the angels advance in knowledge through 599Dthose things which are done in the Church, which we have already diligently pursued above upon the passage: that the manifold wisdom may become known, etc.; and the expositor testifies the same in this place.

QUESTION XXV. Nothing is to be rejected that is received with thanksgiving (I Tim. IV). It is asked whether this is contrary to the legal doctrine, which distinguishes certain foods, calling some clean, others unclean? Solution. In the law certain animals were called unclean not by nature, but by signification: so that, if concerning the pig and the lamb it be inquired, each is clean in nature, because every creature is good; yet in signification the lamb is clean, the pig unclean.

QUESTION XXVI. Piety is profitable to all things, having the promise 600Aof the life that now is, etc. It is asked what he calls the promise of the present life; for concerning the promise of the future life it is established. Solution. The sufficiency of temporal things and the abundance of spiritual things. For God promises both to his worshippers. The sufficiency of temporal things is promised, where it is said: Seek first the kingdom of God, and all these things shall be added unto you (Matth. VI). The abundance of spiritual things, where it is written: Whosoever shall leave these or those things for my sake, shall receive a hundredfold (Matth. XIX), that is, in the present the delightfulness of spiritual goods exceeds the affluence of temporal goods by as much as a hundred surpasses unity.

QUESTION XXVII. Which was given to thee by prophecy, etc. It is asked, what does he call prophecy? Solution. 600BHe calls prophecy the choice of the holy ones who chose him for bishop. Or rather the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, through which the Apostle knew him to be worthy of the episcopate.

QUESTION XXVIII. With the imposition of hands. What is it? Solution. He calls the imposition of hands the mystical words, by which the one chosen is confirmed for this work, receiving authority, his conscience being witness, that he may dare to offer sacrifices in the Lord's stead.

QUESTION XXIX. The laborer is worthy of his hire (I Tim. V), etc. It is asked whether that which is given by the people to the preacher is a due and worthy wage; and whether he sins, if he preaches for it; and whether he who does this sells the Gospel. Solution. Who would dare to say that is not a wage, which Truth itself calls a wage? 600CYet he ought not to preach for such a wage, but that he may receive an eternal wage from the Lord. It is therefore of necessity to receive that whereby one lives; it is of charity to bestow, nay a debt, that those who receive spiritual things should minister carnal things. The preacher ought to receive, that he may preach; not to preach, that he may receive.

QUESTION XXX. But them that sin reprove before all. To this seems to be contrary what the Lord says in the Gospel: If thy brother shall offend against thee, rebuke him between thee and him alone (Matth. XVIII). Does so good a disciple disagree with so good a Master? Solution. Both are true, and sometimes that which the Lord says with his own mouth, namely when thou art alone, is to be done; for a hidden fault 600Dought to be reproved in secret, as the just Joseph did concerning Mary, alone suspecting adultery; otherwise, if thou do otherwise, thou wilt be a betrayer, not a corrector. Sometimes also that is to be done which Truth said by the mouth of Paul, namely when one sins openly. For a public offense needs a public satisfaction.

QUESTION XXXI. Use a little wine. It is asked how he counseled this. Solution. He gives a special counsel, that he govern himself by wholesome instruction; for God wishes to be served prudently, not that by excessive abstinence they become weak, and afterward require the help of physicians for themselves.

QUESTION XXXII. Languishing about questions, and strifes of words (I Tim. VI), etc. The question was, whether anyone was a slave, since all have arisen 601Afrom the same fathers, and Christ has redeemed all. Likewise a strife of words, he may have freed [them], because the Lord says: If the Son hath freed you, you are free indeed (Joan. VIII), which and similar things seem to dissent from the apostolic doctrine, which exhorts servants to be subject to their masters, and likewise from the words of the Lord saying: Render therefore the things that are Caesar's to Caesar, etc. (Luc. XX.) But such a controversy of words is to be resolved thus: this — if the Son shall have freed you, you are free indeed — is to be understood of spiritual liberty, not of carnal. But Paul speaks of carnal liberty and servitude, which the spiritual does not take away.

QUESTION XXXIII. The root of all evils is cupidity. Elsewhere Scripture says: The beginning of every sin is pride (Eccle. X). But here, that it is avarice or 601Bcupidity. For if avarice is held as a species for a genus, how is each true? for if pride is the beginning of every sin, therefore also of cupidity; and if cupidity is the root of all evils, therefore also of pride; and thus the same thing is the cause and the effect of the same. Solution. When it is said that the root of all evils is cupidity, or that pride is the beginning of every sin, if the individual genera are understood, it is false; but if the genera of individuals, it is true. For there is no genus of sin which does not sometimes arise from pride, sometimes from cupidity. For there are some who covet riches, that through them they may be able to reach the summit of honor; there are others who seek dignity for this reason, that they may become richer.

QUESTION XXXIV. Alone powerful. Are not the angels powerful 601C, whence they are also called Virtues and Powers? Solution. God alone is powerful by nature, from that which he is; but the angels are powerful by grace, from that which they have received.

QUESTION XXXV. Who alone hath immortality, etc. Are not souls and angels also by nature immortal? Solution. God alone hath immortality, that is, immutability, because he neither could, nor can, nor will be able to sin. This immortality neither the angels nor the souls of the saints have; for although they are immortal by grace, yet they are truly believed to be mutable by nature.

QUESTION XXXVI. Who inhabiteth light inaccessible. The prophet says: Come ye to him, and be enlightened (Psal. XXXIII): is not God himself the very light which he is said to inhabit? How are we admonished to come 602Ato this light, if it is itself inaccessible? Solution. No one comes to it of himself, but he to whom it is given by his gift.

QUESTION XXXVII. Whom no man hath seen, nor can see. Did not Abraham see God, and Moses, and the other fathers? How then is it true that no one has ever seen God? Likewise, do not we too hope for the vision of him? But how, if no one can see him? Solution. God in his own nature is invisible to the eye of flesh; but those visions were exhibited to the holy fathers in a subject creature. Whence Moses, after those figures in which God was seen, said: Lord, show me thy face (Exod. XXXIII). But in the future God shall be seen by the clean of heart, and now he is seen by the holy angels.

602BQUESTION XXXVIII. Avoiding the profane novelties of words, etc. It is asked whether all novelties of words are to be avoided. Solution. No, because not all are profane, as this very name "Christian," "homoousion," "the new commandment," and "the new testament," and "the new song" — they call these novelties not profane, but sacred, and befitting religion. But "hypostasis," in the time of the heretics, denoted a profane novelty, which name the heretics used, now in the signification of person, now in the signification of substance, for the deception of the simple, so that, if they granted the Trinity to be one hypostasis, they would infer: Therefore they are one person; but if they said the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit to be three hypostases, they would conclude: Therefore they are three substances. But now 602Cthis word does not denote a profane novelty, because it has been reduced to the signification of person. Whence we now simply grant the Trinity to be three hypostases, and not one; which formerly was not to be granted without a qualification, when it still retained a manifold signification.

QUESTION XXXIX. And the oppositions of knowledge falsely so called, etc. It is asked what the Apostle calls knowledge of a false name. Is it logic? But if it is this, how does Augustine call dialectic the science of sciences, which not only makes one knowing, but even demonstrates the knower? Solution. As I judge, he calls knowledge of a false name the sophistical art, whose oppositions are to be avoided by the pious and meek, because they avail for nothing but the subversion of the simple.

XI. IN EPISTOLAM II AD TIMOTHEUM.

  • 601

601DPaulus apostolus (II Tim. I), etc. Jam a mundo transiturus hanc secundam epistolam scribit a Roma de carcere, Timotheo infirmitatibus et adversitatibus fatigato, ut constanter laboret in Dei gratia sibi credita, exhortans eum ad martyrium multis modis, 602Det ut perseveret in officio rectae praedicationis, et sancta operatione: et praedicens quid futurum sit in novissimis temporibus et de suo obitu. Et est intentio Apostoli in hac epistola exhortari Timotheum ad sui officii diligentem exsecutionem, et ad palmam 603Amartyrii, et quaedam adhuc addit de episcopali officio. Modus talis: primo salutat, deinde gratias agit de bono quod habet, ubi suum videndi eum desiderium ostendit: postea monet ad praedicandum, et ad patientiam martyrii, suo exemplo et aliis modis: inde dicit quales futuri sint in novissimis diebus: tandem de tempore resolutionis suae instanti.

QUAESTIO I. Non dedit nobis Deus spiritum timoris. Quaeritur de quo timore hoc dicatur. Solutio. De timore quem expellit amor Dei.

QUAESTIO II. Quae data est nobis ante tempora saecularia, etc. Quando aliquid nobis nondum existentibus potuit dari? Solutio. Data est, id est praevisa dari: unde non dicit simpliciter data est, sed addidit in Christo Jesu.

603BQUAESTIO III. Item quaeritur cur non dicat sempliciter ante tempora, sed addit, saecularia. Nonne omnia tempora sunt saecularia? Ad quorum ergo differentiam dicit saecularia? Solutio. Dicunt quidam angelos creatos esse ante mundi creationem, et spatia illa, quae erant a creatione angelorum, usque ad creationem mundi, vocat Apostolus alibi tempora aeterna, ad quorum differentiam dicit hic tempora saecularia. Sed dicet aliquis: Nonne tempus notat mutabilitatem, et aeternitas immutabilitatem? Quomodo ergo possunt aliqua tempora esse aeterna? quomodo simul esse mutabilia et immutabilia? Solutio. Sic praedicti doctores hoc intelligunt: In illis spatiis, quae dicuntur tempora aeterna, erat successio, et nulla decessio: et sic quaedam immutabilitas, 603Cet secundum hoc quaedam aeternitas. Huic sententiae videtur Hieronymus consonare. Fere autem omnes doctores dicunt creatos angelos non ante, sed cum mundo; sed quid secundum illos per tempora aeterna debeat intelligi, videat et inquirat qui eorum opinionem sectatur. Mihi autem priorum sententia videtur potior, salva reverentia secretorum: hoc dico, nil temere asserendo.

QUAESTIO IV. Nemo militans Deo implicat se negotiis saecularibus (II Tim. II), etc. Nonne viri activi Deo militant, et tamen implicati sunt saecularibus negotiis? quomodo ergo dicit Apostolus: Nemo militans Deo, etc. Solutio. Negotia vocat saecularia cum animus occupatur cura colligendae pecuniae: 603Dquod nemo potest simul facere, et Deo militare. Viri autem activi non ad hoc exterioribus vacant: ut pecuniam colligant: sed ad hoc tantum, ut sibi, et aliis necessaria provideant.

QUAESTIO V. Ex semine David secundum Evangelium meum, in quo laboro usque ad vincula. Quaeritur de qua tribu erant Christus et Maria. Sed ex hoc loco nota Christum ex David natum: sicut in principio ait: Ex semine David secundum carnem. Et Gabriel archangelus de eodem: Dabit ei Dominus Deus sedem David patris sui (Luc. I). Haec dico propter eos qui nolunt matrem Domini esse ex semine David, qui de tribu Juda erat: sed de tribu Levi tantum fuisse, et propter Joseph virum Mariae, qui erat de familia David, Christum dicunt dictum ex 604Asemine David: et Origenes (ut dicitur) sic sensit. Alii dicunt, quod et nobis videtur, Mariam etiam de stirpe David processisse, et ita, de stirpe Juda, non solum de stirpe Levi. Nam duae tribus, regalis et sacerdotalis, permistae erant, et ideo non est mirum Virginem traxisse originem de utraque tanquam verum Regem, et Sacerdotem paritura. Nolite verbis contendere. Inter servos Dei non debet esse contentio, sed collatio, et modesta veritatis inquisitio.

QUAESTIO VI. Dicentes jam resurrectionem factam. Quaeritur de qua resurrectione dicat Apostolus: an de illa, quae est mentium: an de illa, quae est corporum? Nam si de illa, quae est mentium, quae fit in baptismate, hoc dicatur, quomodo illi, qui hanc dixerunt 604Bjam factam esse, subverterunt quorumdam fidem, cum hoc sit verum et credendum? Item si de resurrectione corporum hoc dicebant, quomodo per hoc aliquorum fidem subvertebant, cum constet omnibus hoc falsum esse? Solutio. Potest hoc de utraque resurrectione intelligi: per hoc enim quod dicebant jam resurrectionem mentium factam esse, nec aliam corporum futuram esse, decipiebant scilicet quia subdole resurrectionem corporum negabant. Vel etiam in hoc fidem subvertebant, quod dicebant resurrectionem corporum factam esse: inde sumentes occasionem erroris sui, quod scriptum est in Evangelio: Multa corpora sanctorum surrexerunt, et apparuerunt in sancta civitate (Matth. XXVII), 604Cnegantes generalem resurrectionem, quam exspectamus, futuram.

QUAESTIO VII. In magna domo sunt non solum vasa aurea, et argentea, etc. Quaeritur quos intelligit per vasa aurea, et argentea, et quos per vasa lignea, et fictilia? Solutio. Per vasa aurea, et argentea intelligit praedestinatos; per vasa lignea et fictilia, reprobos. Vel per vasa aurea intelliguntur boni, sive sint praedestinati, sive non; per vasa lignea et fictilia, mali, sive sint ad vitam praesciti, sive reprobi. Et sic secundum hanc sententiam de utrisque quaedam sunt ad honorem, quaedam ad contumeliam. Secundum vero priorem ad honorem tantum sunt vasa aurea et argentea; ad contumeliam vero lignea et fictilia. Stultas quaestiones, et sine disciplina devita, 604Detc. Hic innuit non omnes quaestiones vitandas esse, sed illas tantum, in quibus nullus est fructus. Habentes speciem pietatis: virtutem ejus negantes. Tales multi sunt in hoc tempore, quales hic describit Apostolus, qui se, non Deum, diligunt: habentes nomen et habitum sanctitatis, cum intus sint pleni omnium immunditiarum. Virtutem pietatis vocat charitatem, de qua scriptum est: Fortis est ut mors dilectio (Cant. VIII): hanc necessario praecedit mundi contemptus.

QUAESTIO VIII. Omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur (II Tim. III). Nonne Ecclesia habet tempus pacis in quo multi pie vivunt, nec tamen persecutionem patiuntur? Solutio. Sancti pluribus modis patiuntur, ut in corde et corpore: 605Anunc a diabolo, nunc a malis hominibus, nunc a concupiscentiis suis; quibus etiam est persecutio infirmorum conversatio. Hi enim dicunt cum Apostolo: Quis infirmatur, et ego non infirmor? quis scandalizatur, et ego non uror? (II Cor. XI). Non sunt itaque sine persecutione pie viventes in Christo, etiam tempore pacis.

QUAESTIO IX. Cursum consummavi (II Tim. IV), 606Aetc. Nonne ad cursus consummationem adhuc restabat acrior et crudelior inimicus, scilicet Neronis gladius? Quomodo ergo verum erat Paulum consummasse cursum ante passionis triumphum! Solutio. Hoc dicit non re plena, sed spe certa. Qui enim fecit eum victorem in certamine, jam certum et securum per revelationem eum reddiderat de consummatione.

XI. ON THE SECOND EPISTLE TO TIMOTHY.

  • 601

601DPaul an apostle (II Tim. I), etc. Now about to pass from the world, he writes this second epistle from Rome, from prison, to Timothy, wearied by infirmities and adversities, that he may labor constantly in the grace of God entrusted to him, exhorting him to martyrdom in many ways, 602Dand that he may persevere in the office of right preaching, and in holy working: and foretelling what shall be in the last times, and concerning his own death. And the intention of the Apostle in this epistle is to exhort Timothy to the diligent execution of his office, and to the palm 603Aof martyrdom, and he adds still some things about the episcopal office. The manner is such: first he greets, then he gives thanks for the good which he has, where he shows his desire of seeing him: afterward he admonishes to preaching, and to the endurance of martyrdom, by his own example and in other ways: thence he says what men will be like in the last days: finally, concerning the time of his own dissolution which is at hand.

QUESTION I. God hath not given us the spirit of fear. It is asked of what fear this is said. Solution. Of the fear which the love of God expels.

QUESTION II. Which was given us before the secular ages, etc. When could anything be given to us, we not yet existing? Solution. It was given, that is, foreseen to be given: whence he does not say simply "it was given," but added "in Christ Jesus."

603BQUESTION III. Likewise it is asked why he does not say sempliciter before the ages, but adds, secular. Are not all times secular? To the difference of what, then, does he say "secular"? Solution. Some say that the angels were created before the creation of the world, and those spaces which were from the creation of the angels up to the creation of the world the Apostle elsewhere calls eternal times, to the difference of which he here says "secular times." But someone will say: Does not time denote mutability, and eternity immutability? How then can any times be eternal? how be at once mutable and immutable? Solution. The aforesaid doctors understand this thus: In those spaces which are called eternal times there was succession, and no passing-away: and thus a certain immutability, 603Cand according to this a certain eternity. To this opinion Jerome seems to accord. But nearly all the doctors say that the angels were created not before, but with the world; but what, according to them, ought to be understood by "eternal times," let him see and inquire who follows their opinion. But to me the opinion of the former seems the stronger, saving the reverence due to hidden things: this I say, asserting nothing rashly.

QUESTION IV. No man being a soldier to God entangleth himself with secular businesses (II Tim. II), etc. Do not active men war for God, and yet are entangled in secular businesses? how then does the Apostle say: No man being a soldier to God, etc.? Solution. He calls businesses "secular" when the mind is occupied with the care of gathering money: 603Dwhich no one can do at the same time, and war for God. But active men do not devote themselves to outward things for this, that they may gather money, but only for this, that they may provide necessary things for themselves and for others.

QUESTION V. Of the seed of David according to my Gospel, wherein I labor even unto bonds. It is asked of what tribe Christ and Mary were. But from this passage note that Christ was born of David: as in the beginning he says: Of the seed of David according to the flesh. And the archangel Gabriel of the same: The Lord God shall give unto him the throne of David his father (Luc. I). These things I say on account of those who will not have the mother of the Lord to be of the seed of David, who was of the tribe of Judah, but say that she was only of the tribe of Levi, and on account of Joseph the husband of Mary, who was of the family of David, they say Christ is called of 604Athe seed of David: and Origen (as it is said) thought thus. Others say — which also seems so to us — that Mary too proceeded from the stock of David, and so from the stock of Judah, not only from the stock of Levi. For the two tribes, the royal and the priestly, were intermingled, and therefore it is no wonder that the Virgin drew her origin from both, as one about to bring forth a true King and Priest.
